3336.q: What is the normal body temperature of a healthy cat?
a: About 42 degrees Celsius in every cat
3336.e: At 38 to 39 degrees, a cat's normal body temperature is a little higher than a human's. This is part of the animal's normal metabolism.
3336.m: Cats are a little warmer than humans.

3337.q: What helps a mute swan swim so well?
3337.e: The mute swan has webbing between its toes, like paddles. This lets it move powerfully through the water.

3338.q: What was the aim of the Kyoto Protocol?
a: To commit countries to reducing greenhouse gases
To redraw the borders between states
To regulate world trade in oil
To secure peace between Japan and the USA
3338.e: The Kyoto Protocol was an international agreement under which industrial states were to cut their greenhouse gas emissions. It was an important forerunner of the later Paris Climate Agreement.
3338.m: Kyoto committed states to protecting the climate.

3339.q: What does a young worker honeybee do first?
3339.e: Young bees first work inside the hive and clean the honeycomb. Only later in life do they fly out to collect nectar.
3339.m: Bees have different jobs depending on their age.

3340.q: Besides insects, what else does a hedgehog like to eat?
3340.e: Hedgehogs are not fussy and also like eating earthworms, beetle larvae and small spiders. This makes them useful insect eaters.
3340.m: Hedgehogs also eat worms and larvae.

3341.q: What do you hear music and voices with?
3341.e: Your ears catch sound waves and pass them on to the brain. There they become sounds and words.

3342.q: Do ants have ears to hear with?
a: Yes, big ears on their head
Yes, but only on their belly
No, they hear with their eyes
3342.e: Ants do not have ears like we humans do. They sense shaking and vibrations through their body.

3343.q: What makes the bearded vulture look different from most other European vultures?
3343.e: Unlike many vultures with a rounded tail, the bearded vulture has a strikingly long, wedge-shaped tail. You can recognise it by this from far away.
3343.m: Its tail is long and wedge-shaped.

3344.q: What is the job of the pale patch on the rump of a fleeing roe deer?
a: It warns other deer of danger
3344.e: When a roe deer flees, its pale rump patch is easy to see. This lets other deer know that danger is near.
3344.m: The rump patch warns other deer.

3345.e: With white storks, the mother and father take turns sitting on the eggs. That way both can also go and find food.

3346.q: What does a red deer stag need its antlers for?
a: To impress other stags and to fight
3346.e: A stag shows its strength with its antlers. In autumn, stags sometimes use them to fight over the females.
3346.m: Antlers show strength in a fight.

3347.q: Roughly how far can a lynx jump?
3347.e: The lynx's powerful back legs allow long jumps. This helps it make surprise attacks on prey.
3347.m: A lynx jumps far and powerfully.

a: At the tip of an arm
3348.e: A starfish's mouth sits right in the middle of its underside. It eats its prey from there.
3348.m: The mouth is underneath, in the middle.

3349.q: How many young does a mother hedgehog usually have at once?
3349.e: A mother hedgehog usually gives birth to four or five hoglets. She looks after her young on her own.
3349.m: Hedgehog mothers usually have four or five young.

3350.q: What sound does a cow make?
3350.e: Cows make a deep sound called mooing. They use it to talk to each other or to their calf.

3351.q: How do reindeer get to their food under the snow in winter?
a: They dig tunnels with their antlers
They wait for the snow to melt
3351.e: Reindeer scrape the snow away with their broad hooves. They can smell the lichens even under the snow.

3352.q: How common is the tawny owl in Switzerland compared with other owls?
a: It is the commonest owl in Switzerland
It does not live in Switzerland at all
3352.e: The tawny owl is considered the commonest and most widespread owl in Switzerland. It lives in many forests, parks and even towns.
3352.m: The tawny owl is the commonest Swiss owl.

3353.q: What do magpies do when they find more food than they can eat at once?
a: They just leave it lying there
They always give it to other animals
3353.e: Magpies often hide extra food in different places so they can come back to it later. This behaviour is called food storing or caching.

3354.q: How many legs does an insect such as a beetle or an ant have?
3354.e: All insects have exactly six legs. That sets them apart from spiders, for example, which have eight. Insects also have a body in three parts.

3355.q: What is special about giraffes' blood pressure?
a: It is much higher than in most other animals
It is much lower than in all animals
Giraffes have no blood pressure at all
It is exactly like a mouse's
3355.e: Because the blood has to be pumped so far up to the head, giraffes have very high blood pressure. Their heart and blood vessels are especially strong because of this.
3355.m: Giraffes have very high blood pressure.

3356.q: What is meant by the greenhouse effect?
a: Gases in the atmosphere keep heat on Earth
The sun comes closer to the Earth every year
It makes the Earth spin faster
3356.e: Certain gases such as CO2 let sunlight through to the Earth but hold back the heat radiation that the Earth gives off again. Without this natural effect, it would be much colder on Earth.
3356.m: Greenhouse gases keep heat in the atmosphere.

3357.q: What is the great spotted woodpecker especially good at?
3357.e: The great spotted woodpecker hacks holes in wood with its hard beak. This is how it finds food and makes its nest hole.

3358.q: What is a good hiding place for an adder?
3358.e: There it finds warmth and shelter. That is why stone piles are important for nature conservation.

3359.q: Which language does the word ‘hippopotamus’ come from?
3359.e: Hippopotamus comes from Greek: hippos means horse and potamos means river. So the word means ‘river horse’.
3359.m: Hippopotamus is Greek for river horse.

3360.q: What does the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), based in Geneva, deal with?
a: Worldwide rules for telecommunications and the internet
3360.e: The ITU coordinates technical standards for telephone, radio and the internet worldwide. It is one of the oldest international organisations and is based in Geneva.
3360.m: The ITU sets the rules for communications technology worldwide.

3361.q: What does the word ‘pest’ mean for greenfly in the garden?
a: They harm crops and weaken them
They are always poisonous to humans
3361.e: Pests are animals that damage plants or harvests. In nature, though, greenfly also play a part as food for other animals.
3361.m: A pest is an animal that harms crops.

3362.q: Which colour of clothes do mosquitoes often especially like?
3362.e: Mosquitoes often spot dark clothes more easily than light ones. That is why people in dark T-shirts sometimes get bitten more often.

3363.q: What does a wild hamster build for itself underground?
3363.e: Wild hamsters dig deep burrows with several tunnels and chambers. There they sleep and store their food.

3365.q: What is the group of young males that do not live in the main herd called?
3365.e: Older or young bulls often form their own groups. They join the herd mainly in the mating season.

3366.q: Which sense is especially important for the puma when hunting at night?
a: Good eyesight even in low light
3366.e: Cats can see much better in the dark than humans. This helps the puma hunt at dusk and at night.
3366.m: Pumas see well in the dark.

3367.q: How does its wide head help the hammerhead shark?
a: It helps it see and sense better
It helps it hide in the sand
3367.e: Because the head is so wide, the eyes and sense organs are far apart. This lets the hammerhead notice more of its surroundings.
3367.m: The wide head helps it sense and see.

a: Live or from an egg, depending on the species
Always from eggs in the sand on the beach
3368.e: Depending on the shark species, the young are born live or hatch from eggs. Both happen among sharks.
3368.m: Baby sharks hatch from eggs or are born live.

3371.q: How long can a male emperor penguin go without food while keeping the egg warm?
3371.e: While the male keeps the egg warm, he eats nothing and lives off his fat. This can last many weeks until the female comes back.
3371.m: Male emperor penguins go hungry for weeks for the egg.

3372.q: Why are many seahorse species under threat today?
a: They are caught and sold as souvenirs or medicine
They cannot cope with salt water
3372.e: People catch many seahorses to sell, for example as souvenirs or for traditional medicine. This is making some species rarer and rarer.
3372.m: Being caught threatens many seahorse species.

3373.q: In which habitats on land does the common frog feel especially at home?
a: Only in snow high in the mountains
3373.e: The common frog likes damp, shady places such as woods, meadows and gardens with ponds. There it finds enough food and hiding places.
3373.m: Common frogs like damp, green places.

a: The highest law of a state, which sets out rights and limits on power.
3374.e: A constitution sets out how a state is organised and what rights citizens have. In dictatorships the constitution is often ignored or changed.

3375.q: Do goldfish have eyelids that let them close their eyes?
3375.e: Goldfish have no eyelids, so they cannot close their eyes. That is why they sleep with their eyes open.
3375.m: Goldfish sleep with their eyes open.

3376.q: How does the swift usually catch its prey?
a: With its beak wide open, in mid-flight
By pecking for insects on the ground
By diving into the water like a kingfisher
With its talons like a bird of prey
3376.e: While flying, the swift opens its beak wide and scoops up small insects in mid-air. This way of hunting suits its life in the air perfectly.
3376.m: Prey is caught in flight with an open beak.

3377.q: What sound does a dog normally make?
3377.e: Barking is the typical sound dogs use to communicate, for example to give a warning. Some dogs also howl or growl.
3377.m: Dogs bark to make themselves heard.

3378.q: Why are many female ducks' feathers rather brown and plain?
a: For camouflage while sitting on the nest
Because females do not like colourful feathers
3378.e: The brown, speckled feathers help the mother duck hide on the nest. This gives the eggs better protection from enemies.
3378.m: Brown feathers camouflage her while she incubates.

3379.q: How can you best tell the difference between a white and a black rhino?
a: By the shape of the mouth
By the colour of the fur
By the size of the ears
By the length of the tail
3379.e: The white rhino has a broad, flat mouth for eating grass. The black rhino has a pointed lip for eating leaves.
3379.m: The mouth shows which rhino it is.

3380.q: In which habitats can you find the great tit in Switzerland?
3380.e: The great tit lives in woods, parks and gardens. It is even found in the middle of towns if there are trees.
3380.m: Great tits live in woods and gardens.

3381.q: Which animal is the African wild dog more closely related to than to the hyena?
3381.e: Wild dogs belong to the dog family, so they are related to wolves. Hyenas belong to a family of their own.
3381.m: Related to the wolf, not the hyena.

a: They are among the more primitive primates
They have only half as many teeth
They are only half as big as humans
They live only half the year
3383.e: Lemurs show many features of early primates, such as a moist nose. That is why they are grouped apart from monkeys and apes.

3384.q: What is the firm case that some moth caterpillars pupate inside called?
3384.e: Before pupating, some caterpillars spin a cocoon of silk threads around themselves. Inside it they are well protected.

3385.q: Which animals are the hippopotamus's closest living relatives?
3385.e: Strange as it sounds, whales and dolphins are the hippo's closest relatives. They share common ancestors.
3385.m: Whales are related to the hippo.

3386.q: What does a bonobo mainly eat?
3386.e: Fruit makes up most of its diet. It also eats leaves, shoots and other plant parts.

3387.q: Why is the kingfisher seen as a sign of good water quality?
a: Because it only finds enough fish in clean, natural waters
Because it survives only in chemically cleaned water
Because it drinks and tests the water directly
Because anglers use it to check the water
3387.e: Only clean water has enough small fish for the kingfisher. So if it lives there, that shows the water is healthy.
3387.m: Kingfishers show that water is clean.

3388.q: Which animals can be dangerous to swan cygnets?
3388.e: Small cygnets are not yet as big and strong as their parents. Foxes or large fish can be dangerous to them.
3388.m: Foxes are a danger to cygnets.

3389.q: Why is the sand lizard a good example of species protection in Switzerland?
a: Because it shows how important natural, dry habitats are for many species
Because it is the only protected reptile in Switzerland
Because it has died out in Switzerland
Because it lives in every Swiss garden
3389.e: Protecting the sand lizard's habitat often helps many other animals and plants that need similar conditions. That is why it is seen as an important species in nature conservation.
3389.m: Protecting it helps other species too.

3390.q: Why did people once take chamois to faraway countries such as New Zealand?
a: So they could be hunted there
So they could herd sheep there
So they could eat weeds in gardens
3390.e: Chamois were released in New Zealand, for example, so that hunters could hunt them there. Today wild populations live there.

3391.q: What do stork partners do when they meet again at the nest?
a: They clatter their beaks together as a greeting
They fly away again at once
They build a new nest somewhere else at once
3391.e: When a stork partner comes back to the nest, both greet each other by loudly clattering their beaks together. This strengthens their bond.
3391.m: A greeting with shared beak clattering.

3392.q: Why are many garden owners in Switzerland pleased to have edible frogs in their garden pond?
a: Because they are natural pest controllers and bring life to the pond
3392.e: Edible frogs eat lots of insects and so help keep a natural balance in the garden. Their calls and behaviour also bring a garden pond to life.
3392.m: Edible frogs liven up garden ponds naturally.

3393.q: What is a pond turtle's shell made of?
a: Bony plates covered with horny scutes
Only hard scales that can be shed
3393.e: The shell is firmly joined to the skeleton, for example to the ribs. That is why a turtle can never climb out of its shell.
3393.m: The shell is part of the skeleton.

3395.q: Roughly how long is a female wolf pregnant before her pups are born?
3395.e: A she-wolf's pregnancy lasts about 63 days, so about nine weeks. Then usually several pups are born at the same time.
3395.m: She-wolves carry their pups for about nine weeks.

3396.q: What does a grasshopper use to jump so far?
3396.e: The back legs are much stronger than the other legs. They work like springs.
3396.m: Strong back legs make the jump.

3397.q: Which African country is known as the place where Jane Goodall studied chimpanzees?
3397.e: Jane Goodall studied chimpanzees in Gombe National Park in Tanzania. She watched the animals there for many years.
3397.m: Tanzania is known for Jane Goodall's research.

3398.q: How does a housefly manage to land on the ceiling?
a: It turns over in the air just before landing
It sticks spit on its feet first
3398.e: Just before a housefly reaches the ceiling, it flips over in the air in a flash. This lets it land feet first.

3399.q: How does the bearded vulture's feeding differ from the golden eagle's hunting?
a: The bearded vulture hardly hunts at all but eats dead animals
The bearded vulture hunts only live fish
The bearded vulture hunts only at night
The bearded vulture eats only plants
3399.e: Golden eagles often catch live animals themselves, while the bearded vulture mainly uses carrion and bones. So it is more of a scavenger than a hunter.
3399.m: The bearded vulture scavenges instead of hunting.

3400.q: Which animal group do whitefish belong to?
3400.e: Whitefish have a skeleton made of bone and breathe with gills. That is why they belong to the bony fish.

3402.q: Why do squirrels have to gnaw all the time?
a: Because otherwise their teeth fall out
3402.e: A squirrel's front teeth keep growing throughout its life. Gnawing keeps them at the right length.

3403.q: What is the famous children's story whose main character was originally a roe deer?
3403.e: The story of Bambi was written by Felix Salten and is really about a roe deer. In the famous Disney film, though, Bambi looks a bit different.
3403.m: Bambi was originally a roe deer.

3404.q: Roughly how old can a sheep get?
3404.e: A sheep lives about 10 to 12 years. With good care some sheep can live even longer.

3405.q: How does a great crested grebe usually react when an enemy surprises it?
a: It dives instead of flying away
It attacks the enemy at once
It freezes motionless in the water
3405.e: Because diving is quicker than taking off, the great crested grebe usually escapes under water. There it is also hard to see.
3405.m: In danger it prefers to dive.

3406.q: How fast can a pet cat run?
3406.e: Over short distances, a pet cat can run at up to 48 km/h. That is usually enough to catch a mouse.
3406.m: Cats can sprint very fast for a short time.

3407.q: How do young meerkats learn to eat dangerous prey such as scorpions?
a: Adults first bring them made-safe prey and practise with them
They read about it in books
They learn it alone, by chance
They are never allowed to eat scorpions
3407.e: Older meerkats first bring the young dead prey or prey with the sting removed. Later the young practise with live prey.
3407.m: Adults teach the young to hunt.

3409.q: Since when have golden hamsters been kept as pets?
3409.e: People only started breeding golden hamsters as pets in the 1930s. Before that they were known only from the wild in Syria.
3409.m: Hamsters have only been pets since about 1930.

3410.q: What colour is the great tit's back?
3410.e: The great tit's back shimmers greenish to olive. This lets it hide well among leaves.

3412.q: What happens to a male octopus after mating?
a: It becomes a father and helps out
It looks for a new den
3412.e: Many male octopuses die only a short time after mating. This is part of their short life cycle.

3413.q: Where does the red kite often look for food when farmers mow their fields?
3413.e: Mowing disturbs or injures small animals such as mice or insects. The red kite takes advantage of this and circles over the fields.
3413.m: Red kites like to hunt over mown meadows.

3414.q: In which waters does the edible frog like to live best?
3414.e: Edible frogs prefer ponds, pools and lakes with calm water. There they find enough plants and food.
3414.m: The edible frog likes calm, still water.

3415.q: Are guinea pigs closely related to rabbits?
a: No, they belong to different animal groups
Yes, they are practically the same species
Yes, rabbits are their direct parents
Yes, they can have babies together
3415.e: Even though guinea pigs and rabbits are often kept in a similar way, they are not closely related biologically. Rabbits even belong to a completely different group, the lagomorphs.
3415.m: Guinea pigs are not related to rabbits.

3416.q: How many legs does an ant have?
3416.e: Ants are insects. All insects have exactly six legs.

3417.q: Which creature is closely related to the stag beetle?
3417.e: The lesser stag beetle is a smaller relative in the stag beetle family. It also lives in dead wood.
3417.m: Lesser stag beetles are relatives of the stag beetle.

3418.q: Why does the cuckoo chick sometimes hatch faster than the host bird's eggs?
a: So it can be first to throw the other eggs out
Because it is incubated at a colder temperature
3418.e: Hatching early gives the cuckoo chick an advantage, because it can then throw the other unhatched eggs out of the nest first. This way it gets all the food for itself.
3418.m: Hatching early gives the cuckoo an advantage.

3420.q: Do sparrows prefer to live alone or with others?
3420.e: Sparrows are sociable birds and like living in larger groups. Together they are better protected from enemies.

3421.q: How many wings does a bumblebee have?
3421.e: A bumblebee has two pairs of wings, so four wings in all. With them it can even carry heavy loads such as pollen.

3422.q: How did the rule of the Romanian dictator Nicolae Ceaușescu end?
a: In 1989 he was overthrown in a revolution and executed
He resigned voluntarily and went into exile
He ruled until he died of old age
The EU made him an honorary citizen
3422.e: At the end of 1989 there was a violent uprising against Ceaușescu in Romania. He and his wife were shot after a short trial.

3423.q: What is the typical leap a fox uses to catch a mouse under the snow called?
3423.e: In the mousing pounce, the fox jumps high into the air and then dives nose first into the snow. This lets it surprise the mouse from above.
3423.m: The catching leap is called the mousing pounce.

3424.q: What affectionate name is the white stork sometimes given in old German stories?
3424.e: In old tales the stork is sometimes called Adebar. This name comes from earlier forms of the German language.
3424.m: Adebar is an old name for the stork.

3425.q: Why do dromedaries live in Australia today?
a: They were brought in as pack animals in the 19th century
They were released as zoo animals
3425.e: They were brought to Australia to carry goods through the desert. Later many were set free and went wild.
3425.m: They came to Australia as pack animals.

3426.q: In which year did East and West Germany become one country again?
3426.e: One year after the fall of the Wall, the GDR and the Federal Republic of Germany were reunited. That was on 3 October 1990.

3427.q: Does the stone marten truly hibernate in winter?
a: No, it stays active all year
Yes, it sleeps right through from October to April
Yes, but only for two weeks
No, it migrates to Africa instead
3427.e: Unlike some small mammals, the stone marten does not truly hibernate. It stays active all year round and looks for food in winter too.
3427.m: The stone marten does not hibernate.

3428.q: Where does the bright blue colour of the kingfisher's feathers really come from?
a: From light being scattered by the structure of the feathers
3428.e: The blue does not come from a pigment but from the fine structure of the feathers, which scatters the light. This is called structural colour.
3428.m: The blue comes from light, not pigment.

3429.q: Why do wild boar often churn up the forest floor?
3429.e: Wild boar dig in the soil with their snouts because tasty roots and worms are hidden there. This is also called rooting.
3429.m: Rooting is how they look for food.

3430.q: What must young aphids do in order to grow?
3430.e: Aphids have a firm skin that does not grow with them. So they shed it several times, usually four times before becoming adults.

3431.q: Why do newborn piglets drink their mother's milk straight after birth?
a: The first milk protects them from illness
Otherwise they must find food themselves at once
3431.e: The mother's first milk is very special. It protects the little piglets from illness in their first days.
3431.m: The first milk protects young piglets.

3432.q: Are there different species of mole in the world?
a: No, there is only one species
No, moles live only in Switzerland
No, moles live only in Africa
3432.e: There are several different species of mole around the world. Here in Switzerland we have the European mole.
3432.m: There are several mole species worldwide.

3433.q: Roughly how big does an adult ladybird get?
a: About the size of a small pea
As big as a hen's egg
3433.e: Most ladybirds are only a few millimetres long, about the size of a small pea. Even so, they eat an amazing amount.
3433.m: Ladybirds are as small as peas.

3434.q: What job does a meerkat standing upright on a mound have while the others are feeding?
a: It keeps watch and warns the group
It calls the young to play
3434.e: Meerkats take turns as sentries. If the sentry spots an enemy, it warns the group with a loud call.

3435.q: Why do many robins die in their first year?
a: Because of cold, enemies and lack of experience
3435.e: Young robins do not know dangers as well as adult birds. Cold and enemies are especially hard on them.

3436.q: What do young marmots often do before starting a family of their own?
a: They help their parents raise younger brothers and sisters
They leave the colony right after birth
They build their own burrow far away at once
They never live with the family again
3436.e: Young marmots often stay with their family for one or two years. During this time they help raise their younger siblings.

3437.q: What kind of feet does a roe deer have?
a: Cloven hooves, so two toes per foot
Hooves like a horse with one toe
3437.e: Roe deer are even-toed hoofed animals. Their feet have two toes that together form a hoof.

3438.q: Which woodlouse species is common in gardens in Switzerland?
3438.e: The common rough woodlouse is common in Central Europe. You often find it on walls, under stones and in gardens.
3438.m: The common rough woodlouse is common in gardens.

3439.q: Where does the golden eagle get its English name from?
a: From the golden feathers on the back of its neck
3439.e: Adult golden eagles have feathers on the back of the head and neck that shimmer golden brown. That is where the name golden eagle comes from.
3439.m: Golden neck feathers give it its name.

3440.q: How does a stone marten usually behave towards people?
a: It avoids direct contact and is rather shy
It actively seeks people out for cuddles
It regularly attacks people on purpose
It happily lets people stroke it
3440.e: Although the stone marten often lives near people, it usually stays shy and careful. As a rule it avoids direct contact with humans.

3441.q: Which animal family do the jackal, wolf and domestic dog belong to?
3441.e: The jackal, wolf and domestic dog belong to the dog family. Their scientific genus is called Canis.
3441.m: Jackal, wolf and dog belong to the dog family.

3442.q: How many arms does a sunstar, a large kind of starfish, have?
3442.e: The sunstar is a large starfish with many arms, usually between 8 and 14. This makes it look like a sun with rays.

3443.q: In which season can you see many common frogs crossing roads?
3443.e: As soon as temperatures rise in spring, common frogs start their journey to the ponds. On the way they often have to cross roads.
3443.m: Many common frogs migrate in spring.

3444.q: What does a goose swallow to help grind up plants in its stomach?
3444.e: Geese have no teeth. So they swallow small stones that help grind up the tough plant parts in their stomach.

3445.q: How does a new bee develop?
a: From an egg, via larva and pupa
3445.e: The queen lays an egg in a cell of the honeycomb. A larva hatches from it, later turns into a pupa and finally becomes a fully grown bee.
3445.m: Bees develop from egg to bee.

3446.q: What is a squirrel's nest called?
3446.e: A squirrel's nest is called a drey and is made of twigs, moss and leaves. It is usually high up in a tree.
3446.m: A squirrel's nest is called a drey.

3447.q: When is the wood mouse most active?
a: Only at midday in the sun
Only in the depths of winter
3447.e: The wood mouse is nocturnal and looks for food mainly in the dark.

3448.q: What does a goose's beak look like?
a: Broad, with fine ridges for plucking plants
Pointed and hooked like an eagle's
Geese have no beak at all
3448.e: The broad beak has small ridges along the edge, called lamellae. With them the goose can tear off grass easily and sieve food from the water.
3448.m: A goose's beak has fine ridges.

3449.q: What colour is the red kite's tail compared with the rest of its feathers?
3449.e: The red kite's tail is reddish with fine dark bars across it. Together with its forked shape, this is an important way to recognise it.

3450.q: Which organ produces the hormone insulin?
3450.e: The pancreas makes insulin, which lowers the blood sugar level. It also produces digestive enzymes.

3451.q: What is it called when goat herds come back down from the alpine pasture to the valley in autumn?
3451.e: In autumn it gets too cold on the mountain pastures and the goats move back down to the valley. This is called the Alpabzug.
3451.m: In autumn the goats come down to the valley.

3452.q: How many young does a puma usually have in one litter?
3452.e: Female pumas usually have two or three young, sometimes up to four. They raise them alone.
3452.m: Pumas usually have two or three young.

3453.q: What special adaptation does the Alpine salamander show compared with amphibians from warmer regions?
a: It is adapted to cool temperatures and short summers
It needs very high temperatures to survive
It can live only in deserts
It needs salt water to survive
3453.e: In the mountains, summers are short and temperatures are lower than in the lowlands. Over time the Alpine salamander has adapted to these special conditions.
3453.m: It is adapted to cool mountain conditions.

3454.q: Roughly how old can chamois get in the wild?
3454.e: In the wild, chamois can reach a ripe old age of 15 to 22 years. This also depends on food and enemies, though.

3470.q: Which animal hops on strong back legs and carries its young in a pouch?
3470.e: The kangaroo lives in Australia and can jump very far with its strong legs. The young grow up in their mother's pouch.
3470.m: The kangaroo carries its babies in a pouch.

a: A group of the 20 most important economies in the world
A UN department for environmental issues
3482.e: In the G20 the governments of the biggest economies meet to talk about the economy, the climate and other global issues. Switzerland is not one of the permanent members.
3482.m: The G20 are the 20 biggest economic powers.

3490.q: Which country calls itself the “Land of the Thunder Dragon” and still shows the dragon on its flag today?
3490.e: Bhutan is also called the “Land of the Thunder Dragon”. The yellow and orange halves of the flag stand for worldly and spiritual power.
3490.m: Bhutan's flag shows a thunder dragon.

3528.q: What was the Reichstag fire in 1933?
a: A fire in the German parliament building that the Nazis used for their own ends.
A festival planned by the Nazis.
A natural event with no consequences.
3528.e: After the Reichstag fire the National Socialists blamed their opponents and severely restricted basic rights. This helped them expand their power.
3528.m: The fire served as an excuse to seize power.

3537.q: What is World Refugee Day for?
a: To remember people who have had to flee from war or danger
To celebrate new countries on the map
To remember the founding of the EU
3537.e: On World Refugee Day, people all over the world think of those who have had to leave their homes. It is meant to show that refugees need help and protection.

a: A group in which several countries work together
A club for children in a town
A shop that sells goods from abroad
A school with children from many countries
3582.e: In an international organisation, countries work together on issues such as peace, health or the environment. The UN and the EU are examples.

3623.q: What do the hammer and sickle on communist flags mean?
a: They stand for workers and farmers
They stand for kings and nobles
They stand for soldiers and generals
They stand for teachers and pupils
3623.e: The hammer stands for the workers in the factories, the sickle for the farmers in the countryside. Together they were supposed to build society.
3623.m: The hammer and sickle stand for workers and farmers.

3625.q: How does a leopard typically hunt?
a: It sneaks up and makes a short dash
It chases its prey for hours
3625.e: The leopard creeps as close as possible to its prey. Then it overpowers it with a short sprint.
3625.m: Leopards sneak up on their prey.

3634.q: Which animal is often called the “king of the animals” and lives in Africa?
3634.e: Because of its strength and courage, the lion is seen as the king of the animals. Lions live in groups called prides.
3634.m: The lion is seen as the king of the animals.

3642.q: What is the celebration called when a Jewish boy becomes a religious adult at 13?
3642.e: At his Bar Mitzvah the boy reads from the Torah in public for the first time. After that, in the Jewish faith, he is seen as religiously responsible.
3642.m: The Bar Mitzvah celebrates becoming a religious adult.

3648.q: What happens to your skin if you stay in the sun too long?
3648.e: Too much sun damages the skin and makes it red and sore. That is why sun cream is important.
3648.m: Too much sun hurts your skin.

3651.q: What was the “Cultural Revolution” in China?
a: A campaign by Mao against supposed enemies and old traditions.
3651.e: During the Cultural Revolution millions of people were persecuted, humiliated or killed because they supposedly did not think in a “revolutionary” enough way. Education and culture also suffered badly.
3651.m: The Cultural Revolution persecuted supposed enemies.

3653.q: Which animal is the biggest animal in the world and lives in the sea?
3653.e: The blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived on Earth. It can grow over 30 metres long.
3653.m: The blue whale is the biggest animal of all.

3657.q: What does it show when a wild dog opens its mouth slightly and approaches others in a friendly way?
a: It is showing affection to the pack
It wants to run away at once
3657.e: Wild dogs often greet each other with sounds and body contact. This strengthens the bond within the pack.
3657.m: Greetings strengthen the bond in the pack.

3679.q: Which bear is a close relative of the brown bear and lives in the Arctic?
3679.e: Brown bears and polar bears are closely related. In rare cases they even have cubs together. Raccoons and koalas are not real bears.
3679.m: Brown bears and polar bears are close relatives.

3681.q: Why does a piece of wood float on water?
a: Because wood is lighter than the same amount of water
Because wood is made of water
3681.e: Wood has a lower density than water, which is why it floats on top. Heavy materials such as stone sink because they are denser than water.
3681.m: Lighter things float, heavier things sink.

3682.q: Where does a female stoat usually give birth to her young?
a: In a burrow taken over from a mouse she has caught
In a nest she builds herself in a tree
In a cave high in the mountains
Out in an open field with no shelter
3682.e: The female stoat often uses the burrow of a mouse she has caught to raise her young. This saves time and energy.

3683.q: In which weather do mosquitoes multiply especially fast?
3683.e: After rain, lots of small puddles form where mosquitoes can lay their eggs. In warm weather the larvae then grow especially fast.

3684.q: Who feeds the young robins in the nest?
3684.e: Mother and father both fly back and forth to feed the hungry chicks with insects. That is a lot of work for the two of them.

3685.q: What is a small relative of the kangaroo called?
3685.e: Wallabies are small relatives of kangaroos. They look similar and hop too, but they are much smaller.

3686.q: Why is milk actually not good for hedgehogs?
a: They cannot digest it well and get diarrhoea
Hedgehogs don't like the taste at all
Milk makes their spines fall out
3686.e: Many people think milk is good for hedgehogs, but they find it hard to digest milk sugar. Milk makes them ill and can even be dangerous.

3687.q: What job do the intervertebral discs have in the spine?
a: They cushion knocks between the vertebrae
3687.e: Discs sit between the vertebrae and act like shock absorbers. They make the spine flexible and protect it.

3688.q: How many compound eyes does a praying mantis have?
3688.e: It has two large compound eyes made up of many tiny single eyes. With them it can see movement very well.
3688.m: Two large compound eyes see movement.

3689.q: Which animals are the closest relatives of the alpaca?
3689.e: All these animals belong to the New World camels of South America. The alpaca is especially closely related to the vicuña.

3690.q: How many legs does a garden spider have?
3690.e: Spiders have eight legs; this makes them different from insects, which have only six legs. The garden spider uses its legs for walking and for sensing.

3691.q: Why are ladybirds so brightly coloured?
a: To warn enemies that they taste bad
So they can hide in the dark
3691.e: The bright colours tell birds: careful, I taste horrible! That is why many enemies prefer to leave the ladybird alone.

3692.q: How does a swallow usually drink?
a: In flight, just above the surface of the water
It always lands on the bank to do it
It only drinks raindrops from leaves
It dives completely under the water
3692.e: Swallows drink by briefly skimming the surface of the water with their beak while flying. They do not have to land.
3692.m: The swallow drinks in flight over the water.

3693.q: About how long can a fully grown great white shark get?
3693.e: The great white shark is one of the largest predatory fish. Some individuals grow even a little longer.
3693.m: The great white shark can grow up to 6 metres long.

3694.q: Is it allowed to hunt magpies in Switzerland?
a: Yes, but only during the hunting season
Yes, all year round with no rules
3694.e: In Switzerland the magpie, like the carrion crow and the jay, is one of the birds that may be hunted. It may only be hunted from August to mid-February; during the breeding season it is protected.
3694.m: Magpies may be hunted but have a closed season.

3695.q: Why are jaguars sometimes killed by people?
a: Because they can kill farm animals such as cattle
3695.e: Jaguars sometimes catch cattle and other domestic animals. This leads to conflicts with livestock farmers.
3695.m: Conflicts with livestock farmers threaten the jaguar.

3696.q: What does an earthworm do when it gets cold in winter?
a: It moves deep down into the soil
It makes itself a fur coat
3696.e: Deep in the soil it is warmer than at the surface. There the earthworm waits until it gets milder again.
3696.m: In winter the worm goes deeper.

3697.q: What colour were the wild ancestors of the goldfish mostly?
3697.e: The wild Prussian carp was a dull grey-green colour. The bright colours of today's goldfish only appeared through breeding.
3697.m: The wild ancestors were not golden.

3698.q: Who normally has young in a wolf pack?
3698.e: In a wolf pack usually only the parents, the so-called alpha pair, have offspring. The other members of the pack still help to raise the pups.
3698.m: Only the parent pair has pups.

3699.q: What are a dog's whiskers, also called vibrissae, for?
a: They help it sense its close surroundings
3699.e: The vibrissae on the muzzle and eyebrows are especially sensitive and help the dog sense air movements and obstacles close by, especially in the dark. They are connected to many nerve endings.

3700.q: On which continents is the stoat found?
3700.e: The stoat is found in large parts of Europe, Asia and North America. It also copes well with cold regions.
3700.m: The stoat lives on three continents.

3701.q: What is the legal status of the brown bear in Switzerland today?
a: It is a strictly protected species
It may be hunted all year round
It may only be hunted in winter
3701.e: In Switzerland the brown bear is strictly protected by law. This means that, as a rule, it may not be hunted.
3701.m: Brown bears are strictly protected in Switzerland.

3702.q: How do the horns of the ibex differ from those of the chamois?
a: Ibex horns are much longer and curved like a sabre, chamois horns are short and hook-shaped
Both species have horns of exactly the same shape
Only the chamois has horns, the ibex does not
Ibex horns are straight like sticks
3702.e: The horns of the ibex are long and curve strongly backwards, while the chamois has much shorter, hook-shaped horns. This makes it easy to tell the two mountain animals apart.
3702.m: Long curved horns tell the ibex from the chamois.

3703.q: Which dangers especially threaten eagle owls in Switzerland?
3703.e: A big danger for eagle owls is colliding with power lines and cars. That is why dangerous lines are now partly made safer with protective devices.
3703.m: Pylons and roads endanger eagle owls.

3704.q: About how big can male stag beetles get?
3704.e: Including their antlers, males reach up to around 8 centimetres. This makes them the largest beetle in Europe.
3704.m: The stag beetle is Europe's largest beetle.

3705.q: Which fish family does the trout belong to?
3705.e: Trout belong to the salmon family, just like salmon. Both like to live in cool, clean water.
3705.m: Trout belong to the salmon family.

3706.q: What does the grass snake use to smell its surroundings especially well?
3706.e: The tongue picks up scents from the air. They are then analysed inside the mouth.
3706.m: Flicking the tongue helps with smelling.

3707.q: What is the speculum on a mallard?
a: A blue patch on the wing with a white border
A red pattern on the tail
A yellow dot on the beak
A black stripe on the belly
3707.e: Mallards have a shimmering blue patch on the wing, framed in white at the front and back. It is especially easy to see in flight.

a: A wild donkey from the desert
A donkey from a fairy tale
3708.e: Miniature donkeys are a small breed of donkey and stay small even when fully grown. A young donkey, on the other hand, is called a foal.

3710.q: Is the hippo a good swimmer like a fish?
a: No, it rather walks along the bottom
Yes, it swims like a dolphin
Yes, it can fly and swim
No, it cannot go into the water at all
3710.e: Hippos cannot really swim. Instead they walk or bounce along the bottom of the river.

3711.q: About how much weight can an Alpine marmot lose during hibernation?
a: Up to half its body weight
3711.e: Because it does not eat during hibernation, the marmot lives off its fat reserves. By spring it can lose a lot of weight as a result.
3711.m: Marmots get much lighter in winter.

3712.q: What is the main job of the workers in a wasp colony?
a: Finding food and building the nest
3712.e: The workers collect food for the larvae and keep building the nest. The queen, on the other hand, takes care of laying eggs.

3713.q: How long can the pregnancy of a female Alpine salamander last at higher altitudes?
3713.e: The higher and colder the habitat, the longer the young take to develop inside the mother's body. At lower, warmer altitudes it is quicker.
3713.m: The higher up, the longer the pregnancy.

3714.q: What do young swifts practise shortly before they fly for the first time?
a: They do press-ups and strengthen their wings in the nest
They run around on the ground
3714.e: Before the young leave the nest, they strengthen their muscles by flapping their wings. After that they fly off on their own straight away.
3714.m: Young birds train their wings before leaving.

3715.q: In which European zoo can you visit live giant pandas?
3715.e: Giant pandas have lived at Schönbrunn Zoo in Vienna for many years. Visitors can watch them there.
3715.m: Pandas live in the zoo in Vienna.

3716.q: What colour is a male sparrow's beak usually in summer?
3716.e: In summer, during the breeding season, the male's beak is black. You can see this especially well when he wants to impress a female.
3716.m: The beak is black in summer.

3717.q: How does a ladybird most often get around?
a: It crawls on plants or flies short distances
It jumps very far like a flea
It swims in the water most of the time
It usually digs itself into the ground
3717.e: Most of the time the ladybird crawls around on leaves and stems. When it needs to go further, it can also fly short distances.

3718.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
a: Mass stays the same everywhere, weight depends on gravity
Mass and weight are exactly the same
Weight stays the same everywhere, mass changes
3718.e: The mass of a body is the same everywhere in the universe, wherever it is. Weight, on the other hand, depends on gravity, which is weaker on the Moon, for example.
3718.m: Mass stays the same, weight changes.

3719.q: Where do European pond turtles usually mate?
3719.e: The male swims after the female and tries to climb onto her. Later the female goes onto land to lay her eggs.
3719.m: Mating usually takes place in the water.

3720.q: Why is the stag beetle an indicator species for good forests?
a: It is only found in near-natural forests with lots of dead wood
3720.e: If you find one, the forest is usually valuable for many species. If it is missing, old trees are often missing too.

3721.q: Which bird family does the kestrel belong to?
3721.e: The kestrel belongs to the falcon family, as does the peregrine falcon. Falcons are fast, skilful hunters with pointed wings.
3721.m: The kestrel is a true falcon.

3722.q: Why does a bumblebee buzz when it flies?
a: Because it moves its wings very fast
Because it hums with its mouth
Because air whistles through its fur
Because it rubs its legs together
3722.e: The buzzing comes from the bumblebee's fast wingbeats. You often hear it before you see the bumblebee.

3723.q: About how wide are the spread wings of a barn owl?
3723.e: The wingspan of a barn owl is about 90 centimetres. This helps it glide calmly through the air for a long time.
3723.m: The wings are almost a metre wide.

3724.q: What does the skin of the Alpine salamander produce to protect it?
3724.e: When in danger, the skin releases a poisonous secretion that scares off predators. This alkaloid is called samandarin.
3724.m: Its skin releases poison against enemies.

3725.q: What protection status does the bearded vulture have in Switzerland?
a: It is not protected at all
3725.e: The bearded vulture is strictly protected in Switzerland because it was wiped out for a long time. Its habitat and its nests must not be disturbed.
3725.m: The bearded vulture is strictly protected.

3726.q: Where does the swallow usually spend the winter?
a: In Africa, south of the Sahara
3726.e: Most European swallows spend the winter in Africa, south of the Sahara. In spring they fly back to Europe.
3726.m: It spends the winter south of the Sahara.

3728.q: Roughly how fast can an African wild dog run when hunting?
a: Up to about 60 kilometres per hour
3728.e: Over a short distance it reaches about 60 kilometres per hour. That is much faster than an everyday bike ride.

3729.q: Which country is part of the range of the snow leopard?
3729.e: It is found in twelve countries in Asia, for example Nepal, India, China and Mongolia.
3729.m: Nepal is part of its habitat.

3730.q: What does a young okapi often do in its first weeks?
a: It stays lying in a hiding place
3730.e: Okapi calves are so-called hiders and lie hidden in the undergrowth. The mother only comes to suckle them.
3730.m: Okapi calves are left in a hiding place.

3731.q: Why do lots of sparrows often gather in a thick hedge in the evening?
3731.e: In a thick hedge the sparrows are better protected from cold and enemies at night. Sleeping together means more safety for everyone.

3732.q: What is the resting stage called in which the larva turns into a beetle?
3732.e: In a hollow in the soil the larva turns into a pupa. Later the finished beetle hatches from it.

3733.q: What is special about the antennae of dung beetles?
a: They end in a club made of plates
They are longer than the whole body
3733.e: The ends of the antennae are made of small plates that can open out like a fan. This creates a large surface for scent-sensing cells.

3734.q: What does the garden spider do as soon as an insect wriggles in its web?
a: It runs over quickly and wraps it up
It destroys the whole web straight away
3734.e: As soon as the spider feels the web trembling, it hurries to its prey. It quickly wraps the insect in strong threads.
3734.m: It hurries straight to its prey.

3735.q: What generally makes seals different from fish?
a: Seals have to come up to breathe
3735.e: Unlike fish, seals have lungs and must regularly come to the surface of the water to breathe. They are mammals, not fish.
3735.m: Seals have to come up to breathe.

3736.q: Where is the adipose fin on a trout?
a: Small, on the back, just before the tail
At the end of the tail
3736.e: The adipose fin is a small, soft fin on the back, between the dorsal fin and the tail. It is typical of salmon-family fish such as the trout.
3736.m: The adipose fin is typical of salmon-family fish.

3737.q: Roughly how many different colours and coat patterns do guinea pigs come in?
a: Very many, from one colour to patches of several colours
Only exactly three colours in total
3737.e: Thanks to breeding, guinea pigs now come in many different colours and patterns. Some are one colour, others have patches or several colours mixed.
3737.m: Guinea pigs come in many colours.

3738.q: Where do fire salamanders most like to hide during the day?
a: Under stones, dead wood or leaves
On open meadows in the sun
3738.e: During the day the fire salamander hides in damp, dark places such as under dead wood or stones. This keeps its skin protected and moist.
3738.m: It hides somewhere damp during the day.

3739.q: What does a mosquito often do first before it bites?
a: It lands carefully on the skin
It flies three times in a circle round your head
It lays an egg straight away
It makes a loud noise as a warning
3739.e: A mosquito first lands very lightly and carefully on the skin so that it is not noticed. Only then does it pierce the skin with its fine mouthpart.

3740.q: What does an octopus squirt out when it is frightened?
3740.e: When the octopus gets a fright, it squirts out a dark cloud of ink. This confuses the enemy, and the octopus can escape.
3740.m: The octopus squirts ink when in danger.

3741.q: In which part of the world is the sand lizard found naturally?
a: In Europe and parts of Asia
3741.e: The sand lizard is found in large parts of Europe and as far as Asia. In Switzerland it lives in many, but not all, regions.
3741.m: Its home is Europe and parts of Asia.

3742.q: Why is the beech marten actually considered useful by farmers?
a: It hunts lots of mice and other pests
3742.e: Beech martens eat lots of mice and other small rodents that could otherwise damage crops. Even so, they are often only seen as a nuisance.

3743.q: How many young does a squirrel usually have per litter?
3743.e: A female squirrel usually gives birth to three to six young at once. The young grow up in the nest.
3743.m: A squirrel usually has 3 to 6 young per litter.

3744.q: What does a golden eagle do when it looks out for prey for a long time?
a: It circles high in the sky or sits on a rock
It digs a hiding place in the snow
It swims in the lake and waits
It hides in the tall grass
3744.e: Golden eagles often watch their hunting ground for hours from high rocks or circle high in the sky. As soon as they spot suitable prey, they launch their attack.
3744.m: It looks for prey from rocks or high up.

3745.q: What does it mean that the cat is an obligate carnivore?
a: It absolutely needs animal protein to survive
It eats only once a year
It can easily live on a purely vegetarian diet
3745.e: Cats are so-called obligate carnivores, which means their body depends on animal protein. Without meat they lack important nutrients.

3746.q: What do you sometimes find on the shell of a sea turtle?
3746.e: Small sea creatures such as barnacles sometimes attach themselves to the hard shell. This usually does not harm the turtle much.

3747.q: What does an octopus not have in its body?
3747.e: The octopus has no bones, so it can bend its soft body a lot. This means it can even squeeze through tiny cracks.

3748.q: Which group of animals does the great green bush-cricket belong to?
3748.e: The great green bush-cricket is a large green insect with very long antennae. That is why it belongs to the long-horned grasshoppers.
3748.m: Long antennae give away the group.

3749.q: What does the playful behaviour of young otters show?
a: They are practising important skills for survival
It only shows they are bored
They do it out of fear
3749.e: When playing, young otters train, for example, their agility and skill in the water. This prepares them for hunting later on.

3750.q: What is a female cow that has not yet had a calf called?
3750.e: A young female cow that has not yet given birth to a calf is called a heifer. Only after her first calf is she called a cow.
3750.m: Young female cattle are called heifers.

3751.q: Why is a koala quite fussy about what it eats?
a: It only likes certain kinds of eucalyptus
It only eats leaves from the ground
3751.e: Of the many kinds of eucalyptus, the koala only likes very particular ones. It chooses them carefully with its fine nose.
3751.m: Koalas only like certain kinds of eucalyptus.

3752.q: What is a baby roe deer called?
3752.e: A little roe deer is called a fawn. It has a spotted coat.
3752.m: A baby roe deer is called a fawn.

3753.q: How does a housefly best find its food?
a: It smells it from far away with its antennae
3753.e: With its fine antennae the housefly can pick up smells from some distance away. This way it quickly finds something to eat.

3754.q: How does the weasel usually live socially?
3754.e: Weasels defend their hunting territory against other weasels and meet mainly in the mating season. Outside that time they live alone.

3755.q: How old does a wood mouse usually get in the wild?
3755.e: In the wild, wood mice usually only live for about a year because they have many enemies.
3755.m: Often only about one year old.

3756.q: About how long is a giraffe's tongue?
a: About as long as a finger
3756.e: The giraffe's tongue is very long and flexible. With it, it can reach for leaves even between the thorns of the acacia.
3756.m: Giraffe tongues are about 45 centimetres long.

3757.q: How many calves does a female African buffalo usually have at once?
3757.e: Usually only one calf is born. It can soon follow the herd.
3757.m: Usually only one calf is born.

3758.q: What job do the antennae of a pond skater have?
a: They sense signals from the surroundings
3758.e: With its antennae the animal senses touch and smells. This helps it find its way on the water.

3759.q: How do cockerels usually look different from hens?
a: Cockerels are bigger and more colourful
3759.e: Male chickens, cockerels, are often bigger than hens and have a more striking, colourful set of feathers. You can usually recognise them at first glance.
3759.m: Cockerels are bigger and more colourful.

3760.e: It pushes itself forward with sideways bends of its body. It has no legs.

3761.q: What is the name of the hilly area in the canton of Solothurn with many small villages?
3761.e: The Bucheggberg is a rural area in the canton of Solothurn with fields, forests and small villages. The Emmental and the Seeland are in the canton of Bern, the Toggenburg in St Gallen.
3761.m: The Bucheggberg is a rural region in the canton of Solothurn.

3762.q: What does a jackal's tail look like?
3762.e: The tail is covered in bushy fur. It helps jackals communicate with each other.

3763.q: Why can stag beetle larvae survive in wood for so long?
a: The rotten wood is their food and their hiding place
They sleep in water every night
3763.e: In the ground they are protected and always find food. They grow slowly because their food is low in nutrients.
3763.m: Wood is food and hiding place at once.

3764.q: Which way of walking do camels use, moving both legs on one side of the body at the same time?
3764.e: Camels pace, which means they move both legs on one side together. This gives them their typical rocking walk.
3764.m: Camels walk with a pacing gait.

3765.q: What are the especially long, pointed teeth of a lion called?
3765.e: The long, pointed teeth in a lion's mouth are called canines. The lion uses them to bite firmly into its prey.
3765.m: Canines are the long lion teeth.

3766.q: What do you measure when you take someone's blood pressure?
a: How strongly the blood pushes against the walls of the vessels
How much oxygen is in the blood
3766.e: Blood pressure shows how strongly the blood pushes against the walls of the arteries. It is given as two numbers, for example 120 over 80.
3766.m: Blood pressure is the pressure of the blood in the vessels.

3767.q: About how far can a chamois jump in one leap?
3767.e: As well as jumping high, chamois can also make long leaps of up to six metres. This helps them get across gorges or cracks in the rock.
3767.m: Chamois can jump up to six metres.

3768.q: How does a great tit defend its territory against other great tits?
a: It doesn't, it always shares everything
3768.e: Male great tits sing loudly to mark their territory. When there are intruders, they also make threatening gestures such as raising their feathers.
3768.m: Song protects the great tit's territory.

3769.q: How do ibex usually live outside the mating season?
a: Males and females form separate herds
All the animals live together in one herd all year
Each animal lives completely on its own
They live in pairs like birds
3769.e: Outside the mating season the males usually stay in all-male herds, while the females form their own groups with their young. Only in the rutting season in winter do the two groups meet.
3769.m: Males and females usually live apart.

3770.q: Which people kept alpacas many hundreds of years ago?
3770.e: In the Andes, the Inca and earlier peoples already kept alpacas for their wool. The animal was very valuable to them.

3771.q: Which body position does a gorilla only rarely hold for long?
3771.e: Gorillas can stand upright for a short time, for example when beating their chest. But most of the time they move on all fours.

3772.q: How many hearts does an earthworm have?
3772.e: An earthworm does not have just one heart like us, but five pairs of small hearts. They pump the blood through its long body.

3774.q: What do ants do when part of their nest is destroyed?
a: They all fly away at once
3774.e: Ants work together as a team. If their nest is damaged, many workers repair it together.

3775.q: When is the mating season for Bactrian camels?
3775.e: The rut takes place in winter. The males are especially excitable then.

a: Areas of the Earth with a similar, typical climate
Areas at the same height above sea level
3776.e: The Earth is roughly divided into tropical, temperate and polar climate zones. They differ mainly in temperature and precipitation.
3776.m: Climate zones show the typical weather conditions of a region.

3777.q: Which animal has a hard shell and moves very slowly?
3777.e: The tortoise always carries its shell with it for protection. Some species can live for more than a hundred years.
3777.m: The tortoise carries its house with it.

3778.q: Which small invertebrates are also part of the red kite's diet?
3778.e: As well as small mammals and carrion, the red kite also eats earthworms, which it finds, for example, on freshly ploughed fields. This shows how varied its diet is.
3778.m: Earthworms are on the menu too.

3780.q: About how old can wild carrion crows get?
3780.e: In the wild, carrion crows usually reach an age of about 10 to 15 years. In human care they can live much longer.
3780.m: Carrion crows often live over ten years.

3781.q: Apart from its nose, what else does a hippo close when it dives?
3781.e: When diving, the hippo also folds its ears tightly shut so that no water gets in. Its body is well made for diving.

3782.q: Where does the water louse live?
a: Under tree bark in the forest
In the sea on coral reefs
3782.e: The water louse lives in still and slow-flowing water. It feeds on leaves and plant remains.
3782.m: The water louse lives in fresh water.

3783.q: Is the great spotted woodpecker a migratory bird?
a: No, it usually stays here all year
Yes, it flies to Africa in winter
Yes, it flies to America every winter
No, it only flies away in summer
3783.e: The great spotted woodpecker usually stays in its territory all year. So it does not have to make a long journey.

3784.q: What is it called when dolphins swim along in the waves in front of boats?
3784.e: Dolphins like to swim right in front of boats in the bow wave. This is called bow riding and they clearly enjoy it.
3784.m: Dolphins like riding the bow wave.

3785.q: What helps the giraffe eat thorny acacia branches?
3785.e: Thick, sticky saliva coats the thorns when swallowing so that they do not hurt the giraffe's throat. Its flexible lips also help it pick the leaves skilfully.

3786.q: How are young slow worms born?
a: Alive, the eggs develop inside the mother
They split off from the mother
3786.e: In slow worms the eggs stay inside the mother's body. The young hatch from the thin egg membrane shortly before or during birth.
3786.m: Slow worms give birth to live young.

3787.q: How many eggs does a female raven usually lay in a clutch?
3787.e: A raven's clutch usually has three to six eggs. The exact number depends, among other things, on how much food there is.

3789.q: What is the whole change from egg to maggot and pupa to fly called?
3789.e: This process is called complete metamorphosis. Many insects go through these four stages.

3790.q: What happens to things a kingfisher cannot digest, such as fish bones, in its stomach?
a: It coughs them up again as a pellet
It only gets rid of them as droppings
It collects them as material for its nest
3790.e: The kingfisher cannot digest fish bones and scales and coughs them up again as small pellets. Owls do this too.
3790.m: Fish bones are coughed up as pellets.

3791.q: How can you often recognise a male European pond turtle?
a: The lower shell curves slightly inwards
The shell is much bigger than the female's
It always has a red shell
3791.e: The curve helps the males when mating. Males also have a longer, thicker tail.
3791.m: Males have an inward-curving lower shell.

3792.q: What colour is the tip of the tail of many African wild dogs?
3792.e: The white tail tip works like a signal. It helps the animals keep each other in sight when hunting in tall grass.
3792.m: The white tail tip helps them find their way.

3794.q: About how tall can an adult chimpanzee get?
a: About as tall as a person
3794.e: An adult chimpanzee grows to about one to one and a half metres tall. That makes it roughly as tall as a smaller person.
3794.m: Chimpanzees are about the size of a person.

3795.q: What is it called when a cockerel calls out its loud “cock-a-doodle-doo”?
3795.e: The cockerel's typical call is called crowing. It is much louder than the quiet clucking of the hens.
3795.m: A cockerel crows rather than chirps.

3796.q: How well can a wood mouse smell and hear?
a: Very well, which helps it look for food
It cannot smell anything at all
It smells less well than a person
3796.e: The wood mouse has a very good sense of smell and hearing. This means it finds food even in the dark and notices danger in time.
3796.m: A good sense of smell and good hearing.

3797.q: Can beech martens pull in their claws like a cat?
a: No, the claws are always visible
3797.e: Unlike cats, beech martens cannot pull in their claws. The claws help them climb and dig.
3797.m: A beech marten's claws always stay out.

3798.q: The scientific name of the swift means “without feet”. Why does it fit?
a: Because it hardly uses its short feet
Because it has no legs at all
Because it hides its feet in the water
3798.e: The name Apus comes from Greek and means “without feet”. The swift does have feet, but it almost never lands and only needs them for clinging on.

3800.q: At best, how old can a wild kestrel get?
3800.e: Most kestrels in the wild only live a few years, but some individuals can reach over 10 years. Many young birds do not survive their first year.

3801.q: Which horse breed originally comes from Switzerland?
3801.e: The Freiberger is the best-known horse breed in Switzerland. It originally comes from the Jura.
3801.m: The Freiberger is a Swiss horse.

3802.q: What does the shell of the European pond turtle typically look like?
a: Dark brown to black with yellow dots or lines
3802.e: The dark colour with the yellow pattern helps it stay camouflaged in the water. The pattern is a little different on every animal.
3802.m: A dark shell with yellow dots.

3803.q: What sometimes happens during the day when small birds discover a resting tawny owl?
a: They swarm around it and scold it loudly; this is called mobbing
They all fly away at once
3803.e: Small birds such as tits or blackbirds often recognise the tawny owl as an enemy and circle it noisily to drive it away. This behaviour is called mobbing and helps birdwatchers find tawny owls.
3803.m: Small birds mob resting tawny owls.

a: Supplying West Berlin by aeroplane during a Soviet blockade
A bridge that linked East and West Berlin
3804.e: When the Soviet Union blocked the land routes to West Berlin, the Western powers supplied the city from the air for almost a year. This meant West Berlin could be held.
3804.m: The Airlift supplied West Berlin from the air.

3805.q: What were great crested grebes hunted heavily for in the 19th century?
a: For their feathers, which were put on hats
For their meat as a delicacy
3805.e: At that time the silky feathers were used by the fashion industry to decorate hats. This led to a sharp fall in many populations.
3805.m: Feather fashion put the great crested grebe in danger.

3806.q: How good is a golden eagle's eyesight compared with a person's?
a: Several times better than a person's
About as good as a person's
The golden eagle can hardly see anything
3806.e: Golden eagles have excellent eyesight and can spot prey from a great distance. Their eyes are many times sharper than human eyes.
3806.m: Golden eagles see much more sharply than people.

a: Never in the middle of the night
3807.e: Kangaroos are most active at dawn and dusk, so early in the morning and in the evening. During the day they often rest in the shade.
3807.m: Kangaroos are active in the morning and evening.

3808.q: In which country is Kruger National Park, where wild dogs live?
3808.e: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park in South Africa. It is one of the best-known protected areas in Africa.
3808.m: Wild dogs live in Kruger National Park.

3809.q: Why did the beaver disappear from Switzerland in the 19th century?
a: A disease killed all the beavers
3809.e: People hunted the beaver for its fur, its meat and a scented substance that was used as medicine. That is why it disappeared completely from Switzerland.
3809.m: Hunting once wiped out the beaver.

3810.q: How often does a female adder usually have young?
3810.e: Carrying young takes a lot of energy. That is why many females take a year off.
3810.m: Females need time to recover between litters.

3811.q: What do young birds in the nest do when there is little food in bad weather?
a: They lower their body temperature to save energy
They leave the nest at once
They eat plants instead of insects
They call loudly for their parents all day
3811.e: When food is short, young swifts can fall into a kind of cold stiffness. This way they use less energy and get through bad days.
3811.m: Young birds save energy when hungry.

3812.q: Which feature makes fire salamanders different from lizards?
a: Fire salamanders have moist skin without scales
Fire salamanders have scales like lizards
Fire salamanders have a snail shell
3812.e: Unlike lizards, which have dry, scaly skin, the fire salamander's skin is smooth and moist. This helps it breathe through its skin.
3812.m: Its skin is moist instead of scaly.

3813.q: How many toes does a wild boar have on each foot?
3813.e: Wild boar have four toes on each foot. They leave typical tracks in soft ground.
3813.m: A wild boar has four toes per foot.

3816.q: What is typical of the bearded vulture's call?
a: It is rather quiet and rarely heard
It caws extremely loudly like a crow
3816.e: Unlike many other birds, the bearded vulture is quite silent and only calls rarely. That is why you usually recognise it by its looks and not by its sound.

3818.q: Which kind of duck is especially common in Switzerland?
3818.e: The mallard is the most common wild duck in Switzerland. You find it at almost every lake and river.
3818.m: The mallard is the most common duck.

3819.q: Which animal has a very good memory and a long trunk?
3819.e: The elephant is the largest land animal on Earth and is considered very clever. With its trunk it can grab, drink and smell.
3819.m: The elephant has a trunk and a good memory.

3820.q: In which season do you most often hear the loud chorus of tree frogs?
a: In spring, during the mating season
3820.e: During the mating season in spring, many males call at the same time at ponds. This loud chorus is typical of this season.
3820.m: The tree frog chorus rings out in spring.

3821.q: What should you think about before getting a goldfish as a pet?
a: Whether you have enough space, time and knowledge to look after it
Whether you can give it a name like a dog
3821.e: Before keeping goldfish, you should know how much space and care they need. A tank that is too small makes the animals ill.

3822.q: How does a centipede often move compared with a millipede?
a: Not at all, it stays stuck
3822.e: As hunters, centipedes have to catch their prey. Many species, such as the stone centipede, run very quickly.

3824.q: How endangered is the African elephant today, according to conservationists?
a: It is not endangered at all
There are far too many of them
3824.e: Because of poaching and the loss of its habitat, the African elephant is considered an endangered species. Conservation organisations therefore work to protect it.
3824.m: The elephant is considered endangered today.

3825.q: What colour is cows' hair usually?
a: There are many colours such as brown, black or white
3825.e: Cows can have very different coat colours depending on the breed. Some are one colour, others are spotted.
3825.m: Cow coats come in many different colours.

3826.q: How many eggs does a female sparrow usually lay at once?
3826.e: A female sparrow usually lays four to six small eggs in her nest. After about two weeks the chicks hatch from them.
3826.m: A sparrow lays about five eggs.

3827.e: UNESCO is a UN organisation that protects schools, research and important cultural sites. For example, it draws up the World Heritage List.
3827.m: UNESCO protects education, science and culture.

3828.q: About how often should you change the water in a goldfish tank?
a: Regularly, for example part of it every week
Only when the fish is ill
3828.e: To keep the water clean, you should regularly change part of it. This stops harmful substances staying in the water for too long.
3828.m: Changing the water regularly keeps fish healthy.

3829.q: How long do kingfisher parents sit on their eggs?
3829.e: The incubation lasts about 19 to 21 days. The male and female take turns sitting on the eggs.

3830.q: How does the mallard behave in towns compared with other wild ducks?
a: It adapts very well to life in towns
It dies straight away near people
3830.e: The mallard copes better with people and towns than many other wild ducks. That is why you see it so often in parks and on town ponds.

3831.q: Which three parts is the body of an earwig divided into?
3831.e: Like all insects, the earwig is made up of head, thorax and abdomen. The legs and wings are attached to the thorax.
3831.m: An insect's body consists of head, thorax and abdomen.

3833.q: Can a mole also walk backwards through its tunnels?
a: Yes, it is very good at it
No, it cannot do that at all
Only with help from other animals
3833.e: Thanks to its smooth fur and its sensitive tail, the mole can easily walk backwards through narrow tunnels. This is handy when it cannot turn round.
3833.m: Moles are good at walking backwards.

3835.q: Why do some polar bears move further north in summer?
a: To stay near the ice and find seals
To lie in the warmth there
3835.e: In summer the ice melts first in areas further south. That is why some polar bears move north, where there is still ice.
3835.m: Polar bears follow the ice north.

3836.q: What do common toad tadpoles often do in the water?
a: They swim in large dark swarms
3836.e: Common toad tadpoles often stay together in large groups and swim as a dark swarm. This also makes them a bit safer from enemies.
3836.m: Tadpoles like to swim in swarms.

3837.q: What happens to the body temperature of the edible dormouse during hibernation?
a: It changes a lot every minute
3837.e: During hibernation the edible dormouse's body temperature drops almost to the temperature around it. This saves a huge amount of energy.
3837.m: Body temperature drops sharply in hibernation.

3838.q: Roughly how big is the territory of a pair of bearded vultures?
3838.e: A pair of bearded vultures needs a very large area in the mountains as its habitat. There they look for enough food for themselves and their young.

3839.q: How do budgies in a flock communicate with each other?
3839.e: Budgies call and chirp a lot to stay in contact with each other. This keeps the flock together.

3840.q: Which animal is known for being slow and carries its shell on its back like a house?
3840.e: The tortoise always carries its hard shell with it like a house. When in danger, it can hide its head and legs completely inside.
3840.m: The tortoise carries its house with it.

3841.q: Which subspecies of brown bear is known for being especially large and lives on an island in Alaska?
3841.e: The Kodiak bear lives on the Kodiak Islands off Alaska and is one of the largest land predators in the world. It is a subspecies of the brown bear.
3841.m: The Kodiak bear is the largest brown bear.

3842.q: How does the garden spider catch its prey?
a: It wraps it in silk threads
It immediately gives it a deadly bite
It eats it whole straight away
3842.e: When an insect gets caught in the web, the spider runs over and wraps it in threads. Then it can no longer escape.
3842.m: It wraps its prey up tightly.

3843.q: What is the rearmost section of an insect's body called?
3843.e: Insect bodies have three parts: head, thorax and abdomen. You can see this well in the stag beetle.
3843.m: Insects have a head, thorax and abdomen.

3844.q: How do meerkats behave towards other groups in their territory?
a: They defend their territory, sometimes by fighting
3844.e: Meerkats defend their area against other groups. This can lead to fierce clashes.

3845.q: What does the pond skater mainly use its back legs for?
3845.e: The back legs steer the pond skater like a rudder. This lets it change direction.
3845.m: Back legs steer like a rudder.

3846.q: At what time of day is the common wall lizard mainly active?
a: During the day, especially when the sun shines
Round the clock without a break
3846.e: As a cold-blooded animal, the wall lizard needs the warmth of the sun to become active. That is why it is active during the day.

3847.q: How many earthworms can live in good meadow soil in a patch as big as a bath towel?
3847.e: Very many earthworms live in good meadow soil. In such a small patch there can be over a hundred, sometimes even several hundred.
3847.m: Many worms live in good soil.

3848.q: What sound does a wild boar often make?
3848.e: Wild boar often communicate with grunting sounds. This way they stay in contact within the group.

3849.q: What are the feet of the great tit, which it uses to hold on to branches, like?
3849.e: The great tit has feet with four toes, three pointing forwards and one backwards. With them it can hold on to branches very well.
3849.m: Four toes help it hold on to branches.

3850.q: How does a gorilla mother carry her little baby at first?
a: In a nest in the water
3850.e: In the first months the baby gorilla clings to its mother's belly. Later it climbs onto her back.

3851.q: What is the okapi often also called because of its appearance?
3851.e: The name forest giraffe fits because the okapi lives in the forest and is related to the giraffe. But it is not a zebra.
3851.m: The okapi is also called the forest giraffe.

3852.q: How often do wolves really attack people?
a: Very rarely, wolves usually avoid people
Almost every day in every forest
Always, as soon as they see a person
Only at night, but then very often
3852.e: Wolves are naturally rather shy and avoid contact with people. Attacks on people are extremely rare and hardly ever happen.
3852.m: Wolves only very rarely attack people.

3853.q: What can one toe on a barn owl's foot do that is special?
a: It can point forwards or backwards
It has no claw at all
It is twice as long as the others
3853.e: The barn owl has a reversible toe that can be turned forwards or backwards. This lets it grip and hold prey especially well.
3853.m: A movable toe helps with gripping.

3854.q: How do mute swan parents behave towards their cygnets in the first weeks?
a: They protect them and lead them everywhere
They leave them alone in the nest
They take them to other birds
3854.e: The parents stay very close to their cygnets and lead them to good feeding places. This way the young quickly learn how to survive.
3854.m: Parents go everywhere with their cygnets.

3855.q: What do llamas have at the top front of their mouth instead of incisors?
a: Nothing, just gums with no purpose
3855.e: Like cattle, llamas have a hard pad at the top front. They press grass against it with their lower incisors and pull it off.
3855.m: Llamas have a dental pad at the top front.

3856.q: What do the humps of a Bactrian camel mainly store?
3856.e: The humps contain fatty tissue that serves as an energy reserve. Water is not stored in the hump.

3857.q: How good is a brown bear's sense of smell?
a: Very good, much better than a person's
Brown bears cannot smell at all
Only as good as a fish's
3857.e: Brown bears have an excellent sense of smell and can scent food over long distances. This sense is their most important tool when looking for food.
3857.m: Brown bears have a particularly good sense of smell.

3858.q: Which habitat does the European pond turtle like best?
a: Still or slow-flowing water with a muddy bottom
3858.e: There it finds food and hiding places in the mud. Sunny spots on the bank are also important.
3858.m: Calm water with mud is ideal.

3859.q: What does it mean when a proposal in a vote is ‘thrown out’?
3859.e: If more people say No than Yes, a proposal is thrown out, that is, rejected. Then everything stays as it was.

3860.q: What colour is a grasshopper often?
3860.e: The colours help it hide in the grass. This makes it harder for enemies to see it.
3860.m: Its colour camouflages it in the grass.

3862.q: How does a red fox usually behave towards people in the wild?
a: It is usually very shy and careful
It always runs straight towards people
It attacks people all the time
It begs to be stroked like a dog
3862.e: In the wild the red fox is usually very shy and prefers to keep out of people's way. In towns, though, some foxes have become bolder.

3863.q: What role does an experienced lead nanny goat often have in the herd?
a: She leads the herd and the others follow her
She is always the only one asleep
She never eats with the others
3863.e: An experienced, often older female goat frequently leads the herd. The other goats follow her lead, for example when it comes to which way to go.
3863.m: The lead goat leads the herd.

3864.q: What does a trout live on in the first days after hatching?
a: A small yolk sac on its belly
3864.e: Newly hatched trout carry a small sac of food on their belly. They live off it until they can feed themselves.
