3864.m: Young trout have a yolk sac on their belly.

3865.q: What does a male common wall lizard often do to defend its territory?
a: It shows itself off and drives rivals away
It leaves its territory at once
It sings loudly like a bird
3865.e: Males show their strength by nodding their heads and behaving in a showy way. This drives other males out of their territory.
3865.m: Territories are defended in a showy way.

3866.q: Where does the name “ladybird” probably come from?
a: From the Virgin Mary, “Our Lady”, in the Christian religion
From a girl called Lady who discovered the beetle
3866.e: In the past people believed the helpful little beetle was a gift from the Virgin Mary to farmers. That is probably where its name comes from.
3866.m: The name recalls the Virgin Mary.

3867.q: Where in the Congo is the range of the bonobo?
a: On the peaks of the Virunga Mountains
3867.e: The bonobo's range is in the Congo Basin, south of the great Congo River. There the river acts as a natural border.
3867.m: Bonobos live south of the Congo River.

3868.q: What is a jellyfish's stinging poison mainly for?
a: To stun prey and defend itself
3868.e: The stinging poison helps the jellyfish paralyse small prey. It also protects it from enemies that want to eat it.
3868.m: Stinging poison is for hunting and protection.

3869.q: What is the badger's body shape like?
a: Long thin legs like a deer
A very slim body like a weasel
3869.e: The badger has a stocky body and short but strong legs. This helps it dig.
3869.m: Badgers are stocky with short legs.

3870.q: Why do guinea pigs need fresh vegetables with vitamin C?
a: Because their bodies cannot make vitamin C themselves
Because otherwise they get too light
Because without vegetables they cannot squeak
3870.e: Unlike many other animals, guinea pigs cannot make their own vitamin C. That is why they have to get it every day from fresh vegetables.
3870.m: Guinea pigs need vitamin C in their food.

3871.q: How is the lynx's way of hunting different from a wolf pack's?
a: The lynx hunts alone by ambush, wolves often hunt in packs
The lynx always hunts in large groups
Both always hunt in exactly the same way
3871.e: While wolves often chase prey together as a pack, the lynx relies on creeping up silently and making a quick surprise attack on its own.

3872.q: What is special about every gorilla's nose?
a: The nose wrinkles are unique to each gorilla
All gorilla noses look exactly the same
The nose changes colour every year
Gorillas have no nose at all
3872.e: Just like a person's fingerprint, the pattern of nose wrinkles is different in every gorilla. This lets researchers recognise individual animals.

3873.q: What is special about the koala's ears?
a: They are round, fluffy and very hairy
They are very pointed like a fox's
They are tiny and almost invisible
3873.e: The koala's ears are round, covered in soft hair and stick out a little from its head. They give it a friendly, cuddly look.
3873.m: Koala ears are round and fluffy.

3874.q: What happens if you always spend all your pocket money straight away?
a: You have nothing left when you need something later
You automatically get more pocket money
Nothing, that is always a good idea
3874.e: If you spend everything at once, you have no money left for later wishes or emergencies. It is worth putting something aside.
3874.m: If you spend everything, nothing is left.

3875.q: What are the tiny newly hatched octopuses that drift in the water called?
3875.e: Newly hatched octopuses are tiny larvae that first float freely in the water. Later they sink to the seabed and keep growing.

3876.q: What do an octopus's arms have on their underside?
3876.e: An octopus has lots of suckers on its arms. With them it can hold on, feel and even taste.

3877.q: Which temperatures does the fire salamander prefer?
a: Cool, mild temperatures without great heat
3877.e: The fire salamander likes it cool and damp; it does not cope well with great heat and dryness. That is why it usually lives in shady forests.
3877.m: It likes cool and damp best.

3878.q: What is the International Space Station (ISS)?
a: A crewed research laboratory in orbit around the Earth
An uncrewed satellite for watching the weather
A space probe on its way to Mars
3878.e: The ISS orbits the Earth at about 400 kilometres up and is permanently occupied by international teams of astronauts. Many scientific experiments in weightlessness are carried out there.
3878.m: The ISS is a crewed laboratory in space.

3879.q: Which habitats does the kingfisher prefer?
a: Dense conifer forests with no water
3879.e: The kingfisher lives by streams, rivers and ponds with clear, calmly flowing water. There it finds enough fish and suitable perches.

3880.q: Who normally makes sure a dog gets enough to eat and drink?
a: Nobody, the dog sees to it itself
3880.e: A dog cannot go shopping by itself, so its owner has to provide food and water. That is part of a dog owner's responsibility.
3880.m: The owner takes care of the food.

3881.q: How do European pond turtles survive the winter with little oxygen in the water?
a: They slow their metabolism right down
They eat a lot all winter
3881.e: In their winter rest they need hardly any energy or oxygen. This lets them stay on the bottom of the water for many weeks.
3881.m: In winter their energy needs drop sharply.

3882.q: What do you need your muscles for?
3882.e: Muscles tighten and in this way move your bones. Without them you could neither walk nor grab things.

3883.q: What are the underground tunnel systems that marmots live in called?
3883.e: Marmots use their strong front paws to dig branching burrows in the ground. These are made up of several tunnels and chambers.

3884.q: When is the otter mainly active?
3884.e: Otters are mostly active at dusk and at night. During the day they rest hidden in their den.
3884.m: Otters are mainly active at night.

3885.q: What does a little kangaroo drink in its mother's pouch?
3885.e: In the pouch the baby drinks milk from its mother. This milk makes it big and strong.
3885.m: Baby kangaroos drink their mother's milk.

3886.q: Roughly how long does it take for tiger cubs to be born once the mother is expecting?
3886.e: A tigress carries her young in her belly for about three months before they are born. This is called the gestation period.
3886.m: Tiger cubs develop for about 3 months.

3887.q: How many legs does a grasshopper have?
3887.e: The grasshopper is an insect. All insects have six legs.

3888.q: Why is hunting and trading young gibbons a problem?
a: Mothers are often killed to get the young
Gibbons may only be caught in winter
3888.e: For the illegal pet trade, the mothers are often killed. This badly harms the populations, because gibbons only have young slowly.
3888.m: Wild animals do not belong in living rooms.

3889.q: What is the most popular pet in Switzerland?
3889.e: More cats live in Switzerland than any other pet. Many families have one or more cats at home.
3889.m: The cat is Switzerland's most popular pet.

3890.q: How does the Bactrian camel's coat change during the year?
a: In spring it sheds its thick winter coat in tufts
It changes from brown to white
It falls out completely in autumn
3890.e: In winter a thick, long coat grows. In spring it is shed in large tufts.
3890.m: In spring it loses its winter coat.

3891.q: What does a gorilla use to grind up its plant food?
3891.e: Gorillas have large, flat back teeth. With them they can chew tough leaves and stems well.
3891.m: Broad teeth help with chewing plants.

3892.q: Which disease, which can also affect pet dogs, is dangerous for wild dogs?
3892.e: Diseases such as rabies and distemper can be passed from pet dogs to wild dogs. This can threaten whole packs.
3892.m: Pet dogs can pass diseases on to wild dogs.

3893.q: How do hyenas often move when hunting?
a: With great stamina over long distances
Only by leaping from tree to tree
3893.e: Hyenas can run long distances and wear out their prey. This makes them hunters with great stamina.

3894.q: How many blowholes does a blue whale have?
3894.e: Baleen whales such as the blue whale have two blowholes on their head. Toothed whales, on the other hand, have only one.

3895.q: How does a mute swan show that it is angry or in danger?
a: It lies flat on the water
3895.e: Raised wings make the swan look bigger and more threatening. It is a warning signal to other animals.

3896.q: What special food does the queen bee get?
3896.e: Royal jelly is a special food made by the worker bees. The queen gets it all her life, which is why she grows big and can lay eggs.

3897.q: In the European praying mantis, which sex is usually bigger and stronger?
3897.e: Females are usually more heavily built than males. They need strength and room for the eggs.

3898.q: Which animals are among the badger's favourite food?
3898.e: Earthworms are among the badger's favourite foods and make up a large part of its diet. It also eats insects, fruit and small vertebrates.

3899.q: How is the Tatra chamois from the High Tatras doing today?
a: It is rare and strictly protected
It is very common and hunted a lot
It now only lives in zoos
3899.e: A separate subspecies of chamois lives in the High Tatras in Slovakia and Poland. It is very rare and strictly protected.
3899.m: The Tatra chamois is rare and protected.

3900.q: Where do pond skaters often lay their eggs?
a: On plants in or by the water
3900.e: The females often stick the eggs to water plants or other bits of plants. The larvae then hatch right by the water.

3901.q: The scientific name of the chamois, Rupicapra, means roughly “rock goat”. Why does it fit?
a: It climbs on rocks and is related to goats
It lives in caves under rocks
It is as hard as a rock
3901.e: The chamois is a skilful climber on rocks and belongs to the goat family. That is why the name rock goat fits well.

3902.q: What is special about an orangutan's arms?
a: They are very long and reach down to the ankles
They are shorter than the legs
3902.e: The arm span can be over two metres. With their long arms they swing through the trees.

3903.q: What does a young kingfisher have to do shortly after leaving the nest hole?
a: It has to learn to catch fish on its own
It goes straight back to its mother in the nest
It stays with its parents for a whole year
It can dive perfectly from the start without practising
3903.e: After leaving the nest, young kingfishers are only fed by their parents for a short time and then have to learn to hunt for themselves. At first they often fall into the water without catching a fish.
3903.m: The young must quickly learn to fish for themselves.

3904.q: What does a caterpillar become after it has turned into a pupa?
3904.e: In the end a finished butterfly hatches from the pupa. This is called metamorphosis.
3904.m: The pupa turns into a butterfly.

3905.q: What are the horns of the male minotaur beetle probably for?
3905.e: Males with horns wrestle over females and tunnels. Often the beetle with the bigger horns wins.

3906.q: Why does the sand lizard need a lot of sun?
a: Because it is cold-blooded and controls its body temperature using the sun
Because it is only active at night
Because it needs sunlight to breathe
3906.e: Reptiles cannot make their own body heat like we humans can. That is why they sunbathe to become active and agile.
3906.m: The sun keeps the lizard warm and agile.

3907.q: How can a housefly walk upside down on the ceiling?
a: With little sticky pads on its feet
With sharp claws on its head
3907.e: The housefly has tiny sticky pads with fine hairs on its feet. With them it can even hold on to smooth glass.
3907.m: Sticky pads help it walk on ceilings.

3908.q: How does a seahorse usually swim?
a: Upright, with its head at the top
3908.e: Unlike most fish, the seahorse swims upright in the water. This makes it look almost as if it is standing.
3908.m: Seahorses swim upright in the water.

3909.q: Where does the hippo spend most of the day?
3909.e: During the day hippos mostly stay in the water to protect themselves from the hot sun. Only at night do they come onto land to eat.
3909.m: Hippos rest in the water during the day.

3910.q: What helps a chick break the hard eggshell from the inside?
a: A small cut made by its mother
3910.e: Chicks have a tiny hard bump on their beak, the egg tooth. With it they peck their way out of the shell from the inside.
3910.m: The egg tooth opens the eggshell.

3911.q: What job does the lateral line have in a salmon?
a: It senses movements in the water
3911.e: The lateral line organ senses currents and changes in pressure. This helps the fish find its way in the water.
3911.m: The lateral line senses water movements.

3912.q: About how old can pandas get in the wild?
3912.e: Wild pandas often live to around 20. In zoos they can live even longer.

a: A paper that shows you are allowed to vote
3913.e: The voting card arrives at home by post. You need it to take part in a vote.
3913.m: The voting card shows that you are allowed to vote.

3914.q: How long do young lake trout usually stay in the stream before they move to the lake?
a: They stay there all their lives
3914.e: The young fish first grow up in the stream. After one to three years they move down into the lake.
3914.m: Young fish grow up in the stream first.

3915.q: What sound does a little lion cub make when it is hungry?
a: It roars like an adult lion
3915.e: Little lion cubs cannot roar loudly yet. They make quiet mewing sounds instead, a bit like kittens.
3915.m: Lion cubs mew instead of roaring.

3916.q: How do you calculate the electrical power of an appliance?
a: Power is voltage divided by resistance
3916.e: The formula P = U x I tells you how much electrical energy is converted per unit of time. Power is given in watts.

3917.q: Roughly how many millions of years have sharks existed on Earth?
3917.e: Sharks are among the oldest animals in the world. They have hardly changed since ancient times.
3917.m: Sharks have existed for over 400 million years.

3918.q: Why is the African buffalo important for nature conservation and tourism?
a: It is one of the Big Five and attracts visitors
3918.e: Safaris where you can watch buffalo are popular. This brings money into protecting national parks.

3919.q: How does a bat find its way in the dark?
a: With its eyes like an owl
3919.e: The bat makes high sounds that we cannot hear. From the echo it can tell where obstacles or prey are.
3919.m: Bats hear their way in the dark.

3920.q: What is the barn owl especially good at?
a: Hearing where a mouse is in the dark
3920.e: The barn owl has very good hearing. It finds mice even in complete darkness just by the sound.

3921.q: What is it called when swifts fly round houses in groups in summer, screaming loudly?
3921.e: On warm summer evenings swifts often race around buildings in loud, screaming groups. This behaviour is called a screaming party.
3921.m: Screaming groups are called screaming parties.

3922.q: Why were whitefish doing worse in many lakes in the 1960s and 1970s?
a: Too many nutrients led to a lack of oxygen in the depths
The water had become too cold
The lakes had become too deep
3922.e: Waste water brought a lot of phosphorus into the lakes. Algae grew strongly, and when they broke down there was not enough oxygen at the bottom.

3923.q: What kind of nesting place does a female beech marten prefer for giving birth to her young?
3923.e: For the birth, the female looks for a dry, quiet and well-hidden place, for example a loft or a pile of stones. There the young are protected from the weather and enemies.
3923.m: Dry nooks are used for giving birth.

3924.q: What happens when a robin sees its reflection in a window?
a: It thinks it is a strange robin
It doesn't notice it at all
3924.e: Robins defend their territory and think their reflection is a strange bird. Then they sometimes even attack it.

3925.q: What does the kestrel do when it dives at a mouse just before grabbing it?
a: It drops steeply from hovering or from its perch
It stays still in the air for ever
It flies off in the opposite direction
3925.e: Once the kestrel has spotted prey, it dives straight down at it from hovering or from a perch. At the last moment it grabs it with its claws.
3925.m: When attacking, the kestrel dives steeply.

3926.q: Which country is one of the biggest producers of farmed salmon?
3926.e: Norway has many fjords with cold, clean water. Many salmon farms are found there.
3926.m: Norway farms a lot of salmon.

3927.q: Which animal can be seen on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden?
3927.e: The coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows a black bear on a white background. The bear comes from the Abbey of St Gallen, which Appenzell used to belong to.
3927.m: Appenzell Innerrhoden has a bear on its coat of arms.

3928.q: Which plant is often used as bait to draw aphids away from crops?
3928.e: Aphids like to settle on nasturtiums, so they can draw them away from other plants. That is why nasturtiums are often planted as trap plants.
3928.m: Nasturtiums lure aphids away from vegetables.

3929.q: What is the underground tunnel system of wild rabbits called?
3929.e: A rabbit warren is made up of many tunnels and chambers under the ground. Several rabbits often live in it together.
3929.m: The warren is their underground home.

3930.q: What do you call a large gathering of carrion crows in one place?
3930.e: When lots of carrion crows come together, it is called a flock. Such flocks form mainly outside the breeding season at shared roosting places.
3930.m: Many crows together form a flock.

3931.q: What does a kestrel's head do while it is hovering?
a: It stays completely still in the air while the wings beat
It keeps turning in a circle
It moves in time with the wings
It always looks up at the sky
3931.e: While hovering, the kestrel holds its head amazingly still, even though its body sways slightly with the wingbeats. This lets it keep a sharp eye on the ground.
3931.m: The head stays completely still when hovering.

3932.q: Which statement about the size of the wolverine compared with other martens is true?
a: It is much bigger and heavier than most other kinds of marten
It is smaller than the weasel
It is about the size of a mouse
It is exactly as heavy as a stoat
3932.e: The wolverine stands out for its strong build and is much bigger and heavier than slender relatives such as the stoat or the weasel. This means it can also deal with larger prey.
3932.m: The wolverine is a real giant among martens.

3933.q: How do ring-tailed lemurs often hold their tails when the group is on the move?
a: Straight up, like a question mark
Always dragging flat along the ground
3933.e: The raised tail can be seen from far away. This way members of the group keep an eye on each other.
3933.m: The raised tail keeps the group together.

3934.q: Why are lichens so important for reindeer in winter?
a: They provide energy when there is hardly any other food
They contain a lot of fat like nuts
They are always juicy and sweet
3934.e: In winter lichens are often the reindeer's most important food. They provide plenty of energy but little protein.

3935.q: What do wild boar find in the ground with their fine noses?
a: Birds' eggs high up in the trees
3935.e: With their very fine noses, wild boar can even sniff out food under the ground. This is how they find roots and mushrooms.
3935.m: The fine nose finds food in the ground.

3936.q: What sound does a harbour seal often make?
3936.e: Harbour seals make barking and growling sounds, especially when they feel threatened. These sounds can sometimes be a bit like a dog's.

3938.q: Roughly how long can African buffalo live in the wild?
3938.e: Their age depends on enemies, diseases and food. In human care they often live a little longer.

3939.q: Who rules communist North Korea today?
a: A president elected by the people
3939.e: Kim Jong-un is the ruler of North Korea. His family has already ruled the country for three generations.

3940.q: Which habitat does the reindeer mainly live in?
3940.e: Reindeer live in the tundra and the taiga of the far north. There it is cold and snowy for a long time.
3940.m: Reindeer live in the cold north.

3941.q: When is the beech marten mainly active?
a: Only in broad daylight at midday
Only during the day in winter
3941.e: Beech martens are nocturnal animals and are hardly ever seen during the day. They usually start hunting at dusk.
3941.m: The beech marten hunts at night.

3942.q: Which way does a brown trout usually face in a stream?
a: With its head against the current
With its head in the direction of the current
3942.e: This way fresh water reaches its gills and food drifts straight towards it. With a few flicks of its fins it stays in place.

3943.q: In which habitat do ring-tailed lemurs feel especially at home?
a: In dry forests and rocky areas
High in the mountains above the snow
In marshes near the Arctic Circle
3943.e: Ring-tailed lemurs live in the warm, often dry south of Madagascar. There they climb trees and rocks.
3943.m: Ring-tailed lemurs like dry forest and rocks.

3944.q: What are Swiss cantons allowed to do in foreign policy?
a: Make their own agreements with neighbouring regions abroad in certain areas
Decide on war and peace on their own
Take foreign policy away from the Confederation completely
3944.e: Border cantons may, for example, make agreements on cooperation with neighbouring regions in France, Germany or Italy. But major foreign policy remains a matter for the Confederation.
3944.m: Cantons may work across borders to a limited extent.

3945.q: Why was the golden eagle hunted so much in the past?
a: People wrongly thought it was a big danger to farm animals
Because its meat was considered a special delicacy
Because its feathers were used as money
3945.e: In the past people believed golden eagles often attacked sheep or even small children, which almost never happened. Out of fear, the birds were hunted for a long time.
3945.m: Lack of knowledge led to heavy persecution.

3946.q: What kind of water does the orca live in?
a: In the sea, in salt water
3946.e: The orca lives in the sea. There it finds enough space and food.
3946.m: Orcas live in the salty sea.

3947.q: The picture shows a newly hatched trout with a sac on its belly. What is it for?
a: It is a yolk sac and provides food
3947.e: The yolk sac contains nutrients. The little fish lives on it for the first few weeks.
3947.m: The yolk sac feeds the young fish.

3948.q: What is a feature of the snow leopard's head?
3948.e: Small ears lose less heat. This is an adaptation to the cold.

3949.q: What colour is a tiger's fur usually?
3949.e: Tigers have orange fur with black stripes. The belly is often white.

3952.q: What is the dung for when a dung beetle takes it into the ground?
a: It serves as a food store for the larvae
It is used as building material for towers
It is meant to burn enemies
3952.e: The larva cannot look for food itself. That is why the female puts the dung in the brood chamber as provisions for it.
3952.m: Dung is food for the larvae.

3953.q: What does the coat of a long-haired guinea pig need regularly?
a: Brushing so that it does not get matted
3953.e: Breeds with very long hair, such as the Peruvian, need brushing regularly. Otherwise the coat quickly gets matted and the skin can even become inflamed.
3953.m: Long hair must be brushed regularly.

3954.q: Which kind of goose often lives on lakes here and was originally brought over from North America?
3954.e: The Canada goose originally comes from North America. It was brought to Europe a long time ago and now also lives in the wild here.
3954.m: The Canada goose came to us from North America.

3955.q: What makes the backswimmer different from the pond skater?
a: The backswimmer swims under the surface
The backswimmer walks across the water
3955.e: The backswimmer swims on its back under the surface of the water. The pond skater stays on top of the water.
3955.m: Pond skaters on top, backswimmers under water.

3956.q: How fast can a pike be when it snaps at prey?
a: Only as fast as a butterfly
3956.e: When the pike attacks, it shoots forward as fast as lightning. This surprises the prey so much that it has no chance to escape.
3956.m: The pike shoots off like lightning.

3957.q: Is the robin a protected bird in Switzerland?
a: No, it is a kind of pet
3957.e: Like most wild birds in Switzerland, the robin is protected. You may not catch it or harm it.

3958.q: What protection status does the fire salamander have in Switzerland?
a: It is not on any protection list
3958.e: The fire salamander is protected by law in Switzerland. It may not be caught, and its habitat may not be harmed.

3959.q: How do praying mantises mainly find their prey?
a: By smelling it from kilometres away
3959.e: Their eyesight is very good. They notice small movements and judge distances.
3959.m: Prey is mainly spotted by sight.

3960.q: Apart from keeping watch, what were geese kept on farms for in the past?
3960.e: As well as being loud guards, geese were mainly kept for their eggs and meat. Their feathers were also very much in demand.
3960.m: Geese provided eggs, meat and feathers.

3961.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of penguins in the water?
3961.e: In the water penguins have to watch out for predators such as the leopard seal and the orca. These hunters are much faster and bigger than penguins.
3961.m: Leopard seals hunt penguins in the water.

3962.q: What colour is a carrion crow's beak?
3962.e: The carrion crow's strong, straight beak is black. This matches the rest of its feathers, which are black all over.
3962.m: The carrion crow's beak is black.

3963.q: What does a goldfish tank need so that the fish get enough oxygen?
3963.e: A filter or an air pump makes sure enough oxygen gets into the water. Without enough oxygen the fish could suffocate.
3963.m: A filter brings oxygen into the water.

3964.q: What kind of teeth does a chimpanzee have that show it also eats meat?
3964.e: Chimpanzees have pointed canines that they can also use to eat meat. Even so, they mostly eat plants.
3964.m: Pointed canines show it eats everything.

3965.q: How old can ring-tailed lemurs get in human care?
3965.e: In zoos ring-tailed lemurs can reach a great age. In the wild they usually live for a shorter time.
3965.m: In zoos ring-tailed lemurs live past 20.

3967.q: Who usually has the bigger knob on the beak, the male or the female mute swan?
a: It is the same size on both
3967.e: Male mute swans usually have a more striking, bigger knob. This sometimes lets you tell them apart from the females.

3969.q: What does the panda's black and white fur probably help it with?
a: Camouflage in the forest and snow
3969.e: The colours of its fur help the panda hide in the shade and in the snow. This makes it harder for enemies to spot.
3969.m: Its fur colours camouflage the panda well.

3971.q: Why were dung beetles from other countries brought to Australia?
a: Because native beetles hardly broke down cattle dung
Because there was too little grass
Because kangaroos were supposed to eat beetles
Because beetles were supposed to find water
3971.e: The native beetles were specialised in kangaroo dung. The dung of the cattle that had been brought in just lay there, so suitable dung beetles were brought over.
3971.m: Dung beetles were meant to break down cattle dung in Australia.

3972.q: What is meant by coming to terms with the past after a dictatorship ends?
a: Society working through the injustice that was committed.
A ban on talking about the past.
3972.e: After a dictatorship ends, societies often try to investigate crimes, compensate victims and hold perpetrators to account. This is meant to help prevent similar injustice in future.
3972.m: Working through the past prevents new injustice.

3973.q: What does a robin often do when someone is digging in the garden?
a: It waits patiently nearby for worms
3973.e: The robin sits on a branch or stone close to where the gardening is going on. It waits for worms to come out of the soil.

3974.q: What does the physical quantity density describe?
a: How much mass there is in a certain volume
How heavy an object is on the Moon
3974.e: Density tells you how much mass fits into a certain space, for example grams per cubic centimetre. Lead has a high density, polystyrene a very low one.

3975.q: Which part of the lake does the adult lake trout often stay in?
a: In the open, cool water away from the shore
Buried in the mud at the bottom
At the surface of the water in the sun
3975.e: There it hunts shoals of prey fish. The water is cooler and contains enough oxygen.

3976.q: Roughly how wide is a swallow's wingspan?
3976.e: A swallow's wingspan is about 32 to 34 centimetres. This suits its fast, agile flight.

3977.q: About how heavy can a large leatherback turtle get?
3977.e: A fully grown leatherback turtle can weigh several hundred kilograms. That is as heavy as a horse.
3977.m: Leatherback turtles can get enormously heavy.

3978.q: What do bison have on the sides of their head that are not renewed every year?
3978.e: Bison have real horns with a horn sheath. Antlers, like a deer's, on the other hand, are shed every year.

3979.q: What does a maggot feed on before it becomes a fly?
3979.e: A maggot mainly eats rubbish, manure or other rotting matter. This gives it enough energy to grow.
3979.m: Maggots eat rubbish and rotting things.

3980.q: In which part of the world does the African buffalo live naturally?
a: In Africa south of the Sahara
3980.e: The African buffalo is found in the savannah and in forests south of the Sahara. In Asia, on the other hand, lives the water buffalo.
3980.m: African buffalo live in Africa south of the Sahara.

3981.q: Which animals are among the natural enemies of the magpie?
3981.e: Birds of prey such as the goshawk, as well as martens and other predators, are a danger to magpies and their young. The protective roof of the nest helps against some of these enemies.

3982.q: How widespread is the weasel around the world compared with other predators?
a: It is one of the most widespread predators in the world
It is only found in one small Swiss valley
It is limited to a single island
It now only lives in zoos
3982.e: The weasel lives in large parts of Europe, Asia and North America. Only a few predators have such a large range.
3982.m: Weasels are at home almost everywhere.

3983.q: What is the name of a well-known old tower in the old town of Solothurn?
3983.e: The Riedholz Tower is one of the old defensive towers that were once part of Solothurn's town wall. The Zytglogge and the Käfigturm are in Bern, the Munot in Schaffhausen.
3983.m: The Riedholz Tower was part of the old town wall.

3984.q: Which birds called Huginn and Muninn went with the god Odin in Norse mythology?
3984.e: In Norse mythology the two ravens Huginn and Muninn fly through the world every day and bring Odin news. Their names mean something like thought and memory.
3984.m: Huginn and Muninn are Odin's ravens.

3985.q: What colour can the throat of some male common frogs turn during the mating season?
3985.e: In the mating season in spring, male common frogs can briefly take on a bluish colour on their body. This is a special sign of this time of year.
3985.m: Males can shimmer blue in spring.

3986.q: What happens if you take a starfish out of the water for a long time?
a: It goes hard and just carries on living
3986.e: Starfish need sea water to breathe and move. Without water they cannot survive for long.
3986.m: Without water the starfish is in trouble.

3987.q: How do orcas help each other when hunting?
a: They work together as a team
They ask other animals for help
3987.e: Orcas often plan their hunt together and herd prey together. This makes it easier for them to catch large animals.
3987.m: Orcas hunt together as a team.

3988.q: What happened to the lynx in Switzerland around 100 years ago?
a: It was wiped out by heavy hunting
It left of its own accord
It was made into a pet
3988.e: Because of its fur and because it was seen as a danger to farm animals, the lynx was hunted heavily. As a result it disappeared completely from Switzerland.
3988.m: People once wiped out the lynx.

3989.q: How dangerous is adder venom usually for a healthy adult?
a: Rarely life-threatening, but a doctor is still needed
3989.e: A bite is painful and can cause swelling and circulation problems. Deaths are very rare, but you still need medical treatment.
3989.m: Always see a doctor after a bite.

3990.q: How do baboons such as the Guinea baboon usually live?
3990.e: Baboons are sociable monkeys and live in large groups. Together they look for food and warn each other of enemies.

3991.q: How many venom fangs does the adder have in its upper jaw?
3991.e: When resting, the long fangs lie folded back in the mouth. When biting, they swing upright.

3992.q: Roughly how long is an okapi pregnant?
3992.e: Okapis are pregnant for a very long time. The calf is well developed when it is born.
3992.m: Okapis are pregnant for over a year.

3993.q: How many eggs does a female kingfisher usually lay per clutch?
3993.e: A clutch usually has six to seven eggs. They are laid straight onto the floor of the nest chamber.
3993.m: Usually six to seven eggs per clutch.

3994.q: About how long can a hippo hold its breath?
3994.e: Hippos can stay under water for several minutes without breathing. Then they come back up to get air.

3995.q: Which gibbon is the largest species in the family?
3995.e: The siamang is the largest gibbon and has a striking throat sac. With this sac it makes its loud calls even louder.
3995.m: The siamang is the largest gibbon.

3996.q: Roughly how long does a female wild boar carry her young before they are born?
3996.e: A female wild boar is pregnant for about four months. Then the piglets are born.

3997.q: Why does a red apple look red to us?
a: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours
It contains red dye that glows by itself
It changes the light into red waves
3997.e: White light contains all colours. The apple absorbs most colours and reflects only the red light, which then enters our eyes.
3997.m: We see the colour that is reflected.

3998.q: Roughly how many different species of seahorse are there in the world?
3998.e: Researchers know of over 40 different seahorse species. They differ in size, colour and shape.

3999.q: What do common buzzard parents do when an enemy comes near the nest?
a: They attack the intruder with loud calls
They leave the territory for ever at once
They hide silently in the bushes
They just fly away and stop caring
3999.e: If a possible enemy comes near the nest, the parents often react with loud warning calls and aggressive attacks in flight. This is how they try to protect their young.

a: Because many species have become rare
Because they are dangerous to people
Because they eat too many fish
4000.e: Many seahorse species are becoming rarer and rarer, so there are special rules for catching and trading them. These rules are meant to save them from dying out.

4001.q: Roughly how many countries belong to the European Union?
4001.e: The European Union has around 27 member countries. Switzerland does not belong to it but works together with the EU.
4001.m: The EU has around 27 member countries.

4002.q: What happens if a young bearded vulture falls out of the nest too early?
a: It can be badly injured or die
It flies off at once with no problem
Its parents carry it straight back
4002.e: Young bearded vultures cannot fly well before their first proper flight. A fall from the high nest can therefore be very dangerous.
4002.m: A fall from the nest is dangerous.

4003.q: What is special about the soles of a polar bear's feet?
a: Small bumps for a better grip on ice
They are as smooth as glass
They are made of horn like a horse's
4003.e: Small bumps on the soles give the polar bear a better grip on slippery ice. This way it does not slip so easily.
4003.m: Bumps give grip on the ice.

4004.q: Which sense especially helps salmon find their home river?
a: Sense of touch in their toes
4004.e: Salmon have a very fine sense of smell. It helps them find their way back to the water where they were born.
4004.m: The sense of smell leads salmon home.

4005.q: Apart from hearing, what do pigs use their ears for?
4005.e: The position of a pig's ears often shows whether it is alert, relaxed or frightened. Some breeds have big floppy ears, others small upright ones.

a: Bushfires and loss of their habitat
Too much rain in the desert
4006.e: Large bushfires and the clearing of forests destroy the habitat of many koalas. This makes it harder and harder for them to find enough eucalyptus trees.

4007.q: How does a weasel usually move?
4007.e: The German word “wieselflink” (as quick as a weasel) comes from exactly this fast, agile way of moving. The weasel can change direction in a flash.

4008.q: How long does a bonobo mother look after her young?
4008.e: Young bonobos depend on their mother for a long time. They are carried and suckled and learn a lot from her.
4008.m: Young bonobos stay with their mother for years.

4009.q: What kind of landscape does the giant panda mainly live in?
a: In mountain forests with lots of bamboo
4009.e: Pandas need cool mountain forests where a lot of bamboo grows. Only there do they find enough food.
4009.m: Pandas live in bamboo mountain forests.

4010.q: What does the edible dormouse's bushy tail do when it climbs?
a: It works as a fin in the water
4010.e: The long, bushy tail helps the edible dormouse keep its balance when jumping and climbing. This makes it a skilful climber in the trees.

4011.q: How many legs does a ladybird larva have?
a: Six, just like the adult beetle
4011.e: The larva is an insect too and, like the adult beetle, has six legs. With them it crawls busily around on leaves.

4012.q: How many young does a panda mother usually have per litter?
4012.e: A panda mother usually gives birth to one or two young. But often she can only look after one of them properly.
4012.m: Pandas usually have one or two young.

4013.q: How does the otter move when swimming fast?
a: With wave-like movements of its body
Only rowing with its front legs
By flying just above the water
4013.e: When swimming fast, the otter moves its whole body and tail up and down in waves. This makes it a very agile and fast swimmer.
4013.m: Wave movements make it a fast swimmer.

4016.q: What happens in a series circuit if one bulb breaks?
a: All the other bulbs go out too
Only the broken bulb stays dark, the rest keep shining
4016.e: In a series circuit there is only one single path for the current. If this path is broken at one point, the current cannot flow at all any more.
4016.m: One broken bulb stops the whole series.

4018.q: On which continents do wild leopards live?
4018.e: Leopards live in Africa and parts of Asia. There are no wild leopards in America or Australia.
4018.m: Leopards live in Africa and Asia.

4019.q: What is especially dangerous for young ducklings?
4019.e: Little ducklings are easy prey for many animals. Large fish, herons or crows can be dangerous to them.

4020.q: Apart from rodents, what else does a stoat sometimes eat?
4020.e: As well as mice, birds, eggs and sometimes insects are on the stoat's menu. So it is a versatile hunter.
4020.m: Stoats also eat birds and eggs.

4021.q: In which season do most young grasshoppers hatch?
a: In the middle of the night in December
4021.e: When it gets warmer, the little nymphs hatch from the eggs. Spring is just right for this.
4021.m: Spring brings lots of little grasshoppers.

4022.q: What are slimmer warmblood horses often used for today?
4022.e: Warmblood horses are faster and more agile and today are mainly used for riding and equestrian sport. They are lighter than heavy draught horses.

4023.q: What is an important difference between wolf paws and dog paws of a similar size?
a: Wolf paws are often bigger and narrower
Dogs always have the bigger paws
4023.e: Compared with many dog breeds of a similar body size, wolves often have bigger and narrower paws. This helps them run over long distances and in snow.
4023.m: Wolf paws are big and narrow.

4024.q: Which order of animals does the edible dormouse belong to, like all mice and squirrels?
4024.e: The edible dormouse belongs to the order of rodents. This group also includes mice, squirrels and beavers.
4024.m: The edible dormouse is a rodent.

4025.q: Which modern danger especially often threatens common buzzards?
a: Freezing to death in high summer
4025.e: Because common buzzards often wait for prey at the side of roads, there are often dangerous collisions with cars. Today this is one of the most common causes of death.

4026.q: What pattern can you see on the sides of a perch?
4026.e: There are several dark bands across its flanks. They help the fish camouflage itself between plants and branches.

4027.q: How does a dolphin move its tail fin to swim?
a: Not at all, it gets pushed
4027.e: Unlike fish, dolphins move their tail fin up and down. This lets them move forward quickly.
4027.m: Dolphins swim with up and down movements.

4028.q: Why do gorillas only very rarely drink water directly?
a: Because they get enough liquid from their plant food
Because they don't like the smell of water
Because water is poisonous to them
4028.e: The juicy leaves and fruit that gorillas eat already contain a lot of water. That is why they only rarely need to drink as well.

4030.q: About how long does the male seahorse carry the eggs in his belly pouch?
4030.e: The eggs stay in the male's belly pouch for about two to four weeks. Then the fully formed young swim out.
4030.m: The pouch carries the eggs for weeks.

4031.q: Roughly how long does an African wild dog live in the wild?
4031.e: In the wild they usually live to around 10 to 12 years. But many die earlier from disease or other dangers.
4031.m: Wild dogs live to about ten years.

a: A Swiss app for paying without cash using a smartphone
A Swiss bank that only serves young people
4032.e: Twint is a payment app widely used in Switzerland. You can use it to shop with your phone or send money to friends. The money is taken from the linked bank account.

4033.q: How many incisors does a wood mouse have, like all rodents?
a: Four long incisors that keep growing
4033.e: Like all rodents, the wood mouse has four long incisors that keep growing all its life.

4034.q: What is the process called in which plants make food using sunlight?
4034.e: In photosynthesis, plants use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide to make sugar as food. Oxygen is produced as a by-product.
4034.m: In photosynthesis plants make sugar using light.

4035.q: How long do young beavers usually stay with their family?
a: Only until the autumn of their first year
4035.e: Young beavers usually stay in the family group for around two years before they look for their own territory. During this time they learn how to build lodges and dams.
4035.m: Young beavers stay for about two years.

4036.q: What importance does the Alpine marmot have for tourism in the Swiss Alps?
a: It is bred in zoos in the lowlands
It is kept as a pet in towns
It is completely unknown in Switzerland
4036.e: Many walkers and tourists are delighted to watch wild marmots in the mountains. Their whistling and their behaviour make them popular animals of the Alps.

4037.q: How does an ibex typically move across narrow ledges?
a: It jumps skilfully and safely from ledge to ledge
It flies short distances like a bird
It usually slips and often falls off
It only crawls along very slowly on all fours
4037.e: Ibex are amazingly skilful climbers and often leap easily over cracks in the rock and narrow ledges. Their strong, compact build helps them do this.
4037.m: Ibex jump safely from rock to rock.

4038.q: When are stag beetles most active?
a: In the middle of the day in the greatest heat
4038.e: They fly mainly at dusk and in the early evening. That is when they look for partners and places where sap oozes from trees.
4038.m: Stag beetles mainly fly at dusk.

4039.q: What is a strip of forest that connects two separate jaguar habitats called?
4039.e: Corridors connect separate pieces of forest. This lets jaguars travel and meet other jaguars.

4040.q: Which bird family does the carrion crow belong to?
4040.e: The carrion crow belongs to the crow family, which also includes magpies and jays. This family is known for its high intelligence.
4040.m: Carrion crows belong to the crow family.

4041.q: Is the polar bear threatened with extinction?
a: No, there are far too many
No, it is not protected at all
4041.e: Because the ice is melting, it is getting harder and harder for polar bears to find enough food. That is why the species is now considered endangered.
4041.m: The polar bear is an endangered species.

4042.q: Which group of animals does the bison belong to?
4042.e: Bison feed their young with milk and have fur. These are typical features of mammals.

4043.q: How many litters does a female stoat normally have per year?
4043.e: Because of the long delay before the young start to develop, a female stoat usually has only one litter per year. Even so, the number of young in it can be quite large.
4043.m: There is one litter per year.

4044.q: How does a sea turtle move on land?
4044.e: On land, crawling is very tiring for a sea turtle, because its flippers are made more for swimming. That is why it only moves forward slowly there.

4045.q: Why are warm rising air currents (thermals) important for the swift's hunting?
a: Because flying insects rise up with the warm air
Because the swift needs the warm air to drink
Because it uses them to hide from enemies
Because they make it easier to build its nest
4045.e: Warm, rising air also carries lots of small insects upwards. Swifts deliberately use such thermal areas to find plenty of food there.
4045.m: Thermals carry lots of insects upwards.

4046.q: Roughly how long is a panda mother pregnant?
4046.e: A panda mother carries her baby in her belly for about 5 months. Then the tiny young animal is born.
4046.m: Pandas are pregnant for about 5 months.

4047.q: Which small creature often has black spots on red wings and is said to bring good luck?
4047.e: The ladybird is a small beetle, usually red with black spots. It likes eating aphids and so helps in the garden.

4048.q: What is the outdoor area where chickens are allowed to run around called?
4048.e: In the run, chickens have lots of space outside to scratch and walk around. A fence protects them from enemies.
4048.m: In the run chickens can go outside.

4049.q: What job does the appendix probably have?
a: It probably supports the immune system in the gut
4049.e: Today the appendix is thought to be a possible store for useful gut bacteria. People used to think it was useless.
4049.m: The appendix probably helps the gut bacteria.

4050.q: Which UN organisation makes sure that people in the world have enough to eat?
4050.e: The FAO is the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. It helps to fight hunger in the world.
4050.m: The FAO works to make sure there is enough food for everyone.

4051.q: What are the dromedary's long eyelashes for?
a: They protect the eyes from sand
They are used for feeling in the dark
4051.e: The eyes have long, thick eyelashes, often in a double row. This keeps the eyes better protected in wind and sandstorms.

4053.q: Which symbol is often linked with Islam?
4053.e: The crescent and star decorate many mosques and the flags of Islamic countries. They have become a well-known sign of Islam.
4053.m: The crescent and star often stand for Islam.

4054.q: What do pairs of golden eagles show in their spectacular courtship flight?
a: Dives and loops in the air together
They dance together on the ground
They sing a loud duet like songbirds
They change the colour of their feathers
4054.e: During courtship, pairs of golden eagles perform impressive flying stunts in which they plunge down together and climb up again. These flights strengthen the bond between the partners.
4054.m: Courtship flights are made up of spectacular manoeuvres.

4055.q: What special title has the kingfisher had in Germany?
a: It has been chosen as Bird of the Year there several times
It is the heraldic animal of the federal government
It was declared the national bird
It was officially allowed as a pet
4055.e: Because of its beauty and because it is endangered, the kingfisher has already been chosen as Bird of the Year in Germany several times. This is meant to draw attention to protecting it.
4055.m: The kingfisher has been Bird of the Year several times.

4056.q: Why are many gorillas threatened today?
a: Because their habitat is being destroyed and they are hunted
Because it is getting too cold for them
Because they don't like food any more
Because other apes drive them away
4056.e: People clear the rainforest and some hunt gorillas. This makes it very hard for the animals to survive.

4057.q: How does a cow usually move?
a: It walks slowly on four legs
4057.e: Cows walk leisurely across the pasture on their four legs. Only rarely do they run fast, for example when they get a fright.

4058.q: How do injured or sick wild dogs often get treated in the pack?
a: They are driven away at once
4058.e: Pack members also share food with sick or old animals. This shows how strong the bond is.
4058.m: Wild dogs look after each other.

4059.q: What happens when you cut your finger slightly and it bleeds a little?
a: The blood helps to close the wound later
The skin stays open for ever
4059.e: Blood contains special substances that can close a wound. A crust forms, and the skin heals underneath it.
4059.m: Blood helps your skin to heal.

4060.q: Where does the pygmy hippo mainly live?
a: In the forests of West Africa
4060.e: The pygmy hippo lives in dense forests in West Africa, for example in Liberia. It is much shyer than its big relative.
4060.m: The pygmy hippo lives in West Africa.

4061.q: What does the Roman snail do with its foot before it lays eggs?
a: It digs a hole in the ground with it
It builds a nest of twigs with it
It swims in the pond with it
4061.e: With its strong foot the snail digs a small hole in loose soil. Then it lays its eggs in it.
4061.m: The foot digs the hole for the eggs.

4062.q: What does a young male gorilla often do when he grows up?
a: He builds the nests for everyone
He always stays with his mother
4062.e: When a young male grows up, he often leaves his family. Later he may start a group of his own.
4062.m: Adult males often leave the group.

4063.q: Which feather pattern helps the tawny owl blend in with tree bark?
a: A striking colourful striped pattern like a zebra
4063.e: The tawny owl's feathers are finely speckled and streaked, so they look like the texture of tree bark. This makes it almost invisible in the forest.
4063.m: Tawny owl feathers look like tree bark.

4064.q: Why is a habitat high in the Alps good for marmots?
a: Open meadows offer a good view and enough plant food
There is a lot of rainforest there
There are no natural enemies there any more
It is very hot there all year
4064.e: On the open Alpine meadows marmots find enough grasses and herbs to eat. At the same time, from there they can spot enemies early.
4064.m: Open meadows offer food and a view.

4065.q: In peregrine falcons, which sex is bigger and heavier?
4065.e: In peregrine falcons the females are clearly bigger and heavier than the males. Such size differences are found in many birds of prey.

4066.q: As well as normal flapping, what else can the raven do in flight?
a: Soar like a bird of prey
Hover upright in the air like a hummingbird
4066.e: Ravens make clever use of rising air and can soar without flapping their wings, much like birds of prey. This saves them a lot of energy.
4066.m: It uses rising air to soar like birds of prey.

4067.q: Roughly how many webs does a garden spider build in its life?
a: Very many, because it often builds a new web
Exactly one for its whole life
None, it only lives in the ground
Only two webs in its life
4067.e: Because the web quickly gets dirty and less sticky, the spider keeps building new ones. So it can make many webs a year.
4067.m: It builds many webs in its life.

4068.q: How does the otter move on land compared with in the water?
a: Much faster than in the water
4068.e: On land the otter looks a bit clumsy because of its short legs. In the water, on the other hand, it is elegant and very fast.
4068.m: On land the otter is slower than in the water.

4069.q: In which part of Switzerland is the canton of Solothurn?
4069.e: The canton of Solothurn lies in the Swiss Central Plateau, between the Jura and the Alps. It has many hills and forests.
4069.m: Solothurn lies in the Central Plateau of Switzerland.

4070.q: Why can a penguin not go into the water while it is moulting?
a: Its feathers are then no longer waterproof
4070.e: During the moult many feathers fall out before new ones grow. During this time the feathers are not waterproof, so the penguin stays on land.
4070.m: When moulting, the penguin stays on land.

4071.q: What is special about the edible dormouse's breeding compared with many other rodents?
a: It does not have young every year
It only has young once in its life
4071.e: Unlike many other rodents, the edible dormouse does not breed every year. In years with little food it sometimes does not breed at all.
4071.m: There are not young every year.

4072.q: Does the squirrel really hibernate in winter?
a: No, it only has a winter rest with waking phases
Yes, it sleeps right through the winter
No, it is constantly active in winter, like in summer
Yes, it even sleeps a lot in summer
4072.e: The squirrel does not truly hibernate, but has a winter rest. It keeps waking up to eat from its stores.
4072.m: In winter it only has a winter rest.

4073.q: What do cheetah cubs have on their backs that adult cheetahs no longer have?
4073.e: Cheetah cubs have grey, mane-like fur on their backs. It disappears as they get older.
4073.m: Young cheetahs have a grey mane on their backs.

4074.q: What is a baby dog called?
4074.e: A young dog is called a puppy. It drinks milk from its mother and grows quickly.
4074.m: A baby dog is called a puppy.

4075.q: Which animals are natural enemies of wild budgies?
a: Birds of prey such as falcons
4075.e: Birds of prey such as falcons hunt wild budgies. That is why the birds are especially alert in the flock.

4076.q: In Europe, what is part of the main diet of a brown bear in the mountains?
4076.e: In the Alps and other European mountain regions, brown bears mainly feed on berries, herbs and roots. Meat makes up only a smaller part of their diet.
4076.m: In the Alps bears mainly eat plants.

4077.q: What danger does road traffic pose to fire salamanders in Switzerland?
a: Many animals are run over on their way to breeding waters
Cars have no effect on them
4077.e: On the way to the water where they breed, fire salamanders often have to cross roads and are often run over. That is why some places have amphibian protection fences.

4078.q: About how old can sea turtles get in the wild?
4078.e: Sea turtles can live to a great age; some species live for over fifty years. It takes many years before they can lay eggs themselves.
4078.m: Sea turtles often live to a great age.

4079.q: How many pairs of legs do millipedes have on most body segments?
4079.e: Most of a millipede's segments carry two pairs of legs. This comes from segments that have fused together.
4079.m: Millipedes have two pairs of legs on most segments.

4080.q: What are the plants that aphids live on and feed on called?
4080.e: The plant an animal sucks or feeds on is called its host plant. Some aphids specialise in just a few species.
4080.m: Host plants provide aphids with food.

4081.q: What happens in lakes with too many nutrients such as phosphorus?
a: Algae grow strongly and there can be a lack of oxygen
The water gets clearer and colder
4081.e: Too many nutrients make algae grow strongly. When they die, breaking them down uses up a lot of oxygen, which harms fish.

4082.q: Where do many female dragonflies lay their eggs?
a: In the water or in water plants
4082.e: Depending on the species, they dip the eggs into the water or push them into plant stems. This way the larvae are in the water as soon as they hatch.
4082.m: Eggs go in or by the water.

4083.q: What does the swallow build its nest from?
a: From mud and grass stalks, lined with feathers
4083.e: The swallow shapes its nest from little lumps of mud mixed with grass stalks and sticks it to a beam. Inside it lines the nest with feathers.
4083.m: Mud and stalks form the nest.

4084.q: What does the lion have at the end of its tail that other cats do not have?
4084.e: At the end of a lion's tail there is a small dark tuft of hair. Lions can also use their tail to give signals to other members of the pride.
4084.m: The lion's tail has a tuft of hair.

4085.q: What colour is the red deer's coat in winter?
4085.e: In winter the coat gets thicker and greyish brown. This camouflages the deer better in the bare forest.
4085.m: In winter the coat is greyish brown.

4086.q: What do millipedes and centipedes have in common?
a: A long body with very many legs
4086.e: Millipedes and centipedes have a long body made of many rings with lots of legs. That is why they are grouped together as myriapods.

4087.q: When does the carp usually lay its eggs?
a: In early summer, when the water is warm
In the middle of winter in ice and snow
Only on a single day of the year
In autumn when the leaves fall
4087.e: Carp spawn when the water has become nice and warm, usually in early summer. Warm water is good for the small eggs.
4087.m: Carp spawn in warm early summer.

4088.q: About how old can a mute swan get in the wild?
4088.e: Mute swans can live quite long, often between ten and twenty years. For a bird that is a long life.

4089.q: What does the great crested grebe mainly feed on?
a: Fish, which it catches by diving
4089.e: Great crested grebes dive specially for fish, which are their main food. They also eat insects and small crustaceans.
4089.m: Fish are the great crested grebe's main food.

4090.q: How do orangutans sometimes use large leaves when it rains?
4090.e: Orangutans sometimes hold leaves over their heads. This shows that they can make useful use of objects.
4090.m: Leaves are sometimes used as umbrellas.

4091.q: What colour is a wild carp usually?
4091.e: Wild carp are usually golden brown or bronze. This camouflages them well in murky water.

4092.q: What do many squirrels have on their ears in winter?
a: Small tufts of hair, called ear tufts
4092.e: In winter some squirrels grow small tufts of hair on the tips of their ears, called ear tufts. They fall out again in summer.
4092.m: Ear tufts often grow in winter.

4093.q: What do dragonflies traditionally stand for in Japan?
a: They are a symbol of courage and victory
They are a symbol of bad luck
They are seen as food for the gods
4093.e: In Japan dragonflies (tonbo) stand for strength and victory. They often appear in art and poetry.
4093.m: In Japan dragonflies stand for victory.

4094.q: Which fin gives the carp the most push when swimming?
4094.e: The strong tail fin drives the carp forward. With strokes to the left and right it pushes it through the water.
4094.m: The tail fin drives the carp forward.

4095.q: What does a cat like to eat best?
4095.e: Cats are pure meat-eaters and need animal protein to stay healthy. Plants alone are not enough for them.

4096.q: How does the okapi usually live?
4096.e: Okapis are usually on their own. They mainly meet up to mate.

4097.q: What does a cockerel have on the back of its legs that helps it fight?
4097.e: Spurs are small pointed growths on a cockerel's legs. They are sometimes used in fights with other cockerels.
4097.m: Spurs are on a cockerel's legs.

4098.q: In what state are brown bear cubs born?
a: Already able to see and with full fur
Already as big as their mother
With open eyes but no fur
4098.e: Brown bear cubs are tiny, blind and almost naked when they are born. Only after a few weeks do they open their eyes and get thick fur.
4098.m: Bear cubs are born blind and tiny.

4099.q: Roughly how long is a female leopard pregnant?
4099.e: Pregnancy lasts around 90 to 105 days. That is about three months.
4099.m: Leopards are pregnant for about three months.

4100.q: How many eggs does a female kestrel usually lay per brood?
4100.e: A female kestrel normally lays between four and six eggs. These are incubated for about four weeks.
4100.m: A female kestrel usually lays four to six eggs per brood.

4101.q: Is carp eaten in Switzerland too?
a: Yes, it is farmed and eaten as a food fish here too
No, nobody in Switzerland knows the carp
No, carp is banned in Switzerland
No, it does not live in Switzerland at all
4101.e: In Switzerland too, carp are farmed in ponds and people like eating them. It is one of the well-known food fish.
4101.m: Carp is eaten in Switzerland too.

4102.q: What colour is a squirrel's belly usually?
4102.e: While a squirrel's back is usually reddish brown, its belly is lighter, often whitish.
4102.m: The belly is often lighter in colour.

4103.q: How is the sand lizard's skin different from a frog's?
a: It is covered in scales and dry
It is always moist and slippery
4103.e: Reptile skin is dry and scaly, which helps stop it drying out on land. Frogs, on the other hand, need moist, smooth skin to breathe.
4103.m: Dry, scaly skin sets it apart from the frog.

4104.q: Roughly how long does a duck sit on her eggs?
4104.e: The mother duck sits on the eggs for around four weeks until the ducklings hatch. During this time she keeps the eggs warm.
4104.m: Mother ducks sit on their eggs for about four weeks.

a: Blindness that kids are born with
4105.e: Chamois blindness is an infectious eye inflammation that can spread among chamois. Blind animals easily fall in steep terrain.
4105.m: Chamois blindness is an infectious eye disease.

4107.q: How can you often recognise a bush-cricket such as the great green bush-cricket?
4107.e: Bush-crickets have antennae that are almost as long as their body or longer. This sets them apart from other grasshoppers.
4107.m: You can recognise bush-crickets by their long antennae.

4108.q: Is the hedgehog protected by law in Switzerland?
a: Yes, it must not be caught or injured
It is only protected in winter
4108.e: The hedgehog is protected in Switzerland, so you may not catch it or harm it. This helps keep the numbers of these useful animals up.
4108.m: The hedgehog is protected by law.

4109.q: What do dolphins have so they can hear sea creatures such as fish better over long distances?
a: Very good hearing, but no visible ears
4109.e: Dolphins hear very well, even though you can hardly see their ears. Small openings on the head carry the sounds to the inner ear.
4109.m: Dolphins hear well without visible ears.

4110.q: What helps to protect the African wild dog?
4110.e: Protected areas preserve habitat, and vaccinations protect against disease. Working with local people also helps.

4111.q: Where does the white stork most like to build its nest?
a: In a cave in the rock
4111.e: Storks like to build their big nests on roofs, chimneys or electricity pylons. There they are easy to see and protected.

4112.q: How does the common wall lizard often look different from the sand lizard?
a: The wall lizard is usually slimmer with a more pointed snout
The wall lizard is always much bigger
The wall lizard has no legs
4112.e: The wall lizard looks slimmer and its snout is more pointed than the sand lizard's. This is how experts can tell the two species apart.
4112.m: The wall lizard has a slimmer body and a more pointed snout.

4113.q: Why do you rarely see woodlice during the day?
a: They hide in dark, damp places
They are see-through during the day
They fly high in the air during the day
They sleep in the water during the day
4113.e: During the day woodlice hide under stones, wood or leaves. That is why you usually only see them when you lift something up.
4113.m: Woodlice usually hide during the day.

4114.q: What is true about hyenas' teeth?
a: They have strong back teeth for breaking bones
4114.e: The back teeth in particular are very strong and can withstand great pressure. With them they crack bones.
4114.m: Hyenas have extremely strong back teeth.

4115.q: What is a female ibex called?
4115.e: The female is called a nanny, like a female domestic goat. Nannies are much smaller and lighter than the males.
4115.m: A female ibex is called a nanny.

4116.q: About how heavy is a rhino calf at birth?
4116.e: A newborn rhino calf already weighs quite a lot, about 40 to 65 kilograms. That is as heavy as an adult person.
4116.m: Rhino calves already weigh a lot at birth.

4117.q: What do common toad tadpoles look like?
4117.e: Common toad tadpoles are small, roundish and black. This makes them easy to see in the water.
4117.m: Toad tadpoles are small and black.

4118.q: Roughly how long is a weasel pregnant?
4118.e: Compared with larger mammals, the weasel's pregnancy is quite short. This fits its fast way of life.
4118.m: The young arrive after about five weeks.

4119.q: What does a hamster mainly use to find its food?
4119.e: Hamsters do not see particularly well. But with their fine noses they find food and recognise other hamsters.
4119.m: Hamsters have a very good sense of smell.

4120.q: How do male stag beetles move when they fight?
a: They grab their opponent and lift it up
They sting with a poisonous sting
They fly in circles and wait
4120.e: With their jaws they try to lift their rival and throw it off the branch. The loser backs off.
4120.m: In a fight the opponent is thrown off.

4122.q: Which sea turtle is one of the smallest species?
4122.e: Kemp's ridley sea turtle is much smaller than the giant leatherback turtle. Even so, it is a true sea turtle.
4122.m: This species is one of the smallest.

4123.q: How do adult male and female orangutans differ?
a: Males are bigger and often have cheek pads
4123.e: This is called sexual dimorphism. Males are much stronger and often have cheek pads.

4124.q: How do zoos help protect the snow leopard?
a: With breeding programmes for endangered species
4124.e: Many zoos keep snow leopards in conservation breeding programmes. This is meant to safeguard the species.

a: The material that tusks are made of
4125.e: Ivory is the hard, white material of the tusks. Because it is very valuable, elephants are sadly hunted for it.

4127.q: Roughly how many claws does a badger have on each paw?
4127.e: The badger has five strong claws on each paw. With them it digs skilfully in the ground.
4127.m: Each badger paw has five claws.

4128.q: What kind of animal is the cuckoo?
4128.e: The cuckoo is a bird with feathers and wings. It belongs to a group of birds called cuckoos.
4128.m: The cuckoo belongs to the cuckoo family.

4129.q: When in the year do moles usually meet to mate?
4129.e: In spring moles leave their own territory for a short time to find a partner. After that they live apart again.

4131.q: Why do goldfish need clean water?
a: Because dirty water can make them ill
Because otherwise they get too big
4131.e: Dirty water contains harmful substances that can make goldfish ill. That is why the water must be cleaned or changed regularly.

4132.q: How long do adult cockchafers usually live?
4132.e: After emerging, the beetles live for about four to six weeks. During this time they feed, mate and lay eggs.
4132.m: The beetles only live a few weeks.

4133.q: What colour is the coat of the Toggenburg goat usually?
a: Brown with white stripes on the face
4133.e: The Toggenburg goat comes from eastern Switzerland and has brown fur with white markings on the face and legs. It is a well-known Swiss breed.
4133.m: Toggenburg goats are brown and white.

4134.q: How many toes does a fire salamander have on its back feet?
4134.e: The fire salamander has five toes on its back feet. On its front feet, on the other hand, it has only four.
4134.m: The back feet have five toes.

4135.q: What is the lowest-ranking wolf in a pack often called?
4135.e: The omega wolf is right at the bottom of the pack's ranking. The other wolves sometimes tease it, but it is still an important part of the group.
4135.m: The lowest-ranking wolf is called the omega wolf.

4136.q: What does the stag beetle larva look like?
a: Fat, white to cream-coloured, curved in a C shape
Like a small snail with a shell
4136.e: It is a so-called grub with a brown head. It usually lies curled up in rotting wood.
4136.m: The larva is a fat, pale grub.

4137.q: What does the grass snake especially like to eat?
4137.e: The grass snake mainly hunts amphibians such as frogs and toads. Sometimes it also eats fish.
4137.m: Amphibians are top of the menu.

4138.q: About how fast can a wolf run?
4138.e: Wolves are runners with great stamina that can briefly reach up to 50 km/h. Over longer distances, though, they run at a steady pace.
4138.m: Wolves run at up to 50 km/h.

4139.q: Which animal lives both in water and on land?
4139.e: The frog is an amphibian. As a tadpole it lives in the water; as an adult frog it also hops around on land.
4139.m: Frogs live in water and on land.

4141.q: How does a sick budgie often show that it is not well?
a: It sits fluffed up and quiet
It flies much faster than usual
It eats much more than usual
4141.e: A sick budgie often sits quietly and fluffed up in a corner, sometimes with its eyes half closed. Then you should watch it closely and take it to the vet.
4141.m: Sitting still and fluffed up can be a sign of illness.

4142.q: Which animal has the biggest heart in the world?
4142.e: A blue whale's heart weighs about as much as two to three adults. It is the biggest heart of any animal.
4142.m: The blue whale has the biggest heart.

4143.q: What does it mean that the beaver is sometimes called “nature's master builder”?
a: It changes the landscape a lot with what it builds
It is an architect by profession
It has nothing to do with building
4143.e: With its dams and lodges the beaver reshapes rivers and streams so much that completely new landscapes appear. That is why it is often called nature's master builder.

4144.q: Is a pike cold-blooded or warm-blooded?
a: Warm-blooded in summer, cold-blooded in winter
4144.e: Like all fish, the pike is cold-blooded. Its body temperature adjusts to the temperature of the water.

4145.q: According to science, which animal is the okapi's closest living relative?
4145.e: Despite its zebra stripes, the okapi is not related to zebras. Its closest relatives are giraffes.

4146.q: Why is your shadow much shorter at midday than in the evening?
a: Because the sun is high in the sky at midday
Because you walk faster at midday
Because your body gets smaller at midday
Because it is brighter at midday than in the evening
4146.e: When the sun is high in the sky, its rays fall on you more steeply and your shadow is short. In the evening the sun is low, so your shadow is long.
4146.m: A high sun makes short shadows.

4147.q: Where do perch go to spawn?
a: To shallow areas near the shore
To the deepest part of the lake
4147.e: To spawn, perch look for shallow water with plants near the shore. There the ribbons of spawn find something to hold on to.

4148.q: How well are the African wild dog's teeth adapted to meat?
a: It has strong teeth with sharp carnassials
It has no teeth at all
It only has incisors like a rodent
4148.e: Its teeth are typical predator teeth. The carnassials in particular are good for cutting through meat.

4149.q: About how long can a bison live in the wild?
4149.e: In the wild bison usually live to 15 to 20. In human care they can live a little longer.

4150.q: What does a trout use its swim bladder for?
a: It helps it float at one depth in the water
4150.e: The swim bladder is filled with gas and provides buoyancy. That way the fish can float without much effort.

4152.q: What colour are young slow worms?
a: Silvery or golden with a dark line down the back
4152.e: Newborns look lighter than adults and shine silvery or golden. They have a dark line on their back.
4152.m: Young slow worms shine silvery or golden.

4153.q: How does the great spotted woodpecker typically fly?
a: Up and down in wavy lines
4153.e: The great spotted woodpecker's flight looks like a wave. It flaps and glides in turn.
4153.m: It flies through the air in waves.

4154.q: What is a motion in parliament?
a: A binding order to the Federal Council
4154.e: With a motion, members of parliament can oblige the Federal Council to prepare a law or a decision. If both chambers accept the motion, the Federal Council must act.
4154.m: A motion obliges the Federal Council to act.

4155.q: Where do African wild dogs usually give birth to their pups?
a: In a nest made of feathers
4155.e: They often use abandoned burrows of other animals. The pups are safe there.
4155.m: Pups grow up in an underground den.

4156.q: In which national park in Tanzania did Jane Goodall watch wild chimpanzees for decades?
4156.e: Jane Goodall lived with wild chimpanzees in Gombe National Park for a long time. Today the park is world-famous for its chimpanzee research.
4156.m: Gombe National Park is famous for chimpanzees.

4170.q: What was the name of the only party allowed in the Soviet Union?
a: Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU)
4170.e: In the Soviet Union, the CPSU was the only party allowed. It controlled the state, the economy and society almost completely.
4170.m: The CPSU was the only party in the USSR.

4181.q: Which organisation uses a light blue flag with a map of the world surrounded by a white olive wreath?
4181.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world framed by two olive branches as a symbol of peace. The UN was founded in 1945 and the flag introduced in 1947.
4181.m: The UN flag stands for peace worldwide.

4186.q: What is the basic principle of a heat pump?
a: It takes heat from the surroundings and releases it in the house
It produces heat directly from electricity by burning
It pumps hot water from the sea into the house
It stores sunlight in a battery
4186.e: A heat pump takes in heat from the air, the ground or the groundwater, even when they are cool. With a little electricity, this heat is then raised to a higher temperature and fed into the house.
4186.m: Heat pumps get heat from the surroundings.

4231.q: What is the protective layer around nerve fibres that speeds up signals called?
4231.e: The myelin sheath wraps around many nerve fibres like insulation. It makes electrical signals travel much faster.

4234.q: Why do you wash your hands before eating?
a: So that no germs get into your mouth
So that your hands get cold
4234.e: There are often invisible germs on your hands. Washing removes them before you eat.
4234.m: Before eating, you wash your hands clean.

a: Support for poorer countries from richer countries and organisations
4241.e: Development cooperation includes financial, technical and staff support so that poorer countries can develop economically and socially. Switzerland does this, among other ways, through the SDC.

a: A machine that turns wind into electricity
4244.e: The wind turns the large blades of the turbine. This turning is then converted into electricity.
4244.m: Wind turns the blades, and the blades make electricity.

a: Messenger substances that send signals to organs through the blood
Cells that are only found in the brain
4251.e: Hormones are made by glands and released into the blood. They control, for example, growth and metabolism.
4251.m: Hormones are messengers in the blood.

a: A research centre where countries study physics together
A football stadium for world cups
4277.e: At CERN researchers from many countries work together to learn more about how the world is made. It lies partly in Switzerland and partly in France.
4277.m: At CERN many countries do research together.

a: A leopard or jaguar with black fur
4298.e: Black panthers are usually leopards or jaguars whose bodies make especially large amounts of dark pigment. In slanting light you can often still see the spots.
4298.m: A black panther is usually a black leopard or jaguar.

a: Money borrowed from a bank to buy something like furniture or a car, which must be paid back with interest
A loan you only get for food
Money the state gives to all young people
4301.e: With a consumer loan you borrow money for purchases and later have to pay it back with interest. This can quickly lead to debt if you are not careful.
4301.m: A consumer loan must be paid back with interest.

4304.q: What is the name of the well-known mountain pass in the Jura that belongs to the canton of Solothurn?
4304.e: The Passwang lies in the Jura mountains in the canton of Solothurn and is popular with hikers and cyclists. From there you have a great view of the mountains.
4304.m: The Passwang is a pass in the Jura near Solothurn.

4306.q: Which electoral system is mostly used to elect the Council of States?
4306.e: In a majority vote, whoever gets the most votes wins. This is how the Council of States is elected in most cantons.
4306.m: For the Council of States, whoever has the most votes usually wins.

4328.q: How many seasons are there in Switzerland?
4328.e: In Switzerland there are spring, summer, autumn and winter. Each season lasts about three months.
4328.m: There are four seasons a year.

4339.q: In which landscape does the African wild dog live most often?
a: In the high mountains of the Alps
4339.e: It needs open country where it can hunt its prey well. It usually avoids dense rainforests and deserts.
4339.m: Wild dogs need open country for hunting.

4359.q: In which city does the Swiss government, the Federal Council, meet?
4359.e: Bern is Switzerland’s federal city, and the Federal Council works there. The whole country is governed from there.

4366.e: Forests are cleared, and leopards are hunted for their fur. There are also conflicts with people when livestock is killed.
4366.m: Habitat loss and poaching threaten leopards.

4371.q: Who usually has the pups in a pack?
a: All the females at the same time
4371.e: Usually only the highest-ranking pair breeds. The other animals help raise the young.
4371.m: Usually only the leading pair has pups.

4379.q: In the picture a trout is jumping. What does it often do this for?
a: To get over small obstacles and steps
To hunt birds in the air
4379.e: Brown trout can jump over small waterfalls and weirs. Sometimes they also leap for insects.

4386.q: What happens to a young cuckoo as soon as it can fly?
a: It flies south on its own
It stays with its foster parents for life
It immediately looks for its real mother
It builds a nest for its foster parents
4386.e: As soon as the young cuckoo can fly, it leaves its foster parents and sets off all alone on the long journey to Africa. It never meets its real parents along the way.
4386.m: A young cuckoo migrates all on its own.

4387.q: What kind of teeth do adult donkeys have, because they chew a lot of tough grass?
4387.e: Donkeys have strong molars that grind tough grass and straw well. Their teeth keep growing a little throughout their whole life.

4388.q: Which animal with big round ears and a colourful coat of yellow, black and white patches can you see in the picture?
4388.e: The African wild dog has an irregular, patchy coat. Each animal has its own pattern, a bit like a fingerprint.
4388.m: Every wild dog has a unique coat pattern.

4389.q: Why do wild geese often fly in a V formation in the sky?
a: Because it helps them save energy
