4732.e: Swans spend a lot of time cleaning their feathers with their beaks. This keeps them clean and waterproof.

4733.q: How well do bison see compared with their senses of smell and hearing?
a: Their sense of smell is very good, their eyesight rather average
4733.e: Bison rely heavily on smell and hearing. That way they notice enemies in time.
4733.m: Bison smell and hear very well.

4735.q: Which nimble animal with very long legs often hunts insects in houses?
4735.e: The house centipede is a centipede with very long, thin legs. It hunts insects and spiders in buildings and is harmless to humans.
4735.m: House centipedes have extremely long legs.

4736.q: How does a blackbird find earthworms in the ground?
a: It tilts its head and looks closely
It smells them from the air
It only listens to other birds
4736.e: The blackbird tilts its head to one side and looks and listens very carefully for movement in the grass. That way it spots worms before it grabs them.
4736.m: The blackbird looks for worms with its head tilted.

4738.q: What do you call a group of African buffalo that live together?
4738.e: African buffalo live in herds that, depending on the area, can be made up of a few animals up to several hundred. This protects them better from predators.

4739.q: The brown trout is cold-blooded. What does that mean?
a: Its body temperature adjusts to the water
Its body temperature is always 37 degrees
4739.e: Cold-blooded animals produce hardly any heat of their own. When the water is cold, their body works more slowly.
4739.m: In the cold-blooded brown trout, body temperature adjusts to the water.

4740.q: What is a baby horse called?
4740.e: A young horse is called a foal. It can stand and walk soon after it is born.
4740.m: A baby horse is called a foal.

4741.q: What is the female lion called?
4741.e: The female is called a lioness. Unlike the males, lionesses have no mane.
4741.m: The female is called a lioness.

4742.q: What is the second largest fish in the world, which is also a shark?
4742.e: The basking shark can grow several metres long. Like the whale shark, it eats only tiny creatures from the water.
4742.m: The basking shark is the second largest fish.

4743.q: How do harbour seals usually eat their fish?
a: They chew them for a long time
They cut them up with their flippers
4743.e: Harbour seals have pointed teeth that they use to hold fish, but they hardly chew. Smaller fish are usually swallowed whole.
4743.m: Harbour seals often swallow fish whole.

4744.q: How is the black kite's tail different from the red kite's?
4744.e: The black kite's tail is only slightly notched, while the red kite's tail is deeply forked. This lets you tell the two species apart in flight.
4744.m: The black kite has a shallower tail fork.

4745.q: How well does an elephant see compared with its sense of smell?
4745.e: Compared with their powerful sense of smell, elephants see rather poorly. That is why they rely much more on their noses and their hearing.

4746.q: How does a stone marten typically hunt its prey?
a: By creeping up quietly and skilfully
By drumming loudly from far away
Only in a group with other martens
By waiting for prey without moving
4746.e: The stone marten creeps up quietly on its prey and surprises it with a quick leap. This hunting technique makes it a successful night-time hunter.
4746.m: Creeping up quietly is its hunting technique.

4747.q: What does the praying mantis catch its prey with?
a: With poisonous spines on its abdomen
4747.e: Its front legs are shaped into grasping legs with spines. They shoot forward in a flash and hold the prey tight.
4747.m: Spiny grasping legs seize the prey.

4748.q: How varied are the coat colours of different goat breeds?
a: Very varied, from white to brown to black and patched
4748.e: Depending on the breed, there are goats in many colours: white, brown, black or with colourful patterns. Each Swiss breed often has its own typical colour.

4749.q: Can the mosquito pupa move in the water?
a: No, it only hangs on plants
4749.e: Unlike many other insect pupae, the mosquito pupa can move in the water and even swim away when there is danger. But it does not stay in this stage for long.
4749.m: Mosquito pupae can swim in water.

4751.q: What does the call of a male koala sound most like?
4751.e: The call of a male koala is surprisingly deep and loud and sounds almost like grunting or snoring. At night you can often hear it far across the forest.
4751.m: Koala calls sound deep like a grunt.

4752.q: How does the magpie usually react to new, unfamiliar objects?
a: It eats them at once without checking
It immediately flies away in a panic
4752.e: Magpies are known as curious birds that examine unfamiliar objects carefully before dealing with them. This curiosity is part of their intelligent behaviour.
4752.m: Magpies are curious and careful at the same time.

4753.q: Was the blackbird originally mainly a woodland bird or a town bird?
a: Originally a mountain bird above the tree line
4753.e: The blackbird was originally mainly a shy woodland bird. Only later did it get used to living in towns and gardens too.
4753.m: The blackbird first lived in woodland.

4754.q: Which feature most clearly tells male and female sand lizards apart?
a: Males are green in the mating season
Females are bright red in the mating season
Only males can shed their tails
Females have blue spots on their heads
4754.e: In spring, males turn green along their sides, while females stay more brown. Outside the mating season the difference is less striking.
4754.m: Green colour often gives away the male.

4755.q: In years with little food, what is the longest the edible dormouse's hibernation can last?
4755.e: In years with little food, the edible dormouse's hibernation can last an unusually long time, sometimes up to eleven months. This saves energy when there is hardly any food to be found outside.
4755.m: Hibernation can last up to eleven months.

4756.q: Who teaches young otters to swim and hunt?
4756.e: The mother looks after the young on her own and shows them how to swim and catch fish. Males do not usually help raise the young.
4756.m: The mother teaches the young everything.

4757.q: What is the treeless cold plain called where reindeer live?
4757.e: In the tundra the ground is frozen almost all year round. Only mosses, lichens, grasses and small shrubs grow there.
4757.m: The tundra is a treeless cold region.

4758.q: What does the swift mainly eat?
a: flying insects and spiders in the air
4758.e: Swifts catch their prey in flight with their beaks wide open. These insects and spiders are also called aerial plankton.
4758.m: Swifts hunt insects high in the air.

4759.q: What nickname does the robin have because it likes to look for worms near gardeners?
4759.e: Because it so often turns up near gardeners and waits for worms, it is fondly called “the gardener's friend”. It is very tame when doing so.
4759.m: The robin is called “the gardener's friend”.

4760.q: What is special about gibbons' hands?
a: They have a very flexible wrist that helps with swinging
They have webbing between their fingers
They have hooves instead of fingers
4760.e: A ball-and-socket joint in the wrist lets gibbons turn smoothly while swinging. This protects their joints at high speed.

4761.q: How far can some sea turtles swim on their migrations?
a: Never further than the next beach
4761.e: Some sea turtles travel thousands of kilometres through the oceans on their migrations. That is a truly amazing achievement.

4762.q: What does the tip of the great spotted woodpecker's tongue have?
4762.e: The barbs help it hold on to insects when it pulls them out of the wood. That way they cannot escape.
4762.m: Barbs on the tongue hold on tight.

4763.q: Why do ants often walk one behind the other in long lines?
a: They follow another ant's scent trail
They sing a song while walking
4763.e: Ants leave scents on the ground. Other ants smell this trail and follow it.

4764.q: Does the mole usually live alone or in a large group?
4764.e: Apart from the mating season in spring, the mole usually lives alone in its own tunnel system. It defends its area against other moles.

4765.q: What does a gorilla like to eat most?
4765.e: Gorillas eat almost nothing but plants. All day long they look for leaves, fruit and tender parts of plants.

4766.q: Which family of carnivores does the jaguar belong to?
4766.e: The jaguar belongs to the cat family and, within it, to the big cats. So it is more closely related to the lion and the tiger than to wolves.
4766.m: The jaguar is a big cat.

a: Well, they remember how to get to food
Not at all, they forget everything at once
Only when they are in the barn
4767.e: Goats are considered quite clever animals. They can remember how to get at food and even recognise people they know.
4767.m: Goats are clever animals that can learn.

4768.q: What is a feature of a bison's horns?
a: They are short and curve upwards
They are spiral-shaped and very long
They are straight and point backwards
4768.e: The horns are short, black and curve upwards. Branched shapes are found in antlers.
4768.m: Bison horns are short and curve upwards.

4769.q: What is the duck called that is kept on farms?
4769.e: Domestic ducks live on farms. They come from the wild mallard but were bred by humans.
4769.m: Farm ducks are called domestic ducks.

4770.q: Where does the barn owl hide during the day?
a: In the middle of a meadow
4770.e: During the day the barn owl withdraws to dark hiding places, for example a loft. There it sleeps undisturbed.
4770.m: During the day it rests in the dark.

4771.q: What colour are the great spotted woodpecker's wings mainly?
4771.e: The wings are black with striking white patches. You can see this pattern especially well in flight.

4772.q: Why do aphids often appear in especially large numbers in spring and early summer?
a: Because young shoots have lots of sap and it gets warm
Because they only live in snow
Because they only hatch at night
4772.e: In spring, plants sprout and offer juicy tissue. As temperatures rise, the aphids multiply faster.
4772.m: Warm weather and young shoots help aphids.

4774.q: What do you call an area that an animal marks and defends against others of its kind?
4774.e: Snow leopards mark their territory with scent marks and scratches. This tells other animals that the area is taken.
4774.m: A territory is marked and defended.

4775.q: How many antennae does an earwig have on its head?
4775.e: As in most insects, there is one pair of antennae on the head. They are thread-like and can move.
4775.m: One pair of antennae sits on the head.

4776.q: Does a squirrel usually live alone or in large groups?
a: Usually alone, except in the mating season
Always in pairs together for life
Always with a hundred others in the same nest
4776.e: Squirrels mostly live alone. Only in the mating season or when it is cold do they meet up with other squirrels.

4777.q: What is the warm, dry wind called that blows down the mountainsides in the Swiss Alps?
4777.e: The föhn forms when moist air rises up a mountain range, drops its rain and sinks down dry on the other side. As it sinks, the air warms up a lot.
4777.m: The föhn is a warm wind from the mountains.

4778.q: What do whitefish filter out of the water with fine spines on their gills?
4778.e: On the gill arches of whitefish there are fine spines called gill rakers. They hold back plankton when water flows through the gills.
4778.m: Whitefish filter plankton from the water.

4779.q: Apart from eating, what else is plenty of hay in a guinea pig enclosure important for?
a: For hiding and as a soft bed
As a substitute for drinking water
4779.e: Hay is not only food for guinea pigs but also a cosy hiding place and a soft bed. This makes them feel safe and secure.
4779.m: Hay is food and a hiding place at the same time.

4780.q: Roughly how long do baboons live in the wild?
4780.e: Baboons often live 20 to 30 years in the wild. In human care they can live longer.

4781.q: What does a male tree frog do to attract females?
a: It puffs up its vocal sac and calls loudly
4781.e: Male tree frogs have a vocal sac under the chin that they can blow up. With it they make loud calls to attract females.

4782.q: What does a pike feel like when you touch it?
4782.e: Fish have a thin layer of slime on their skin. It protects them from diseases and helps them swim.

4783.q: What does it mean when a dog playing puts its front end flat on the ground and sticks its back end up?
a: It is inviting others to play
4783.e: This posture, also called a play bow, signals to other dogs or people that what follows is just meant as play. It helps avoid misunderstandings.
4783.m: The play bow is an invitation to play.

4784.q: How does a simple electromagnet work?
a: Electricity flows through a coil of wire and creates a magnetic field
A stone is heated until it becomes magnetic
Two mirrors are placed facing each other
Water is poured around a wire
4784.e: When electricity flows through a coiled wire, a magnetic field forms around it. If you switch the electricity off, the magnetic force disappears again.
4784.m: Electricity in a coil makes a magnet.

4786.q: What does a bee show with the round dance?
a: A source of food very close by
A source of food very far away
4786.e: The round dance is simpler than the waggle dance and is used when flowers are found near the hive. The bee turns in circles while dancing.
4786.m: The round dance shows food nearby.

4787.q: How does the lynx behave towards farm animals such as sheep?
a: It can occasionally kill sheep, especially unguarded ones
It only eats grass near sheep
It lives peacefully with flocks of sheep
4787.e: Unguarded sheep can occasionally fall victim to a lynx. Measures to protect flocks help reduce such cases.

4788.q: What kind of coat do rabbits have?
4788.e: Rabbits are covered in soft, thick fur. It keeps them warm and protects their skin.

4789.q: Why do some orca families remember very particular hunting tricks?
a: Because they pass these tricks on over generations
Because they do not like fish
Because they change them at random every day
4789.e: Young orcas learn special hunting techniques from their mothers and grandmothers. That way this knowledge stays in the family.
4789.m: Hunting tricks are passed on in the family.

4790.q: Where does an eagle owl normally make its nest?
a: It does not build a proper nest but uses rock ledges or hollows in the ground
It builds an elaborate nest high up in trees
It builds a nest of mud on riverbanks
It digs its own cave in the ground
4790.e: The eagle owl hardly builds a nest itself but breeds in rock ledges, quarries or abandoned nests of other large birds. Shallow hollows in the ground are also used.
4790.m: The eagle owl uses rock ledges instead of a real nest.

4791.q: Roughly how long is a stoat's tail?
a: Almost as long as its body
4791.e: The stoat's tail is about 6 to 12 centimetres long. At its tip it has the typical black tuft.
4791.m: The tail measures about 6 to 12 cm.

4792.q: What do you call a large group of migrating reindeer?
4792.e: Reindeer live in herds. Some herds are made up of many thousands of animals.

4794.q: How can you often recognise a young budgie that has not yet moulted?
a: The wavy pattern reaches down to the forehead
It has a completely yellow head without waves
It has a long red tail
4794.e: In young budgies, the wavy pattern reaches over the forehead. After the first moult, the forehead becomes smooth and one colour.
4794.m: Young budgies have waves down to the forehead.

4796.q: What does the pulse you can feel at your wrist show?
a: How many times the heart beats per minute
4796.e: With every heartbeat a wave of blood flows through the arteries. You can feel and count this as your pulse.

4797.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Schaffhausen?
4797.e: The coat of arms of Schaffhausen shows a black ram rearing up on a gold background. The town's name, though, actually comes from “Schiffshausen”, meaning boat houses.

4799.q: What is a striking physical feature of the bison?
4799.e: Above their shoulders, bison have a powerful hump of muscle. It carries the heavy head.

4800.q: What does the body of the alpine salamander show compared with lizards?
a: It has moist, smooth skin instead of dry scales
It has fins instead of legs
4800.e: Although alpine salamanders and lizards look similar at first sight, their skin is very different. Lizards are reptiles with dry scales, while the alpine salamander is an amphibian with moist skin.
4800.m: Moist skin instead of dry scales.

4801.q: How can you often tell who is in charge in a herd of goats?
a: By the colour of the coat
4801.e: Goats often sort out their ranking by gentle or hard head-butting. That way everyone knows who the boss of the herd is.
4801.m: Goats sort out rank by head-butting.

4802.q: Can ducks fly while they are moulting?
a: No, for a short time they cannot fly
4802.e: While moulting, ducks lose many flight feathers at the same time. During this time they cannot fly and prefer to stay hidden.

4803.q: Roughly how big does an adult housefly get?
a: About as big as a small fingernail
4803.e: A housefly is only about six to eight millimetres long. That is roughly the size of a small fingernail.

4804.q: When does the garden spider usually rebuild its web?
a: Often every day, usually in the morning or evening
Only once in its whole life
Only in the depths of winter
4804.e: The web wears out and loses its stickiness. That is why the garden spider often builds a completely new web.

4805.q: Where does the female cockchafer lay its eggs?
4805.e: The female digs into loose soil and lays her eggs there. She often chooses the edges of woods or meadows.
4805.m: The eggs are laid in the ground.

4806.q: What do roosters sometimes do to sort out their ranking in the group?
a: They test their strength in a fight
4806.e: When several roosters live together, they sometimes sort out their ranking with small fights. The stronger rooster then usually gets first choice of food and hens.
4806.m: Roosters sort out rank by fighting.

4807.q: What does a badger's face typically look like?
4807.e: The badger has a striking face with black stripes over its eyes. This makes it instantly recognisable.

4808.q: What is the hole on an orca's head called that it breathes through?
4808.e: On top of its head the orca has a blowhole. It takes a breath through it every time it comes to the surface.
4808.m: The orca breathes through its blowhole.

a: Sitting on branches, often in forks of branches
Hanging upside down from cave ceilings
4809.e: Gibbons do not build proper nests like orangutans. They sit on thick branches to sleep and rest there.
4809.m: Gibbons sleep sitting in the branches.

4810.q: How long do pairs of mute swans usually stay together?
4810.e: Mute swans usually look for a partner for life. They often stay together for many years.
4810.m: Mute swans usually stay together for life.

4811.q: Roughly what percentage of their genes do humans share with orangutans?
4811.e: The human genome is about 97 percent similar to that of orangutans. This shows how closely related the great apes are.
4811.m: Their genome is very similar to ours.

4812.q: In what posture does the grey heron often stand for hours by the water?
a: Motionless, often standing on one leg
4812.e: So as not to scare off prey, the grey heron often stays completely still for a long time. Sometimes it stands on just one leg.
4812.m: It waits patiently and without moving.

4813.q: How does a harbour seal move on land?
a: It shuffles and wriggles like a caterpillar
4813.e: Harbour seals have flippers, not legs for walking. That is why on land they move rather clumsily by shuffling along.
4813.m: On land the harbour seal shuffles.

4814.q: What is special about the least weasel among carnivores?
a: It is the smallest carnivore in the world
It is the largest carnivore in Europe
It is the fastest land carnivore
It is the heaviest kind of weasel
4814.e: The least weasel often weighs only a few dozen grams. That makes it the smallest carnivore of all in the world.
4814.m: The least weasel: small but brave.

4815.q: What shape are the mole's front paws?
a: Broad like little shovels with strong claws
4815.e: The mole's front paws are turned outwards and very broad. With their strong claws it shovels soil aside with ease.
4815.m: Shovel paws make it a master digger.

4816.q: Why does the stork clatter its beak so often?
a: because it has no voice for singing
4816.e: Storks have no real song. That is why they clatter their beaks to communicate.
4816.m: Clattering is the language of storks.

4817.q: What does a lizard's regrown tail usually look like?
a: Shorter and a different colour than before
4817.e: The regrown tail is often shorter and a different colour. Instead of vertebrae it only contains a rod of cartilage.
4817.m: The new tail is only a replacement.

4818.q: Apart from prey it has killed itself, what else does the wolverine like to eat?
a: Carrion, meaning animals that are already dead
4818.e: The wolverine is not fussy and also eats carrion, the bodies of animals that are already dead. This helps it find enough food even in barren, cold regions.

4819.q: What does the wall lizard do to warm itself up?
a: It digs deep into the ground
It moves fast in the shade
4819.e: Stones store the sun's warmth especially well. That is why the wall lizard often lies motionless in the sun on a wall.
4819.m: Sunbathing warms up the wall lizard.

4820.q: What are the broad, toothed front legs of a dung beetle for?
4820.e: The powerful digging legs push soil aside. This is how the beetles make tunnels under the dung.

4821.q: How do adult wild dogs often bring food to the pups?
a: They bring up meat for them
They put fruit in the nest
4821.e: The adults bring up half-digested meat. This way the pups and the guards at the den are fed too.
4821.m: The pack shares food with the young.

a: A breed of pig specially bred to be small
A piglet that never grows up
A toy shaped like a pig
4822.e: Mini pigs were deliberately bred to stay much smaller than normal domestic pigs. Some people even keep them as pets.
4822.m: Mini pigs stay small through breeding.

4823.q: How do blue whales communicate over long distances?
4823.e: Blue whales send out deep sounds that travel far through the water. This lets them stay in contact over great distances.
4823.m: Deep sounds travel far in the sea.

4824.q: How fast does a blue whale normally swim?
a: Always very fast like a racing car
It does not swim at all
4824.e: The blue whale usually swims leisurely through the water. But when in danger it can briefly go faster.

4825.q: In the photo you can see a spawning pit. How is it made?
a: The female beats a hollow in the gravel with her tail
Beavers dig it for the fish
The male builds it from twigs
It forms when rain churns up the stream
4825.e: The female beats a pit into the gravel bed with her tail. There she lays her eggs and then covers them up again.
4825.m: The female beats pits into the gravel.

4826.q: What does the perch have on its gill cover?
4826.e: The gill cover ends in a sharp spine. That is why you should be careful when handling a perch.
4826.m: Gill cover with a spine, so take care.

4827.q: How does a stoat usually behave towards people?
a: It actively looks for people's company
4827.e: Stoats are shy animals by nature and avoid contact with people. That is why you rarely see them in the wild.

4828.q: What does the shape of the starfish show?
a: It is shaped like a star
It is round like a ball
It is long like a snake
It is square like a dice
4828.e: The starfish's body is shaped like a star, usually with five arms. That is how it got its name.
4828.m: Its body looks like a star.

4829.q: How many toes do tapirs have on their back feet?
4829.e: The back feet have three toes with small hooves. The weight rests mainly on the middle toe.
4829.m: Tapirs have three toes at the back.

4830.q: What does a carp use to swim through the water?
4830.e: Fins help the carp move and change direction. The tail fin gives it the most push.

4831.q: What is the aim of the agreement on the free movement of persons between Switzerland and the EU?
a: People can more easily work and live in Switzerland and the EU
4831.e: This agreement allows citizens of Switzerland and the EU to work, study or live more easily in each other’s countries. It is part of the bilateral agreements.
4831.m: Free movement makes it easier to work and live abroad.

4832.q: In a wild dog pack, who often gets to eat first?
4832.e: In wild dogs, the pups are often allowed to eat first. This is a special kind of social behaviour.
4832.m: In wild dogs, the young often eat first.

4833.q: Why is the great spotted woodpecker important for the forest?
a: it creates holes for other animals
it drives away all other birds
4833.e: The holes it pecks are later used by many other animals. That is why it is called an important species in the forest.

4834.q: Roughly how long does a ladybird live?
4834.e: A ladybird usually lives for only about a year. For a small insect that is quite a long time.

4835.e: Mallards like to sleep right on the water. There they are safe from many enemies that might lie in wait on land.
4835.m: Ducks often sleep on the water.

4837.q: Where in Switzerland do you often see mute swans?
4837.e: Mute swans like to live on lakes and rivers. In Switzerland you find them, for example, on Lake Zurich.
4837.m: Swans like living on large lakes.

4838.q: Which kind of domestic animals do pumas sometimes attack?
4838.e: When wild prey is scarce, pumas occasionally take farm animals. This often leads to conflicts with farmers.

4839.q: Does the mole have visible outer ears?
a: No, it has no outer ear flaps
Yes, huge ears like a hare
4839.e: The mole has no visible ear flaps, only small openings under its fur. That way no soil gets stuck in its ears.

4840.q: What does a hamster line its nest in the cage with?
a: With sand from the sand bath
4840.e: Hamsters like to line their nests with scraps of paper or hay. This makes it soft and cosy for sleeping.

4842.q: How can you often tell a female kingfisher from a male?
a: By the orange lower half of the beak
By the length of its tail
4842.e: Females usually have an orange lower part of the beak, while the male's beak is completely black. This makes it easy to tell the sexes apart.
4842.m: An orange-red lower beak shows the female.

4843.q: Roughly how big is the territory of a single stone marten?
a: It can cover several square kilometres
It is always only a few square metres
Stone martens have no fixed territory at all
It is as big as the whole of Europe
4843.e: Depending on how much food there is, a stone marten's territory can be several square kilometres in size. In towns and villages with plenty of food, territories are often smaller.
4843.m: Territories can be several square kilometres in size.

a: A rule that everyone must follow
4844.e: Laws are rules that apply to everyone in a country. They are decided by parliament or by the people.

4845.q: Which fish belongs, like the carp, to the carp family?
4845.e: The goldfish is a close relative of the carp. Both belong to the carp family.
4845.m: The carp belongs to the carp family.

4846.q: Which parts of plants do aphids especially like to settle on?
a: Young shoots and the undersides of leaves
Only the roots of all species
4846.e: Young shoots have soft tissue and lots of sap. On the undersides of leaves the aphids are also better protected.
4846.m: Aphids often sit on young shoots.

4848.q: What does a chicken use to pick up its food?
4848.e: Chickens peck up their food with their hard beaks. This lets them eat grain, worms and small stones.

4849.q: How does the barn owl hunt its prey?
a: It glides silently over fields and listens
It digs holes in the ground
4849.e: The barn owl flies low and silently over meadows and fields. It hears the mice in the grass before it strikes.

4850.q: What colour is an octopus's blood?
4850.e: Octopus blood is blue because it contains a special substance with copper. In us humans, blood is red because of iron.

4851.q: Which are longer on a chimpanzee: the arms or the legs?
a: The arms are longer than the legs
The legs are longer than the arms
Arms and legs are the same length
4851.e: Chimpanzees have very long arms that are longer than their legs. This helps them climb from branch to branch.
4851.m: Chimpanzee arms are longer than their legs.

4852.q: What is the outer skeleton of woodlice and other arthropods called?
4852.e: An exoskeleton lies on the outside of the body. It protects and supports the animals, but has to be shed for them to grow.
4852.m: The exoskeleton lies on the outside of the body.

4853.q: Does the small remora harm the shark it swims along with?
a: No, the shark is not harmed by it
Yes, it eats the shark up
Yes, it makes the shark ill
4853.e: The remora only takes leftover scraps of the shark's food. This is no problem for the shark itself.
4853.m: The remora does not harm the shark.

4854.q: How many eyes does an earthworm have?
4854.e: Earthworms have no eyes, because they live underground. But they can still sense light with their skin.
4854.m: Earthworms sense light with their skin.

4855.q: How does a mallard move on land?
a: It waddles from side to side
4855.e: On land, mallards walk with short steps and wobble from side to side. This is called waddling.

4856.q: What can a hamster do when it is very frightened and cannot get away?
a: It rolls into a spiky ball
4856.e: A very frightened hamster can defend itself and bite. That is why you should always handle it calmly and carefully.

4857.q: How do dung beetles travel over longer distances?
a: They fly with their membranous wings
They get ants to carry them
4857.e: Under the hard wing cases lie the large membranous wings. With them dung beetles can fly, buzzing loudly.
4857.m: Dung beetles fly with membranous wings.

4858.q: What are the holes on top of the blue whale's head called, through which it takes in air?
4858.e: The blowholes are on top of the head. The blue whale breathes in and out through them when it is at the surface.

4903.q: What do Christians celebrate at Easter?
a: The end of fasting in Islam
4903.e: At Easter Christians believe that Jesus came back to life after his death. It is one of the most important Christian festivals.
4903.m: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus.

4911.q: What do you call people who help govern the municipality, the canton or the country?
4911.e: Politicians work in governments and parliaments. They make important decisions for everyone.
4911.m: Politicians make decisions for the community.

4942.q: In the photo, the brown trout can hardly be seen on the gravel bed. What is its colouring for?
4942.e: The colours and spots match the bottom of the stream. So the trout is hard to see and can take prey by surprise.

4967.q: Why does your face go red when you run fast?
a: More blood flows to the skin to give off heat
4967.e: When you run, you get warm. To get rid of the heat, more blood flows to the surface of the skin.
4967.m: Blood helps to cool you down.

4998.q: There are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka. So what is the Sri Lankan leopard on the island?
a: The biggest wild cat on the island
An animal that only lives in zoos now
4998.e: Because there are no lions or tigers in Sri Lanka, the Sri Lankan leopard is the biggest wild cat on the island. It is at the top of the food chain.
4998.m: In Sri Lanka the leopard is the biggest wild cat.

5009.q: Besides water and light, what does a plant need to grow?
5009.e: Plants take important nutrients from the soil through their roots. Together with water and light they can then grow well.
5009.m: Plants need nutrients from the soil.

5012.q: Which organ produces bile for digesting fat and breaks down poisons?
5012.e: The liver is an important organ for removing poisons. It also produces bile, which helps to digest fat.
5012.m: The liver removes poisons from your body.

a: A brochure explaining the proposals being voted on
5016.e: Before every vote, the Confederation sends all voters a booklet with arguments from supporters and opponents.
5016.m: The booklet explains the pros and cons.

5017.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
5017.e: On 9 November 1989 the border between East and West Berlin opened. People celebrated at the Wall.

5018.q: Which country has a red maple leaf on its flag?
5018.e: The maple leaf is Canada's best-known symbol and has been on the flag since 1965. Maple trees grow there in huge forests.
5018.m: Canada has a red maple leaf.

5024.q: In a shop you are given too much change by mistake. What do you do?
a: I tell the shop assistant and give it back
I keep it and say nothing
I give it to a friend
5024.e: Honesty matters a lot with money. Money you receive by mistake should be given back.
5024.m: Honestly give back money you were given by mistake.

5042.q: Which water temperature does the brown trout like best?
a: Water that is frozen in winter
5042.e: The brown trout is a cold-water fish. If the water gets too warm, it gets stressed and there is too little oxygen.
5042.m: The brown trout is a cold-water fish.

5059.q: What do you call energy that is obtained from the power of the wind with large wind turbines?
5059.e: Wind drives the large blades of the wind turbines, which produces electricity. Because the wind never runs out, wind energy is a renewable energy.
5059.m: Wind turns the blades, and that makes electricity.

5064.q: What does a minimum size mean in fishing?
a: A minimum length a fish must reach before it may be caught
The lowest allowed weight of the fishing line
5064.e: Smaller fish must be put back gently into the water. That way they can grow and breed later.
5064.m: Fish that are too small stay in the water.

5083.q: What is the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development, or OECD for short?
a: A group of countries that promotes the economy
5083.e: The OECD is made up of many economically strong countries, and Switzerland is also a member. It compares economic data and gives recommendations for better policies.
5083.m: The OECD promotes economic cooperation between states.

5087.q: Besides building dams, what does a beaver do with the trees it fells?
a: It stores branches underwater as winter food
It just leaves them lying around
5087.e: In autumn, beavers collect branches and push them into the mud on the bottom near their lodge. In winter they can reach this food under the ice.
5087.m: Beavers store branches as winter food.

5088.q: Which material stops electricity flowing through a wire into your hand?
5088.e: Plastic does not conduct electricity, which is why cables are covered with it. This means you can touch them safely.

5089.q: What does a ladybird larva mainly eat?
a: Aphids, just like the adult beetle
Only other larvae from its own family
5089.e: The larva is just as hungry as the adult beetle and mainly hunts aphids. In this way it helps plants from an early age.
5089.m: Larvae eat just as many aphids.

5090.q: Why can the tawny owl fly almost silently?
a: Its feathers have a special comb-like structure that muffles the sound of flight
It has no feathers on its wing tips
5090.e: The edges of the tawny owl's flight feathers have comb-like serrations. These break up the air turbulence and make its flight almost silent, which helps when catching prey.
5090.m: Feather combs let the tawny owl fly silently.

5091.q: What does a cockerel have on its toes?
5091.e: A cockerel walks on scaly legs with claws on its toes. With them it can scratch the ground well to find food.
5091.m: A cockerel's feet have scales and claws.

5092.q: Which of these animals is a fruit eater?
5092.e: Fruit eaters feed mainly on fruit. Fruit bats and many gibbons are among them.

5093.q: What is the easiest way to tell a house martin apart from a barn swallow?
a: By the white rump above its tail
5093.e: The house martin has a striking white rump, which the barn swallow does not have. The barn swallow, on the other hand, can be recognised by its rusty red throat.
5093.m: A white rump shows it is a house martin.

5094.q: How does the common wall lizard catch its prey?
a: With a quick snap of its mouth
It waits in the water for fish
5094.e: The wall lizard creeps up on small insects and then snaps at lightning speed. It has no venom.
5094.m: A snap, not a venomous bite.

5096.q: How do young mute swans look different from their parents?
a: they are grey instead of white
they are much smaller and colourful
5096.e: Young swans, also called cygnets, have grey plumage. Only after some time do they turn white.
5096.m: Young swans are grey, not white.

5098.q: How many large eyes does a grasshopper have?
5098.e: The grasshopper has two large compound eyes. These are made up of many tiny individual eyes.
5098.m: Compound eyes see with many parts.

5099.q: What does the breast of a female blackbird usually look like?
5099.e: The female's breast is brownish and often lightly speckled. This helps her stay well camouflaged while sitting on her eggs.
5099.m: The female has a brown, speckled breast.

5100.q: How does a stone marten usually live, except in the mating season?
a: Always in pairs all year round
5100.e: Stone martens live alone and defend their own territory. Only in the mating season in summer do males and females meet briefly.

5101.q: Why were wolves wiped out in Switzerland in the past?
a: Because they were seen as a danger to farm animals and people
Because their habitat became too cold
Because they suffered from a disease
Because they could not find enough food
5101.e: Because wolves sometimes killed farm animals, they were hunted intensively for centuries. As a result, the wolf disappeared from Switzerland completely, until it returned much later.
5101.m: Wolves used to be heavily hunted.

5102.q: What do hunters call an especially large, strong stag with magnificent antlers?
5102.e: An especially powerful, old stag with large antlers is called a royal stag. A pricket is a young stag, and a yearling hind is a young female.
5102.m: A strong stag is called a royal stag.

5103.q: Roughly how old can a sand lizard get in the wild?
5103.e: Many die much younger because they are eaten by predators, but in good conditions a sand lizard can live for several years. Some live even longer in captivity.
5103.m: Sand lizards usually live a few years.

5104.q: In which habitat does the least weasel feel especially at home?
a: Only on mountain peaks above 3000 metres
5104.e: Open countryside with mice nearby gives the least weasel the best hunting opportunities. Hedges and stone walls also serve as hiding places.
5104.m: Meadows and hedges are its home.

5105.q: Roughly how long is a female donkey pregnant before her foal is born?
5105.e: A female donkey is pregnant for about a year, about as long as a horse. At birth the foal is already quite big and strong.
5105.m: Donkey foals grow in the womb for almost a year.

5106.q: Which penguin is the smallest in the world?
5106.e: The little penguin only grows to about 30 centimetres. It lives, for example, on the coasts of Australia and New Zealand.
5106.m: The little penguin is the smallest penguin.

5107.q: How are the groups of most baboon species made up?
a: Several males and many females with young
5107.e: Many baboon species live in large groups with several males and females. Hamadryas baboons have smaller harem groups.

5108.q: What is the job of the fire salamander's shiny, moist skin?
a: It helps with breathing and must stay moist
It makes it waterproof like a fish
5108.e: The animal takes in extra oxygen through its moist skin, so the skin must not dry out. Dry conditions are therefore dangerous for the fire salamander.
5108.m: Moist skin is vital for survival.

5109.q: What do barn swallows often do shortly before they leave in autumn?
a: They gather in large flocks on wires
They dig themselves in for the winter
They hide on their own in caves
They build one giant shared nest
5109.e: Before migrating in autumn, barn swallows often gather in large flocks on power lines or in reed beds. From there they set off together on their long journey.
5109.m: Before migrating they gather in flocks.

5110.q: Who builds a new wasp nest in spring?
5110.e: The queen has survived the winter and starts building the nest on her own. Later the workers help her.
5110.m: The queen starts the nest alone.

5112.q: What is the difference between a wood mouse and a shrew?
a: The wood mouse is a rodent, the shrew is an insect eater
They are exactly the same animal
The wood mouse only lives in water
5112.e: Although both are small and look like mice, the wood mouse is a rodent, while the shrew is an insect eater.
5112.m: The wood mouse is a rodent, unlike the shrew.

5113.q: What is the best way for young wolves to learn to hunt?
a: By playing and watching the older pack members
By being sent into the forest on their own
By reading tracks in the snow without practice
Not at all, hunting is inborn and does not need to be learnt
5113.e: Wolf pups first practise hunting in play with each other and learn important skills. They also watch closely how the adults in the pack go about it.
5113.m: Pups learn to hunt through play.

5114.q: Roughly how long is its tail compared with its body?
a: Almost as long as the body
Only a tenth of the body length
Twice as long as the body
5114.e: The tail is almost as long as the head and body together. It is also thick and bushy.
5114.m: The tail is almost as long as the body.

a: A millipede with a cylindrical body
5115.e: Snake millipedes have a round, cylinder-shaped body. They are millipedes and roll up into a spiral.

5116.q: What is the name of an area in the canton of Solothurn with many fields, close to the canton of Aargau?
5116.e: The Gäu lies in the canton of Solothurn near the border with the canton of Aargau. There are many fields and small villages there.

5117.q: What do hunters call the pale patch on the back end of a red deer?
5117.e: The pale patch on the back end is called the rump patch. When the deer flees, it is easy for other deer to see.
5117.m: The pale patch on the bottom is the rump patch.

5118.q: What material are an elephant's tusks made of?
5118.e: The tusks are made of ivory. They are greatly lengthened upper incisor teeth.
5118.m: Tusks are lengthened incisors made of ivory.

5119.q: What is the stage between caterpillar and butterfly called?
5119.e: Inside the pupa, the caterpillar slowly turns into a butterfly. How long this takes depends on the species.
5119.m: The pupa is the in-between stage.

5120.q: Who founded the organisation called the Red Cross?
5120.e: The Swiss Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross in 1863 after he had seen wounded soldiers at a battle. He later received the first Nobel Peace Prize for it.
5120.m: Henry Dunant founded the Red Cross.

5121.q: What do wasps often do at a picnic?
a: They help themselves to food and drinks
They lay eggs in the cake
They only drink water from the glass
5121.e: Wasps can smell sweet food from far away. That is why they like to land on cake or drinks at a picnic.
5121.m: Wasps love to snack at picnics.

5122.q: Where in Switzerland did the eel use to be more common than today?
a: In rivers and lakes, for example in the Rhine
5122.e: The eel used to live in many Swiss rivers and lakes. Today its routes are often blocked by power stations, so young eels are also released.
5122.m: Eels lived in rivers and lakes.

5123.q: What do fish ladders do for eels?
a: They help them get past obstacles in rivers
They serve as a feeding place
5123.e: Fish ladders and eel passes make it easier for fish to get past weirs. For eels there are special ramps with a rough surface or brushes.

5124.q: What is the name of the animal group that octopuses, cuttlefish and squid belong to?
5124.e: Cephalopods are sea animals with arms around their head. Besides the octopus, they include cuttlefish and squid.

5125.q: What happens to raindrops on a goose's feathers?
a: They soak straight through to the skin
5125.e: Because the feathers are coated in oil, water cannot get in. The drops simply roll off the feathers.
5125.m: Water rolls off a goose's feathers.

5126.q: What is a dung beetle's exoskeleton mainly made of?
5126.e: Insects wear their skeleton on the outside of the body. It is made of a tough substance called chitin.
5126.m: The exoskeleton is made of chitin.

5127.q: How do elephants usually move around?
a: They walk almost silently on soft soles
5127.e: The soles of elephants' feet are soft and cushion-like. This means they can walk surprisingly quietly despite their weight.

5128.q: Roughly how long do young pumas stay with their mother?
a: They leave their mother on the first day
5128.e: The young learn from their mother how to hunt. After that they look for a territory of their own.
5128.m: Young pumas learn for one to two years.

5129.q: What skin colour do many domestic pigs have under their thin coat?
5129.e: Many well-known breeds of domestic pig have pale, pink skin with a thin coat. But there are also breeds with dark or spotted skin.
5129.m: Many domestic pigs have pink skin.

5130.q: Roughly how fast does a peregrine falcon fly in normal flight, without diving?
a: At around 90 to 110 kilometres per hour
It does not fly actively, it only dives
5130.e: Even in normal flight the peregrine falcon is fast, at around 90 to 110 km/h. It only reaches its top speed when diving.
5130.m: Even its normal flight is fast.

5131.q: What do the feathers of young mallards usually look like?
a: Similar to the female, brownish and speckled
Just as green as the drake
5131.e: Young mallards look like the female at first, brown and speckled. Only later do the young males get their colourful feathers.

5134.q: Who do young mute swans often swim across the lake with in summer?
a: With their parents and brothers and sisters
5134.e: You often see swan families with several cygnets swimming together. The parents keep a close eye on their young.

5136.q: What happens to the eggs of the blue whitefish after spawning in open water?
a: They sink to the lake bed
They are carried in the mouth
5136.e: The eggs are heavier than water. They sink to the bottom and develop there in the cold water.
5136.m: Whitefish eggs develop on the lake bed.

5137.q: When do young garden spiders usually hatch from the cocoon?
a: Straight after the eggs are laid in autumn
5137.e: The eggs spend the winter protected in the cocoon. When it gets warmer in spring, the tiny spiders hatch.
5137.m: The young spiders hatch in spring.

5138.q: Apart from red, what colours can ladybirds be?
5138.e: Not all ladybirds are red. There are also yellow, orange or black species with different numbers of spots.

5140.e: A barometer measures air pressure, meaning how strongly the air presses down on the Earth. Changes in air pressure help to forecast the weather.

5141.q: Besides swimming, what else can the stoat do well?
a: It can jump very far like a kangaroo
It can glow in the dark
5141.e: With its flexible body, the stoat climbs skilfully up trees and rocks. This extends its hunting ground upwards as well.
5141.m: The stoat is a skilful climber.

5142.q: How often a year can a wood mouse have young?
a: Several times, if there is enough food
Only once in its whole life
5142.e: If there is enough food, a wood mouse can have young several times a year.
5142.m: Several times a year, depending on food.

5143.q: What does the great crested grebe's call often sound like in the breeding season?
a: Like the croak of a raven
5143.e: During the breeding season, great crested grebes make loud, barking or creaking calls. These help the partners communicate and defend their territory.
5143.m: Loud calls go with the breeding season.

5144.q: What do budgies like to do to keep themselves clean?
a: Dig in the sand for worms
5144.e: Budgies like to bathe in shallow water and then preen their feathers. This keeps their plumage clean and healthy.
5144.m: Budgies bathe and preen their feathers.

5146.q: What do you call a protected area where animals such as the wild dog live safely?
5146.e: In national parks, animals and their habitats are protected. Wild dogs can live there undisturbed too.
5146.m: National parks protect animals and habitats.

5148.q: Roughly how long is an otter pregnant?
5148.e: An otter's pregnancy lasts around two months. Then the helpless young are born in the den.
5148.m: Pregnancy lasts just over two months.

5150.q: What happens when a predator grabs a sand lizard by the tail?
a: It can shed its tail and escape
It bites and kills the predator
It squirts venom from the tip of its tail
5150.e: This trick is called autotomy and often saves the lizard's life. The detached tail keeps twitching and distracts the predator.
5150.m: The tail is shed to escape.

5151.q: What does a wood mouse like to eat most?
5151.e: The wood mouse especially likes seeds, nuts and berries. Sometimes it also eats small insects.
5151.m: Seeds and nuts are its favourite food.

5152.q: How can you roughly tell the age of a whitefish?
a: By the growth rings on its scales
By the colour of its eyes
By the length of its barbels
By the number of its teeth
5152.e: Rings form on the scales, a bit like in trees. If you count them, you can estimate the age.
5152.m: Scale rings give away the age.

5153.q: Roughly what is the wingspan of a kestrel?
5153.e: The wingspan of an adult kestrel is roughly 70 to 80 centimetres. The wings are long and pointed.
5153.m: The wingspan is around 70 to 80 centimetres.

5154.q: What should you do first if you are stung by a jellyfish?
a: Carefully rinse the area with seawater
Rub it hard with fresh water
Jump straight back into the sea
5154.e: If you are stung by a jellyfish, it is best to rinse the area carefully with seawater and get help from an adult. Fresh water can even make the pain worse.

5155.q: What does a ladybird do when it is lying on its back?
a: It pushes itself up with its legs and turns over
It stays stuck there helplessly for ever
It waits until another beetle turns it over
5155.e: With a lot of skill, the beetle pushes off with its legs and turns back onto its tummy. Then it can crawl on.

5157.q: When were the first lynxes reintroduced to Switzerland?
a: Right after the Second World War
5157.e: From the 1970s, lynxes from the Carpathians were brought to Switzerland. This created a new population that grows slowly.
5157.m: The lynx has been returning since the 1970s.

5158.q: Apart from sounds, how do donkeys show other donkeys how they feel?
a: With their ears, head and posture
By changing the colour of their coat
By tapping their hooves on stones
Not at all, only with sounds
5158.e: Donkeys show their mood not only with sounds but also with the position of their ears, head and body. This way they understand each other well.
5158.m: Donkeys also talk with their bodies.

5159.q: What do a wolf's large paws especially help it with?
a: They spread its weight in the snow like snowshoes
They make it slower when swimming
They are only for digging dens
5159.e: A wolf's large paws spread its weight over a larger area. As a result it sinks less deeply into the snow and can move more easily.
5159.m: Large paws help wolves in the snow.

5160.e: Hens lay eggs, from which chicks can later hatch. Some eggs are also eaten by people.

5161.e: Only the male cuckoo makes the well-known “cuckoo” call. The female makes more of a laughing, trilling sound.

5162.q: Why is the praying mantis called a predator among insects?
a: It catches and eats live animals
5162.e: The praying mantis lies in wait without moving and grabs insects at lightning speed with its catching legs. It lives by catching live prey, which makes it a predator.

5163.q: What is the famous bear enclosure in the city of Bern, where live bears are kept, called?
5163.e: The Bear Pit in Bern is one of the city's best-known sights. Visitors can watch live brown bears there.
5163.m: The Bear Pit in Bern has live bears.

5164.q: Roughly how long is a red deer hind pregnant before her calf is born?
5164.e: The pregnancy lasts around eight months. Then usually a single calf is born.

5165.q: What helps the grass snake find prey in the water?
a: It can dive and hunt underwater
5165.e: It can stay underwater for quite a long time. There it catches frogs, tadpoles and fish.
5165.m: Diving is part of hunting too.

5166.q: Why do elephants like to roll in mud?
a: For protection from the sun and insects
5166.e: The mud forms a layer on the skin that protects against sunburn and annoying insects. Then the mud dries and falls off again.

5167.q: How does a wood mouse find its way in the dark?
a: With its whiskers and its sense of smell
It sees nothing in the dark and stands still
5167.e: With its whiskers and fine sense of smell, the wood mouse finds its way even in complete darkness.

5170.q: What applies when young people under 18 sign a contract such as a mobile phone contract?
a: They usually need their parents' consent, because minors only have limited legal capacity
The contract is always automatically valid
Minors may not sign any contracts at all
The contract is only valid if it is made verbally
5170.e: In Switzerland minors have only limited legal capacity, so many contracts need their parents' consent. This protects young people from financial traps.

5171.q: What can you often tell from a llama's ears?
a: Whether it is male or female for sure
5171.e: Pricked-up ears show attention, while ears laid back often show annoyance. This is how llamas communicate even without sounds.

5172.q: Why do scientists give animals such as the brown trout a Latin name?
a: So that they have the same name all over the world
Because Latin is shorter than English
So that nobody understands the name
Because the animals come from Italy
5172.e: The brown trout has a different name in every language. But the Latin name Salmo trutta fario is used everywhere, so scientists worldwide know which animal is meant.
5172.m: Latin names are valid all over the world.

5173.q: Can a lynx pull in its claws?
a: Only on the front paws, never at the back
5173.e: Like other cats, the lynx can pull in its claws to keep them sharp. When hunting, it extends them on purpose.

5175.q: What is the process called in which a sand lizard sheds its tail for protection?
5175.e: Autotomy means deliberately shedding a body part to escape. It happens in various species of lizard.
5175.m: Shedding the tail is called autotomy.

5176.q: What shape are the horns of the African buffalo?
a: They curve downwards first and then upwards
They are straight and point forwards
5176.e: The horns sweep outwards and downwards and then curve upwards. In old bulls they grow together on the forehead to form a shield.
5176.m: The horns sweep down and up.

5177.q: Does the peregrine falcon build its own nest?
a: No, it lays its eggs in a simple hollow
Yes, a large nest of twigs
Yes, a nest made of clay
Yes, a nest of grass deep in the ground
5177.e: Peregrine falcons do not build a proper nest, they just scrape a shallow hollow on rock ledges or in nest boxes. They lay their eggs straight into it.
5177.m: A simple hollow is enough for the peregrine.

5178.q: Which physical changes are typical of puberty?
a: A growth spurt and the development of adult body features
5178.e: In puberty, hormones change the body into an adult body. This includes growth and physical changes.

5179.q: How is the least weasel's tail different from the stoat's?
5179.e: The stoat always has a black tip at the end of its tail, the least weasel does not. This is the most important way to tell the two species apart.
5179.m: The least weasel has no black tail tip.

5180.q: Roughly how old does a leopard get in the wild?
5180.e: In the wild, leopards usually live 12 to 17 years. In zoos they can live longer.
5180.m: Wild leopards live to about 15 years.

5181.q: What do young pumas look like in their first months?
a: They have dark spots on their fur
They have stripes like a tiger
They look exactly like their parents
5181.e: Puma cubs have spotted fur and blue eyes. The spots fade as they grow up.

5182.q: Who is usually in charge in a group of ring-tailed lemurs?
5182.e: In ring-tailed lemurs, the females rank above the males. For example, they get to eat first.

5183.q: How are the toes of the great spotted woodpecker arranged?
5183.e: This toe arrangement is called a climbing foot. It helps the bird hold on tightly to tree trunks.
5183.m: The great spotted woodpecker has two toes forwards and two backwards.

5184.q: Where do whitefish mainly live in Switzerland?
a: In cool lakes rich in oxygen
In the sea off the coast
5184.e: Whitefish need cool water that is rich in oxygen. They find this mainly in large, deep lakes.

5185.q: When are African wild dogs usually active?
a: Mainly in the morning and evening
Only in the middle of the night
5185.e: They usually hunt in the cooler morning and evening hours. At midday they often rest in the shade.
5185.m: Wild dogs hunt at dawn and dusk.

5186.q: What are water fleas, which whitefish like to eat?
5186.e: Water fleas are tiny crustaceans and part of the zooplankton. They float in open water and are important food for many fish.
5186.m: Water fleas are crustaceans, not insects.

5187.q: What does a male common frog use to hold on to a female when mating?
5187.e: During the mating season, male common frogs have rough pads on their thumbs. With these they can hold on tightly to the female.
5187.m: Nuptial pads help them hold on.

5188.e: They can close their ears when digging. That way no sand gets in.
5188.m: They close their ears when digging.

5189.q: Which animal is the largest living species of deer in the world?
5189.e: The moose grows much bigger and heavier than the red deer. This makes it the largest species of deer.
5189.m: The moose is the largest deer.

5190.q: What colour is the belly of many donkeys compared with the rest of their coat?
a: Exactly as dark as the back
5190.e: Many donkeys have lighter fur on the belly, the muzzle and around the eyes. The back, on the other hand, is usually darker.
5190.m: A donkey's belly is often lighter.

5191.q: How does a bison protect itself from the cold in winter?
a: With a very dense, thick coat
With a layer of fat and no fur
5191.e: The winter coat is especially dense and very warm. Bison do not hibernate.
5191.m: Dense fur protects bison from the cold.

5192.q: What colour is a housefly's body usually?
5192.e: The housefly is usually grey and has four dark stripes on its back. This gives it good camouflage.
5192.m: The housefly is grey with stripes.

5193.q: What is the spotted hyena known for because of its sounds?
a: Its loud call that sounds like giggling
A deep roar like a lion's
5193.e: Spotted hyenas make sounds that sound like laughter. They use them to communicate, for example when excited or fighting.
5193.m: The spotted hyena sounds as if it is laughing.

5194.q: In which years do edible dormice breed especially often?
a: in years with lots of beechnuts
in years with lots of snow
5194.e: When beech trees produce lots of beechnuts (so-called mast years), edible dormice have enough energy to breed. In years with little food, some females have no young at all.

5195.q: The scientific name of the great crested grebe is Podiceps, which roughly means “foot at the rear”. What does that tell you about it?
a: Its legs are set far back on its body
It has feet on its tail
5195.e: The great crested grebe's legs are set very far back. That is ideal for swimming and diving, but bad for walking.

5196.q: How fast can a polar bear run on land for a short time?
5196.e: Over short distances a polar bear can run surprisingly fast. Over a longer time, however, it would quickly get too hot.
5196.m: Polar bears can run very fast for a short time.

5197.q: What does a goose use to protect its feathers from getting wet?
a: Oil from a gland, which it spreads with its beak
5197.e: Geese have a small gland near the tail that produces oil. They spread this oil through their feathers with their beak, so water simply rolls off.

5198.q: When do mallards usually find their partners?
a: Only after their ducklings have hatched
5198.e: Mallards usually look for a new partner for the next breeding season as early as autumn or winter. In spring they then get on with building the nest.

5200.q: What can often be seen at the back end of a perch's first dorsal fin?
5200.e: Many perch have a dark spot at the end of the front dorsal fin. It is one of their identifying features.
5200.m: A dark spot on the dorsal fin.

5201.q: In which season do you hear the eagle owl's courtship call especially often?
a: In late winter, around December to February
In high summer, around July and August
Only in autumn during bird migration
Never, the eagle owl calls equally often all year
5201.e: The eagle owl calls especially during courtship in late winter, to attract partners and mark its territory. Then its deep call can often be heard over long distances.
5201.m: Eagle owls court especially in late winter.

5202.q: What does a cheetah's body look like?
a: Slim and long with long legs
Short and stocky like a bear
5202.e: The cheetah has a very slim body with long, strong legs. That is what makes it so fast when running.
5202.m: The cheetah is built especially slim.

5203.q: Apart from Europe, on which continents is the golden eagle found?
a: Asia, North Africa and North America
Only on islands in the Pacific
5203.e: The golden eagle is widespread and, besides Europe, lives in parts of Asia, North Africa and North America. This makes it one of the most widespread birds of prey in the world.
5203.m: It lives on several continents in the northern hemisphere.

5204.q: What do cockchafer grubs mainly feed on?
5204.e: The grubs eat the roots of grasses, herbs and trees. This means they can damage meadows and forest plantations.

5205.e: Baboons are active during the day. At night they sleep in safe places.

5206.q: Where does the cuckoo get its name from?
a: From the colour of its feathers
From a mountain in the Alps
5206.e: The male calls a loud “cuck-oo”. The bird was named after this call.
5206.m: The cuckoo is named after its call.

5207.q: Which way does a carp's mouth point?
a: It has no mouth at all
5207.e: The carp's mouth points rather downwards. This lets it search well for food on the bottom.
5207.m: A carp's mouth points to the bottom.

5208.q: Why are peregrine falcons protected in Switzerland today?
a: Because their numbers had fallen sharply in the past
Because they became popular as pets
Because they have no natural enemies
5208.e: Because of poisons such as DDT and persecution, their numbers fell sharply in the past. That is why the peregrine falcon is protected today and must not be disturbed.
5208.m: A past decline led to today's protection.

5209.q: Does a broken rhino horn grow back?
5209.e: The horn is made of keratin and, like our fingernails, can slowly grow back if it breaks off. But this takes several years.

5210.q: How old can tapirs get in captivity?
5210.e: In zoos, tapirs can live to over 30. In the wild their life expectancy is usually lower.
5210.m: Tapirs live to over 30 in zoos.

5211.q: In summer, what does the sparrow especially like to eat as well as grain?
5211.e: In summer there are lots of insects, which the sparrow likes to eat, especially to feed its chicks. In winter it mainly eats seeds and grain.
5211.m: In summer sparrows like to eat insects.

5212.q: When do common frogs usually lay their spawn?
a: Very early in spring, often in March
In the middle of winter in December
5212.e: Common frogs are among the first amphibians of the year. Often as early as February or March, they lay their clumps of spawn in ponds and pools.
5212.m: Common frogs spawn very early in the year.

5213.q: What pattern do wild boar piglets have on their fur?
5213.e: Young wild boar have striped fur. This helps them hide in the forest.
5213.m: Wild boar piglets have striped fur.

5214.q: Roughly how much does an adult magpie weigh?
5214.e: An adult magpie weighs on average about 200 to 250 grams. This makes it much lighter than a crow.
5214.m: Magpies weigh about as much as an apple.

5215.q: What is one difference between the soles of the feet of the stone marten and the pine marten?
a: The pine marten has hairy soles, the stone marten bare soles
The stone marten has webbed feet, the pine marten does not
Only the pine marten has claws at all
The stone marten has four toes, the pine marten five
5215.e: The pine marten has hair on the soles of its feet, which helps it climb on branches. The stone marten, on the other hand, has rather bare, hairless soles.

5217.q: Why is the giant panda endangered in the wild?
a: Because its habitat is disappearing through deforestation
Because it has too many enemies in the water
Because it is too small to survive
5217.e: When forests are cut down, the panda loses its habitat and its bamboo. That is why protecting the forests is so important.

5218.q: What do bees make from nectar?
5218.e: The bees carry the nectar into the hive and turn it into honey there. Honey is their most important winter store.

5219.q: Which animal group does the hedgehog belong to?
5219.e: The hedgehog is a mammal, which means its young drink their mother's milk at first. It also has a coat with special spines.

5220.q: What is the difference between the EU and NATO?
a: The EU is an economic and political union, NATO a military defence alliance
The EU has a shared army, NATO does not
5220.e: The EU mainly promotes economic and political cooperation between its member states. NATO, on the other hand, is a military alliance whose members promise to help each other in case of attack. Switzerland belongs to neither.
5220.m: The EU is economic and political, NATO is military.

5221.q: What is the shape of the garden spider's web called?
5221.e: The garden spider's web looks like a wheel with lots of spokes. That is why such spiders are also called orb-weaver spiders.
5221.m: Its web looks like a wheel.

5222.q: At what altitude is the Alpine salamander mainly found?
a: About 700 to 2800 metres above sea level
5222.e: The Alpine salamander prefers to live at medium to high altitudes in the Alps. It is even found much higher up than the fire salamander.
5222.m: It lives high in the mountains.

5224.q: How do falcons usually kill their prey, unlike eagles and buzzards?
a: With a bite of the beak
5224.e: Eagles and buzzards kill their prey mainly with their talons. Falcons have a small tooth on their beak and usually kill with a bite to the neck.
5224.m: The beak is the falcon's weapon.

5225.q: Where do millipedes typically shelter in winter?
5225.e: In winter they retreat deeper into the soil. There it is free of frost and damp.
5225.m: In winter they move down into the soil.

5226.q: Why do African buffalo usually stay near watering holes?
a: They lay their eggs in the water
5226.e: Buffalo need water every day. That is why they often stay near rivers and water holes.

5227.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult male lion get?
5227.e: A large male lion can weigh up to about 250 kilograms. Lionesses are usually much lighter than the males.
5227.m: Male lions weigh up to 250 kilograms.

5228.q: What do ants use their antennae for when they meet?
5228.e: When two ants meet, they often touch each other with their antennae. This is how they exchange information.
5228.m: Antennae are used to exchange information.

5229.q: How does a bumblebee develop before it is an adult?
a: Egg, then straight to adult bumblebee
It is born as a small bumblebee
5229.e: Like many insects, the bumblebee goes through several stages. The egg becomes a larva, the larva becomes a pupa, and finally the adult bumblebee appears.

5230.q: How many toes does a common frog usually have on each back foot?
5230.e: The common frog has five toes on each back foot, joined by webbing. This helps it swim in the water.
5230.m: The common frog has five toes on each back foot.

5231.q: How does an octopus often hide from enemies?
a: It puffs itself up like a pufferfish
It makes itself hard like a stone
It swims to the water surface
5231.e: The octopus can change the colour of its skin in a flash. This is how it hides from predators.
5231.m: The octopus hides by changing colour.

5232.q: What can you see in some centipedes after an attack?
a: They change colour like a chameleon
They hide in the sand like crabs
5232.e: Some species shed legs when in danger so that they can escape. This is a defence strategy that lizards also use with their tails.

a: Only one party is allowed to govern.
Anyone may start their own party.
5233.e: In a one-party system only a single party is allowed. Other opinions and groups may not take part.
5233.m: Only one party has a say.

5234.q: What does it mean that the puma is a predator?
a: It catches and eats other animals
It only lives on dead animals in the water
5234.e: The puma usually kills its own prey. For this it has sharp teeth and strong jaws.

5235.q: Can you also see rhinos in Swiss zoos?
a: Yes, for example at Zurich Zoo
5235.e: In some Swiss zoos, such as Zurich Zoo, you can watch rhinos up close. They are well looked after there.
5235.m: Rhinos also live in Swiss zoos.

5236.q: Which predator is even bigger than the lion?
5236.e: The tiger is the largest big cat in the world, just ahead of the lion. Both belong to the same animal family.
5236.m: The tiger is a little bigger than the lion.

5237.q: How many legs does a honeybee have?
5237.e: Like all insects, the honeybee has six legs. It even carries pollen home on its back legs.
5237.m: Bees have six legs, like all insects.

5238.q: How do elephants communicate with each other over long distances?
a: With very low sounds that people can hardly hear
5238.e: Elephants make low sounds called infrasound. They can hear these over several kilometres, even though people cannot notice them.

5239.q: What does the Roman snail need lime for?
5239.e: Lime is important so that the snail's shell can grow and stay strong. Without lime it could not build a solid house.

5240.q: In which Swiss canton is the ibex especially well known as the animal on the coat of arms?
5240.e: The ibex has decorated the coat of arms of the canton of the Grisons for centuries. There it is seen as a symbol of the mountains.
5240.m: The Grisons shows the ibex on its coat of arms.

5241.q: Why do people sometimes fit special grilles or guards to cars?
a: To stop martens damaging cables in the engine compartment
To keep fish away from the radiator
To make it harder for insects to get inside
5241.e: Because martens sometimes damage cables in the engine compartment, some car owners fit special guards or deterrents. These are meant to stop martens getting into the engine compartment at all.

5242.q: How does a fire salamander usually react when you find one in the wild?
a: It usually moves only slowly and does not run away fast
5242.e: Because the fire salamander relies on its poison glands, it does not flee as hastily as other animals. It tends to move off at a leisurely pace.
5242.m: It moves off at a leisurely pace.

5243.q: What does a housefly use to taste whether something is delicious?
5243.e: As soon as a housefly lands on something, it can taste it with its feet. So it knows straight away whether the food is good.

5244.q: What do goldfish need in an aquarium so they can hide?
5244.e: Plants and hiding places make goldfish feel safe and make their home more varied. Without hiding places they sometimes feel stressed.
5244.m: Plants give goldfish places to hide.

5246.q: What are a pike's scales like?
a: Small and firmly attached to the body
There are no scales at all
5246.e: The pike's body is covered with lots of small, firm scales. These protect it in the water.
5246.m: Small scales protect the pike's body.

5247.q: What happens to an ibex's horns during its life?
a: They keep growing and are never shed
They fall off every year like a deer's
They change colour completely every year
5247.e: Unlike deer, which shed their antlers every year, ibex keep their horns for life. They keep on growing.
5247.m: Ibex horns grow all their life.

5248.q: What colour are young sparrows usually?
5248.e: Young sparrows at first look more like adult females, plain and brownish grey. Only later do the males get their black patch on the throat.
5248.m: Young sparrows look like the females.

5249.q: How many gold stars are on the flag of the European Union?
5249.e: The EU flag always shows 12 gold stars in a circle, no matter how many countries are members. The number 12 stands for unity and completeness.
5249.m: The EU flag always has twelve stars.

5250.q: What do you call a habitat such as the rainforest together with all the living things in it that depend on each other?
5250.e: An ecosystem is made up of a habitat and all the plants and animals in it that depend on each other. Gibbons are part of the rainforest ecosystem.
5250.m: Gibbons are part of the rainforest ecosystem.

5251.q: How do jackals walk on the ground?
a: On the whole sole of the foot
5251.e: Jackals are toe walkers. This makes them fast and gives them stamina.

5252.q: How can you often tell young common buzzards apart from adults?
a: By their more heavily streaked underside
By their tiny size, like a hummingbird
5252.e: Young common buzzards often have a more heavily streaked underside than adult birds. Over time their plumage changes and gets its typical markings.
5252.m: Young birds are more heavily streaked.

5253.q: Does the Roman snail have bones?
a: Yes, but only in its head
Yes, but only in its foot
5253.e: The Roman snail has no bones at all in its body. Instead, its shell made of lime protects it.

5254.q: What does the great spotted woodpecker especially like to eat in winter?
5254.e: In winter there are fewer insects, so it eats seeds from cones and nuts instead. These are rich in energy.
5254.m: In winter it eats seeds and nuts.

5256.q: What is it called when cantons, parties and associations may give their views on a planned law before it goes to parliament?
5256.e: In the consultation procedure, different groups can comment on a draft law before it is debated in parliament.
5256.m: The consultation procedure collects opinions in advance.

5257.q: What can you often see on a comb jelly when light falls on it?
5257.e: Comb jellies have rows of tiny hairs that they use to swim. When light falls on them, they shimmer in all the colours of the rainbow.

5258.q: What does a magpie's nest typically look like?
a: Large, with a roof of twigs
Small and in a hole in the ground
Made of mud like a swallow's
5258.e: Magpie nests are large, ball-shaped structures made of twigs, closed at the top like a roof. This protects the eggs and chicks from enemies and bad weather.
5258.m: Magpie nests have a protective roof.

5259.q: What do tadpoles lose as they turn into frogs?
5259.e: When a tadpole turns into a little frog, its tail slowly shrinks away. At the same time it grows legs.
5259.m: The tadpole's tail disappears as it changes.

5261.q: How is a wasp's waist different from a bee's?
a: The wasp's waist is thinner and easier to see
Bees have no waist at all
5261.e: Wasps have a very narrow waist, almost like a thin string. In bees this join is much rounder and thicker.

5262.q: What do adult common frogs like to eat most?
5262.e: Adult common frogs are meat eaters and hunt small animals such as insects, snails and worms. They do not eat plants.

5263.q: Where does the barn swallow like to build its nest best?
a: On the ground in open meadows
5263.e: Barn swallows usually nest inside buildings such as cowsheds or barns. There they find shelter from the weather and enemies.
5263.m: The nest is usually on a beam in a cowshed.

5264.q: What does a guinea pig usually do when it is scared?
5264.e: Guinea pigs are prey animals that flee, not fighters. When in danger they would rather hide or stand completely still.
5264.m: Guinea pigs hide when in danger.

5265.q: What does the organisation KORA do in Switzerland?
a: It researches predators such as the lynx and wolf
It builds hiking trails in the Alps
It organises the hunting of roe deer
5265.e: KORA collects data on predators such as the lynx, wolf and golden jackal, for example with camera traps. It works closely with the authorities.

5266.q: What is used to measure weather data high up in the atmosphere?
5266.e: Weather balloons carry instruments high up and send data on temperature, pressure and humidity to ground stations.
5266.m: Weather balloons measure data high up in the air.

a: Yes, they see perfectly from the start
No, they never see in their whole life
5267.e: Tiger cubs are born blind and only open their eyes after a few days. During this time they depend especially on their mother.

5268.q: Roughly how long does a common earwig live?
5268.e: The earwig only lives a short time. It usually manages about a year.

5269.q: In which country do wild bonobos live?
a: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo
5269.e: Bonobos live in only one country, the Democratic Republic of the Congo. There they live in the rainforest south of the River Congo.
5269.m: Bonobos only live in the Congo.

5270.q: What colour is the milk a cow gives?
5270.e: The milk a cow gives is always white, whatever colour the cow's coat is. Some children think brown cows give chocolate milk, but that is not true.

5271.q: Why did researchers in Switzerland used to find it hard to observe the lynx?
a: Because it is very shy and hides well
Because it only lives in water
Because it never existed in Switzerland
5271.e: Lynxes are secretive, nocturnal animals that are rarely seen by people. Their well-camouflaged fur makes observing them even harder.
5271.m: The lynx likes to stay out of sight.

5272.q: How does the wood mouse behave towards others of its kind?
a: It mostly lives alone and defends its territory
It always lives in huge herds
It shares its burrow with foxes
5272.e: Wood mice mostly live alone and defend their own small territory against other mice.

a: An attempt by Czechoslovakia to make communism more humane, ended by Soviet troops
The start of communist rule in Czechoslovakia
A trade fair in Eastern Europe
5273.e: Under Alexander Dubček, Czechoslovakia tried to reform socialism. Warsaw Pact troops ended this attempt with an invasion.
5273.m: The Prague Spring was an attempt at reform that was crushed.

5274.q: What are dragonflies especially good at in flight?
a: Hovering on the spot and flying backwards
5274.e: Dragonflies control each of their four wings separately. This lets them hover, turn suddenly and sometimes fly backwards.

5275.q: What happens if a dolphin calf needs help while its mother is hunting?
a: Another female often looks after it
5275.e: In dolphin groups, the females often help each other. They also look after the young of other mothers.
5275.m: Dolphin mothers help each other babysit.

5276.q: What does a hippo's body look like?
a: Like a ball with no legs
5276.e: The hippo's body is round like a barrel and sits on short, strong legs. This helps it look heavy and be stable.
5276.m: Hippos have short legs and a big belly.

5277.q: What does a meerkat mainly eat?
5277.e: Meerkats feed mainly on insects, spiders and scorpions. Sometimes they also eat small vertebrates and eggs.

5278.q: Roughly what body length does an adult common raven reach?
