5278.e: The common raven is a fairly large bird with a body length of around 54 to 67 centimetres. This makes it much bigger than a carrion crow.

5279.q: What does the ring-tailed lemur use the “tooth comb” in its lower jaw for?
a: Among other things, for grooming its fur
5279.e: The front teeth in the lower jaw stand close together like a comb. Ring-tailed lemurs use them to comb their own fur and that of their group members.
5279.m: The tooth comb is used for grooming.

5280.q: Which animal group do grasshoppers belong to?
5280.e: Grasshoppers are insects with six legs. Experts group them together with crickets and bush crickets.

a: Newspapers may write what really happens.
5281.e: With a free press, journalists may report the truth even if the government doesn’t like it. In dictatorships this is often forbidden.
5281.m: A free press reports the truth.

5282.q: Does the panda hibernate in winter like other bears?
5282.e: Pandas do not hibernate, because they need bamboo all year round. They stay active in winter too.

5283.q: How does the moon change its appearance in the sky over a month?
5283.e: The moon does not shine by itself; we only see the part lit by the sun. That is why the moon sometimes looks like a crescent and sometimes completely round.
5283.m: The moon changes shape every month.

5284.q: What happens when a sparrow in the group notices danger?
a: they all fly up together at once
5284.e: If a sparrow notices danger, it warns the others and the whole group flies up together at once. That way nobody is in danger for long.
5284.m: When there is danger, the whole group flies up.

5285.q: Roughly how big does an adult carrion crow get?
5285.e: An adult carrion crow measures about 45 to 47 centimetres from the tip of its beak to the tip of its tail. This makes it much smaller than the common raven.
5285.m: Carrion crows grow to around 46 centimetres.

5286.q: How does the polecat defend itself against enemies?
a: It releases a strong-smelling liquid from glands
5286.e: The polecat has scent glands with which it can release a strong-smelling liquid. This powerful smell is meant to scare enemies away.
5286.m: The polecat scares off enemies with a stink.

5287.q: What kind of social animals are llamas?
5287.e: Llamas live in groups. They do not feel comfortable alone.

5288.q: How does a gorilla usually move around?
a: On all fours, leaning on its knuckles
5288.e: Gorillas usually walk on all fours and lean on their knuckles as they go. This is called knuckle-walking.

5289.q: How many legs does a sand lizard have?
5289.e: Like almost all lizards, it has four strong legs for running and climbing. This makes it different from legless snakes, for example.

5290.q: What is the procedure for resolving differences?
a: The National Council and the Council of States bring their different decisions on a law into line
5290.e: If the National Council and the Council of States disagree on a law, the proposal is sent back and forth until they reach agreement. This is called resolving differences.
5290.m: Resolving differences settles disagreements between the chambers.

5291.q: Why is it a good idea to look at prices when shopping with your parents?
a: So you learn how much things cost and shop thoughtfully
Because the shop staff require it
Because otherwise you will be punished
5291.e: If you pay attention to prices, you learn what things are worth and can make more thoughtful decisions. This helps later when you run your own household.
5291.m: Looking at prices helps you learn.

5292.q: Which habitat does the great crested grebe prefer for breeding?
a: Lakes and ponds with reeds and water plants
5292.e: Great crested grebes need waters with enough reeds and water plants for building nests and for cover. Such habitats protect them from enemies.
5292.m: Lakes full of reeds are its breeding ground.

5293.q: What does the typical call of the kingfisher sound like?
a: a melodious twitter like a blackbird
5293.e: The kingfisher calls with a short, high, piercing whistle. You often hear it before you even see it.
5293.m: A high whistle gives the kingfisher away.

5294.q: In barn owls, who mainly sits on the eggs?
5294.e: Usually the female sits on the eggs and keeps them warm. The male helps by fetching food.
5294.m: The female sits on the eggs.

5295.q: What do mute swans do in winter when lakes freeze over?
5295.e: When water freezes, swans look for open patches where they can still swim and feed. Sometimes they gather there in groups.
5295.m: In winter swans look for open water.

5296.q: What are fox cubs like when they are born?
a: Able to run straight away like foals
Already with sharp teeth and fully independent
5296.e: Fox cubs are born blind and deaf and depend completely on their mother. They only open their eyes after about two weeks.
5296.m: Fox cubs are blind at first.

5297.q: According to conservationists, how is the hippo population assessed today?
a: It is not protected at all
5297.e: The hippo is considered a threatened species, because its habitat is getting smaller and smaller. Conservationists are trying to protect it.

5298.q: Do penguins have teeth in their mouths?
a: No, but they have spiky barbs on their tongue
Yes, sharp teeth like a shark
No, they have no mouth at all
5298.e: Penguins have no real teeth, but they do have spiky barbs in their throat and on their tongue. These help them hold on to slippery fish and swallow them.
5298.m: Penguins have barbs instead of teeth.

5299.q: What does an adult salmon mainly eat in the sea?
5299.e: In the sea, the salmon hunts fish such as herring and small crustaceans. This makes it big and strong.
5299.m: In the sea, salmon eat fish and crustaceans.

5300.q: What do meerkats have around their eyes that protects them from sunlight?
5300.e: The dark rings around the eyes work rather like sunglasses. They reduce the glare from the bright light.
5300.m: Dark eye rings work like sunglasses.

5302.q: How do young blackbirds often leave the nest?
a: They can hop before they can fly properly
They fly away perfectly straight away
They stay in the nest all their life
5302.e: Young blackbirds often leave the nest before they can really fly well. They then hop around on the ground and are still fed by their parents.
5302.m: Young blackbirds often hop before they fly.

5303.q: Which Swiss city has a zoo where you can see snow leopards?
5303.e: Zurich Zoo keeps snow leopards in a mountain enclosure. They have also been kept at Basel Zoo.
5303.m: Snow leopards live at Zurich Zoo.

5304.q: What is social grooming in baboons?
a: They clean each other's fur and strengthen bonds
5304.e: When grooming, they remove dirt and parasites. At the same time it strengthens friendships and calms the animals.

5305.q: What does the spring dumbledor beetle mainly feed on?
5305.e: The spring dumbledor eats dung, for example from deer or cows, and also buries it for its larvae. This helps bring nutrients into the soil.
5305.m: Dung beetles make use of other animals' droppings.

5306.q: What is an adult female pig called?
5306.e: An adult female pig is called a sow. After giving birth she takes loving care of her piglets.
5306.m: An adult female pig is called a sow.

5307.q: How does an octopus move along the seabed?
5307.e: On the seabed, the octopus usually crawls along on its arms. To swim fast, however, it prefers to use jet propulsion.
5307.m: The octopus crawls with its arms.

5308.q: What is the badger especially good at?
5308.e: With its strong paws and claws, the badger digs long tunnels in the ground. That is where it lives.
5308.m: The badger is a good digger.

5309.q: Why is it sometimes hard to tell the edible frog apart from its two parent species with certainty?
a: Because it combines outward features of both parent species
Because it can never be seen
5309.e: Because the edible frog is a cross between the marsh frog and the pool frog, it often shows features of both species. That is why close examination is sometimes needed to tell the three species apart for sure.
5309.m: The edible frog mixes features of both parent species.

5310.q: What does a polar bear eat first when it catches a seal?
5310.e: The seal's fatty blubber is especially important for the polar bear. It gives it lots of energy for the cold.
5310.m: The polar bear eats the blubber first.

5311.q: What happens to goldfish in a pond when it gets cold in winter?
a: They become calmer and move less
5311.e: In winter, goldfish in a pond slow down their metabolism and hardly move. This way they survive the cold season, as long as the pond does not freeze solid.

5312.q: In which country do people often eat carp at Christmas?
5312.e: In the Czech Republic, fried carp is a traditional part of the Christmas meal. Many families buy a carp especially for it.
5312.m: In the Czech Republic people eat carp at Christmas.

5313.q: Where do most species of isopod live?
5313.e: Most isopod species live in water, especially in the sea. Woodlice that live on land are only part of the group.

5314.q: What does an especially dark mane on a male lion often show?
a: That he is strong and healthy
That he is still a baby
5314.e: In lions, a dark, thick mane is seen as a sign of strength and good health. Lionesses often prefer males with dark manes.
5314.m: A dark mane shows strength and health.

5316.q: What does it mean when a hippo opens its mouth wide?
a: It is threatening and showing its strength
It is tired and yawning before sleep
5316.e: Opening the mouth wide is usually a threat to other hippos. This is how they show who is stronger.
5316.m: A wide-open mouth is a threat.

5317.q: Why were foxes often linked with the disease rabies in the past?
a: Because back then they often spread rabies
Because rabies only occurs in foxes and nowhere else
Because foxes are immune to rabies and were therefore to blame
5317.e: In the past, foxes in Switzerland often spread the dangerous disease rabies. Thanks to targeted vaccination campaigns, rabies in foxes was successfully pushed back.
5317.m: Foxes used to spread rabies often.

5320.q: How often a year does the stone marten change its coat?
5320.e: Stone martens have a summer coat and a thicker winter coat. The change adapts their coat to the different temperatures through the year.
5320.m: Stone martens change their coat twice a year.

5321.q: Where do many red kites from Switzerland go in winter?
a: to Africa south of the Sahara
5321.e: Many red kites leave Switzerland in autumn and spend the winter in warmer parts of western Europe such as Spain or southern France. There they find enough food even in winter.
5321.m: Many red kites spend the winter in Spain.

5322.q: What are price comparison websites useful for?
a: To compare prices or services of different providers before buying or signing up
To automatically choose the most expensive offer
5322.e: Comparison websites show different offers side by side clearly, for example for insurance or mobile phone contracts. This makes it easier to find a cheap offer that suits you.

5323.q: Roughly how long is a sow pregnant with her piglets before they are born?
5323.e: Pregnancy in pigs lasts about 115 days, so almost four months. Then the piglets are born.
5323.m: Piglets grow in the womb for about four months.

5324.q: What is the males' throat sac for?
a: It makes their loud calls stronger
It is used for carrying young
It keeps them warm at night
5324.e: The throat sac works like a sound chamber. This means the males' calls can be heard far away.
5324.m: The throat sac makes calls louder.

5326.q: In carrion crows, who builds the nest?
a: the whole crow family from the year before
5326.e: The male and female build their nest together, usually high up in a tree. This also strengthens the bond between the two birds.
5326.m: Carrion crow pairs build the nest together.

5327.q: What do tiger cubs drink in their first weeks?
5327.e: In their first weeks, tiger cubs drink only their mother's milk. Only later do they eat meat as well.

5328.q: Roughly how long does an Atlantic salmon live?
a: A few years, usually up to about 5 to 8
5328.e: Salmon usually live for several years, some up to about eight. The exact length depends on their environment and migration.

5329.q: How do common buzzard pairs often behave over several years?
a: They often stay together as a pair
They never live together as a pair
They only meet once in their lives
5329.e: Common buzzards are usually monogamous and often stay with the same partner for several years. They also often use the same nest again and again.
5329.m: Pairs often stay together for a long time.

5330.q: Which feature shows that the snow leopard is a mammal?
a: Its young drink their mother's milk
5330.e: Mammals feed their young with milk. The snow leopard also has fur and is warm-blooded.
5330.m: Mammals feed their young with milk.

5331.q: Where was the dromedary probably first domesticated?
5331.e: People there began keeping dromedaries a few thousand years ago. From there they spread to other desert regions.

a: The distance light travels in one year
The time a planet takes to go round once
An especially bright year for astronomers
The time between two solar eclipses
5345.e: A light year is a unit of distance, not of time, and is about 9.5 trillion kilometres. It is used to make the huge distances in space easier to understand.
5345.m: A light year measures distance, not time.

5352.q: You see a leopard and a cheetah. How can you recognise the cheetah?
a: By the black tear stripes on its face
5352.e: Cheetahs have black lines running from the eyes to the mouth and simple spots on their fur. Leopards have rosettes.
5352.m: The cheetah has tear stripes on its face, the leopard has rosettes in its fur.

5386.q: Which animal is an enemy that often tries to take the wild dogs' prey?
5386.e: Lions and spotted hyenas sometimes steal the wild dogs' prey. Lions can also kill wild dogs.
5386.m: Lions and hyenas are rivals of wild dogs.

5401.q: What is the basic principle of a generator?
a: It converts kinetic energy into electricity using magnetic fields
It stores chemical energy in a cell
It produces light by heating a wire
It turns electricity directly into water
5401.e: If a coil of wire is turned in a magnetic field, a voltage is produced in it. Generators in power stations use exactly this principle to produce electricity.
5401.m: Movement in a magnetic field produces electricity.

a: A famine in Ukraine in the 1930s partly caused by the Soviet government
A festival celebrating the October Revolution
A trade agreement between East and West
5414.e: In the early 1930s, millions of people in Ukraine died in a famine. It was made much worse by the forced collectivisation of farming and Stalin’s policies.
5414.m: The Holodomor was a famine in Ukraine.

5429.q: What does the World Trade Organization (WTO), based in Geneva, do?
a: It sets rules for international trade
5429.e: The WTO makes sure there are shared trade rules between countries and settles trade disputes. Its headquarters are in Geneva.

5467.q: How successful are African wild dogs at hunting compared with lions?
5467.e: Wild dogs are among the most successful hunters in Africa. Their teamwork and stamina pay off.
5467.m: Wild dogs are very successful hunters.

5497.q: What is the person called who calls people to prayer from the minaret?
5497.e: The muezzin calls out the call to prayer five times a day. In the past he climbed the minaret to do it; today loudspeakers are often used.
5497.m: The muezzin calls people to prayer.

5508.e: The brain sits protected inside your skull. It controls everything you think, feel and do.
5508.m: Your brain lives in your head.

5514.q: What does freedom of expression mean?
a: You may say openly what you think.
You must always agree with the government.
You may only talk at home.
5514.e: Freedom of expression means that everyone may express their thoughts freely without being punished. In dictatorships this is often not allowed.
5514.m: Freedom of expression allows open speech.

a: Energy obtained from the heat inside the Earth
Energy from the movement of the seas
Energy from the Earth's magnetic field
5552.e: Deep inside the Earth it is very hot. This heat can be used to heat houses or to produce electricity.
5552.m: Geothermal energy uses heat from the Earth.

a: An important leader of the October Revolution who was later exiled by Stalin
The founder of the Berlin Wall
5553.e: Leon Trotsky played a major part in organising the Red Army and the Revolution of 1917. Later Stalin drove him out of the Soviet Union, and he was murdered in Mexico in 1940.
5553.m: Trotsky was later exiled by Stalin.

5564.q: Which organ stores extra sugar as glycogen?
5564.e: The liver stores glucose in the form of glycogen. When needed, it turns it back into sugar for energy.
5564.m: The liver stores sugar as glycogen.

5570.q: What happens to an ice cube when you hold it in your hand?
a: It melts because of your body heat
5570.e: Your hand is warmer than the ice, so it gives heat to the ice. This turns the solid ice into liquid water.

5581.q: What do you call a group of African wild dogs?
5581.e: Wild dogs live in packs. A pack usually consists of related animals.
5581.m: Wild dogs live in a pack.

5585.q: Why do cacti have spines instead of large leaves?
5585.e: Large leaves lose a lot of water through evaporation. Cacti live in dry areas, and thanks to their spines they save precious water.

5645.q: What protects your teeth on the outside?
5645.e: Tooth enamel is the hard outer layer of the teeth. It is even harder than bone.

5658.q: What is the force called that always pulls you towards the ground?
5658.e: The Earth's gravity pulls everything downwards. That is why things fall when you let go of them.

5662.q: Which big cat is the only one that usually lives in groups called prides?
5662.e: Lions live in prides with several females, their young and one or a few males. Tigers, leopards and jaguars are loners.
5662.m: The lion is the only big cat that lives in a pride.

5672.q: Which trout originally comes from North America and is now often kept on fish farms?
5672.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. It grows quickly and is therefore often farmed. Brown trout, lake trout and sea trout are native here.
5672.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

5676.q: What is the difference between a popular initiative and a referendum?
a: With an initiative you ask for something new, with a referendum you oppose a law that has been passed
Initiatives only apply to cantons, referendums only to municipalities
5676.e: With a popular initiative, the people ask for a new article in the constitution. With a referendum, the people can still stop a law passed by parliament.
5676.m: An initiative demands, a referendum brakes.

5688.q: Roughly how heavy does an adult African wild dog get?
5688.e: It is about as heavy as a medium-sized dog. The animals are slim and long-legged.
5688.m: Wild dogs weigh about 20 to 30 kilograms.

a: A strong thinning of the protective ozone layer, mainly over Antarctica
A hole in the Earth’s crust
5715.e: Certain chemicals have greatly weakened the ozone layer over Antarctica. As a result, more dangerous UV radiation reaches the Earth.
5715.m: The ozone hole weakens the atmosphere’s UV protection.

5722.q: The picture shows a habitat. Where does the brown trout feel most at home?
a: In a cool, clear stream with lots of oxygen
In a swamp with no current
5722.e: The brown trout needs clean, cold water rich in oxygen. It finds such conditions in fast-flowing streams.
5722.m: It loves cool, clear, fast streams.

5726.q: What does a seed need in order to germinate?
5726.e: A seed needs moisture and warmth to start sprouting. In the soil it also finds support and nutrients.
5726.m: Seeds need water, warmth and soil.

5745.q: What do Buddhist monks and nuns often do to find inner peace?
5745.e: When meditating, Buddhist monks and nuns sit still and concentrate on their breathing. In this way they try to calm their thoughts.
5745.m: Meditation helps you find inner peace.

a: The vote of a canton when counting the majority of cantons
The vote of a single citizen
A second vote for Swiss living abroad
5746.e: In votes that need a majority of the cantons, the result in each canton counts as one cantonal vote. The six former half-cantons, such as Obwalden or Basel-Stadt, each have half a cantonal vote.
5746.m: Each canton has one cantonal vote.

5749.q: How many pups are often in an African wild dog litter?
a: Often more than six, sometimes over ten
5749.e: Wild dogs have quite large litters. The number of pups can even be over ten.

5758.e: Fish eggs are called roe. Milt is the name for the males' sperm.

5807.q: Which country has a red circle in the middle of a white flag?
5807.e: The red circle on the Japanese flag represents the rising sun. That is why Japan is also called the “Land of the Rising Sun”.
5807.m: Japan's flag shows a red sun.

5843.q: What is special about the African wild dog's paws compared with many other dogs?
a: They have four toes on the front paws
5843.e: The wild dog has no fifth toe, the so-called dewclaw, on its front paws. So it has four toes there.
5843.m: Wild dogs have only four toes at the front.

a: Being unable to digest milk sugar properly
5849.e: With lactose intolerance, an enzyme for digesting milk sugar is missing. This often leads to tummy ache after dairy products.
5849.m: With lactose intolerance, milk sugar is hard to digest.

a: Restructuring the economy with more freedom for businesses
5868.e: Perestroika means ‘restructuring’. Gorbachev wanted to reform the weak Soviet economy with it, which in the end also led to big political changes.
5868.m: Perestroika meant restructuring the Soviet economy.

5875.q: What is a treaty between two countries?
a: A written agreement that both keep to
5875.e: In a treaty, countries promise, for example, to work together or to avoid disputes. Such treaties are very important for peace.
5875.m: A treaty is an agreement between countries.

5881.q: What does the African wild dog mainly eat?
5881.e: It is a meat-eater and mainly hunts medium-sized antelopes such as impalas. Smaller prey is also on the menu.
5881.m: Wild dogs are meat-eaters and hunt antelopes.

5898.q: What is the name of the beautiful old castle with a large garden near Solothurn?
5898.e: Waldegg Castle stands on a hill near Feldbrunnen and was built long ago for a rich gentleman. Today you can visit the beautiful garden and the rooms.
5898.m: Waldegg Castle stands on a hill near Solothurn.

a: A question from members of parliament to the Federal Council, which it must answer
A law about Swiss living abroad
5900.e: With an interpellation, members of parliament can ask the government for information. The Federal Council must then answer these questions in writing.
5900.m: An interpellation asks the Federal Council for information.

5903.q: What does ‘cumulating’ mean in an election?
a: Writing a name twice on the ballot paper
5903.e: When cumulating, you give a person twice the weight by writing their name twice. This way the person gets more votes.
5903.m: Cumulating doubles the vote for one person.

5908.q: What makes the wild dog a good long-distance runner?
5908.e: It can chase its prey over long distances. This tires out the prey animals.
5908.m: Wild dogs hunt with lots of stamina.

5916.q: What is the so-called ‘magic formula’ in Swiss politics?
a: A fixed sharing of Federal Council seats among the largest parties
The name of the Federal Constitution
5916.e: The magic formula describes how the seats on the Federal Council are traditionally shared among the largest parties.
5916.m: The magic formula shares out Federal Council seats.

5932.q: Where is the asteroid belt in our solar system?
a: Between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter
Between the Earth and the moon
5932.e: The asteroid belt contains countless rocks of different sizes. It lies between the orbit of Mars and the orbit of Jupiter.
5932.m: The asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter.

5940.q: You see a brown trout. Which family of fish does it belong to?
5940.e: The brown trout belongs to the salmon family. Its relatives include the salmon and the rainbow trout.
5940.m: The brown trout is in the salmon family.

5956.q: What is one difference between a leopard and a jaguar?
a: The jaguar is more powerfully built
The leopard lives in South America
5956.e: The jaguar looks bulkier and has a bigger head. It also lives in America, while the leopard lives in Africa and Asia.
5956.m: The jaguar is stockier, the leopard slimmer.

5979.q: What shape is our galaxy, the Milky Way?
a: A flat disc with no structure
5979.e: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy with several arms winding round a centre. Our solar system is in one of these arms.
5979.m: The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy.

5988.q: What is the layer called that protects the Earth from dangerous UV radiation?
5988.e: The ozone layer is high up in the atmosphere and filters out a large part of the sun’s harmful UV radiation. Without it, life on Earth would be much harder.
5988.m: The ozone layer protects against UV radiation.

6009.q: In the photo a leopard is lying on a branch. What does it often do with its prey in the tree?
a: It hides it and eats it there
It throws it into the water
6009.e: Leopards are strong climbers and drag their prey up trees. This protects it from lions and hyenas.
6009.m: Leopards take their prey up trees.

6011.q: Why is it important that all adults are allowed to have a say?
a: So that decisions are fair for everyone
So that there are more holidays
So that nobody has to work
So that everyone looks the same
6011.e: When many people are allowed to help decide, decisions become fairer. Every vote counts the same.

a: Signals are passed from one nerve cell to the next
6023.e: At the synapse, a nerve cell uses messenger substances to pass a signal to the next cell. This is how communication in the nervous system works.

6056.q: What is the Federal Constitution, explained very simply?
6056.e: The Federal Constitution contains the most important rules about how Switzerland is organised. It can only be changed by the people.
6056.m: The constitution is the most important rule book.

6062.q: What is the protein in red blood cells that picks up and carries oxygen called?
6062.e: Haemoglobin contains iron and picks up oxygen in the lungs. It also gives blood its red colour.

6069.q: Which language, besides English, is often also spoken at many international conferences?
6069.e: Besides English, French is one of the most important languages at international meetings, partly because Geneva is a French-speaking city. The UN has six official languages in total.
6069.m: French is often an important conference language.

6080.q: Who began a period of ‘de-Stalinisation’ after Stalin’s death?
6080.e: In 1956 Nikita Khrushchev criticised Stalin’s crimes in a famous speech. After that, some rules in the Soviet Union were relaxed a little.

6112.q: What does a torch need to shine?
6112.e: The battery supplies the electricity that makes the small bulb or LED light up. Without electricity the torch stays dark.
6112.m: No torch shines without a battery.

6116.q: What does a secret police do in a dictatorship?
a: It secretly watches people who think differently.
6116.e: A secret police searches in secret for people who criticise the ruler. This makes many people afraid, and they no longer dare to speak freely.
6116.m: Secret police secretly watch the people.

6121.q: Which animal is the national symbol and heraldic animal of the USA?
6121.e: The bald eagle was declared the national symbol of the USA in 1782 and appears on the country's Great Seal. It stands for strength and freedom.
6121.m: The USA has the bald eagle as its symbol.

6133.q: How does a male leopard usually differ from a female?
a: It has stripes instead of spots
6133.e: Male leopards are usually much heavier than females. They can weigh about 60 to 90 kilograms.

a: A state insurance that pays a pension in old age and is partly funded by working people
A private savings insurance for children
A health insurance for young people
6138.e: AHV (old-age and survivors' insurance) is Switzerland's state pension insurance. All working people pay into it during their working life so that pensions can be paid out later.
6138.m: AHV provides a pension in old age.

6143.q: What is the Hindu place of worship called?
6143.e: In a Hindu temple there are statues of different gods. People pray there and bring flowers and offerings.

6160.q: Which part of the body helps you grab and hold things?
6160.e: With your fingers you can grab, hold and feel things. Your hand is very skilful.

a: A disease in which bones lose density
A vision problem in old age
6161.e: With osteoporosis the bones lose density and break more easily. Older people in particular are affected more often.
6161.m: Osteoporosis makes bones break more easily.

6163.q: How can you tell individual leopards apart in camera trap pictures?
a: By the spot pattern, which is different for each one
By the size of their ears
By the colour of their eyes
6163.e: Every leopard's spot pattern is unique, a bit like a fingerprint. Researchers use this to count the animals.

6176.q: What do bees collect from flowers?
6176.e: Bees fly from flower to flower and suck up the sweet nectar. In doing so they help the plants to reproduce.

a: The group that runs a country, a canton or a municipality
6183.e: A government makes important decisions and makes sure laws are carried out. In Switzerland there are governments at federal, cantonal and municipal level.
6183.m: The government runs the country, canton or municipality.

6189.q: Is the snow leopard a subspecies of the leopard?
a: No, it is a separate species
Yes, a subspecies from the Himalayas
Yes, a subspecies with light fur
No, it belongs to the lynxes
6189.e: The snow leopard is called Panthera uncia and is a separate species. It is related to the leopard, but it is not the same animal. It is not a lynx either.
6189.m: The snow leopard is a separate species.

6203.e: Leopards usually hunt at dusk and at night. During the day they often rest in the shade or in trees.

6217.q: Because of its coat, what else is the African wild dog called?
6217.e: The name hyena dog comes from its spotted appearance and its hunched walk, which is reminiscent of hyenas. But it is not related to hyenas.
6217.m: Hyena dog is another name for it.

6230.q: What is the force called that keeps an aeroplane in the air when it flies?
6230.e: The shape of the wings makes the air flow faster over the wings than underneath. This creates a difference in pressure that carries the aeroplane upwards.
6230.m: Lift keeps the aeroplane in the air.

6236.q: In which part of Africa does the African wild dog mainly live today?
a: In the middle of the Sahara
6236.e: The African wild dog lives mainly in the savannahs south of the Sahara, for example in Botswana, Tanzania and Zimbabwe. Today it is only found in small areas.
6236.m: The wild dog lives in Africa's savannahs south of the Sahara.

6267.q: What do you usually hear shortly after a flash of lightning?
6267.e: Lightning and thunder happen at the same time, but light is much faster than sound. That is why you see the lightning first and only hear the thunder afterwards.
6267.m: After the lightning comes the thunder.

6270.q: What is the main colour of the United Nations flag?
6270.e: The UN flag shows a map of the world on a light blue background. The colour stands for peace.
6270.m: The UN flag is light blue with a map of the world.

6273.q: What is the name of the well-known monastery in the canton of Solothurn that many pilgrims visit?
6273.e: Mariastein Abbey lies in the canton of Solothurn near the border with Basel and France. Many people make pilgrimages there because it has a famous chapel of grace.
6273.m: Mariastein Abbey is in the canton of Solothurn.

6281.q: Which material does light shine through well?
6281.e: Glass is transparent, so light gets through almost unhindered. Wood or stone blocks the light.
6281.m: Glass lets light through, stone does not.

6327.q: What does the Antarctic Treaty lay down?
a: That Antarctica may only be used for peaceful and scientific purposes
That only Switzerland may do research in Antarctica
That Antarctica will be sold to a single country
That wars may be fought in Antarctica
6327.e: Several states agreed to keep Antarctica free of military activity and to use it only for research. The treaty shows how countries can make rules for an area together.
6327.m: Antarctica is for peace and research.

6338.q: Why do you slip more easily on a smooth wooden floor in socks than in trainers?
a: The friction between socks and floor is smaller
6338.e: The rubber sole of trainers grips the floor well. Smooth fabric on smooth wood creates only a little friction, so you slip easily.

6348.q: Which animals are the “Big Five” in Africa?
6348.e: The Big Five are the lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo. They used to be seen as especially hard to hunt; today they are mostly photographed.
6348.m: The leopard is one of the Big Five.

a: Living far from home because you are not safe there.
A big party in the palace.
A kind of prison just for children.
6350.e: People who are persecuted in their country sometimes flee abroad into exile. There they are safer from the dictatorship.
6350.m: In exile you live far from home.

6359.q: Why do banks sometimes charge fees for an account?
a: Because the bank has costs for running the account and its services
Because otherwise accounts would give out unlimited money for free
Because fees automatically go into the savings account
6359.e: Banks offer services such as cards, online banking or advice, and these cost money. Part of this is covered by account fees.
6359.m: Bank fees cover the cost of services.

6363.q: Which insect, whose larva lives in streams, is a favourite food of trout?
6363.e: Larvae of mayflies, stoneflies and caddisflies live in streams. They are important food for trout.

6382.q: In fly fishing for trout, an artificial fly is often used. What is it made of?
a: Feathers and thread, copying an insect
Shiny metal, shaped like a spoon
6382.e: Fly fishers tie small copies of insects out of feathers, hair and thread. They use them to fool hungry trout.

6388.q: What job does the lymphatic system have in the body?
a: It carries tissue fluid and supports the immune defences
It pumps blood around the body
6388.e: The lymphatic system collects extra fluid from the tissues and filters it in the lymph nodes. Germs are caught along the way.
6388.m: The lymphatic system supports your defences.

6411.q: Why is direct democracy an important difference between Switzerland and the EU?
a: In Switzerland citizens can vote directly on laws
In the EU all citizens vote directly on every law
6411.e: In Switzerland the people and the cantons can have a direct say through initiatives and referendums. The EU does not have this kind of direct participation in this form.
6411.m: Switzerland has direct popular votes, the EU does not.

6448.q: What is a delegation at the UN?
a: A group of people who represent a country at meetings
A sum of money for poor countries
A flag flying in front of the UN
6448.e: Every country sends a delegation to UN meetings so that it can give its opinion. The delegation is usually made up of diplomats.
6448.m: A delegation represents a country at meetings.

6464.q: Which feature of the brown trout can you see particularly well in the photo?
a: Red spots with a pale ring
A big black spot on the tail
6464.e: The brown trout has red and black spots on its skin. The red spots are often surrounded by a pale ring.
6464.m: Red spots with a pale ring

6477.q: What is one feature of the African wild dog's coat?
a: Each animal has a different pattern
It is the same plain colour on all of them
6477.e: The patches of black, yellow, brown and white are different on every animal. This makes it possible to recognise individual animals.
6477.m: No two wild dogs look the same.

6494.q: Which planet is called the “red planet” because of its colour?
6494.e: Mars looks reddish because there is a lot of rusty iron oxide on its surface. It is the fourth planet from the sun.
6494.m: Mars glows red because of iron dust.

6509.q: What was the South Vietnamese city of Saigon renamed after the communist victory in 1975?
6509.e: After the end of the Vietnam War, the victorious communists renamed Saigon after their late leader Ho Chi Minh. Today the city is Vietnam’s economic centre.
6509.m: Since 1975 Saigon has been called Ho Chi Minh City.

6522.q: A stone lies at the top of a cliff. What kind of energy does it mainly have there?
6522.e: The stone is not moving, but because of its height it has potential energy. If it falls, this turns into energy of movement, kinetic energy.
6522.m: Movement is kinetic, position is potential.

a: A body of ice and dust in space with a tail
6538.e: Comets are made of frozen water, dust and rock and travel round the sun on a long path. Near the sun their surface melts a little and a glowing tail forms.
6538.m: Comets are made of ice and dust and have a tail.

6539.q: What does it mean when a plant or animal species is on the Red List?
6539.e: The Red List names species whose numbers have fallen sharply or that are threatened with extinction. It helps to plan protection measures.
6539.m: The Red List shows threatened species.

6542.q: Which country was united under communist rule after a long war?
6542.e: In the Vietnam War, the communist North fought against the South. In 1975 the North won and the country was united.

6549.q: Where does the Amur leopard you see in the photo live?
a: In the east of Russia and the north-east of China
6549.e: The Amur leopard lives in forests in the Russian Far East and neighbouring China. It is one of the rarest big cats in the world.
6549.m: Amur leopards live in the Far East.

6569.q: What is the time before Christmas called, when one more candle is lit every Sunday?
6569.e: During Advent Christians look forward to Christmas. On the Advent wreath one more candle burns each Sunday.
6569.m: Advent is looking forward to Christmas.

6581.q: Why can you see through a window pane but not through a wall?
a: Glass lets light through, a wall does not
Glass is colder than a wall
Glass is always cleaner than a wall
A wall is always a darker colour
6581.e: Glass is transparent, which means light can shine through it almost unhindered. A stone wall is opaque and lets no light through.

a: Giving money freely to someone who needs it, without asking for anything in return
6643.e: When you donate, you give money to help others, for example a charity. You get nothing back for it.
6643.m: Donating helps others without anything in return.

6646.q: What is meant by the ‘Cold War’?
a: The decades-long political rivalry between the USA and the Soviet Union without a direct war between them
A real war with many battles in Europe
A period of extreme cold in Russia
A trade war between China and Japan
6646.e: In the Cold War, the capitalist West led by the USA faced the communist Eastern Bloc led by the Soviet Union. There was no direct armed war between the two.
6646.m: In the Cold War, two powers were rivals without fighting each other directly.

6684.q: How many colours does a rainbow usually have?
6684.e: When sunlight passes through raindrops, it is bent and split into its colours. This makes a rainbow with seven colours.

6696.q: What is a ballot box in a vote?
a: A container into which you put your ballot paper
A computer in the Federal Palace
6696.e: If you go to the polls, you put your ballot paper into a special container. That way your vote is counted.
6696.m: The ballot paper goes into the ballot box.

6697.q: Which small crustacean, living under stones in streams, is eaten by brown trout?
6697.e: The freshwater shrimp is only about 1 to 2 centimetres long. It lives in clean streams and is common prey.
6697.m: The freshwater shrimp is a popular food.

6698.q: Apart from a piggy bank, where else can you keep saved money safe?
a: In a savings account at the bank
Under your pillow at holiday camp
In your trouser pocket while playing
6698.e: Money in a savings account at the bank is safe and does not get lost so easily. Many children have their own savings account.

6709.q: The brook trout looks similar to the brown trout. Where does it originally come from?
6709.e: The brook trout came to Europe from North America. It is a char and does not belong to the trout genus.
6709.m: The brook trout comes from North America.

6711.q: What do antibodies do in the immune system?
a: They recognise and fight foreign invaders
6711.e: Antibodies recognise germs such as viruses or bacteria. They help the body to make them harmless.

6738.q: Which insect with colourful wings collects nectar from flowers?
6738.e: Butterflies use their long proboscis to suck sweet nectar from flowers. In doing so they also help the plants with pollination.

6749.q: Which animal has black and white stripes and lives in Africa?
6749.e: Every zebra has a unique stripe pattern, almost like a fingerprint. Zebras live in herds on the savannah.
6749.m: Zebras have black and white stripes.

6761.q: Why is it wise not to spend all your pocket money straight away?
a: So you can afford something bigger later
So that your parents take the money back
6761.e: If you do not spend everything at once, over time you can afford more expensive things too. Saving takes patience.
6761.m: Saving makes bigger wishes come true.

6781.q: What were the “Great Purges” under Stalin?
a: A wave of persecution against real and suspected opponents of Stalin.
6781.e: In the 1930s Stalin had hundreds of thousands of people arrested, deported or shot. Many were innocent but were labelled as supposed enemies.
6781.m: The purges killed many innocent people.

6789.q: What makes the brown trout different from the Atlantic salmon?
a: It usually stays in fresh water and in the stream
It always lives in the sea
6789.e: The salmon migrates to the sea to feed and returns to spawn. The brown trout usually spends its life in the stream.
6789.m: The brown trout usually stays in the stream.

a: A rapidly spinning column of air
A kind of cloud without wind
6816.e: A tornado is a funnel-shaped whirlwind that can form during thunderstorms. It can produce very strong winds and cause great damage.
6816.m: A tornado is a powerful whirlwind.

6831.q: What is the name of the big church that is the landmark of the town of Solothurn?
6831.e: St Ursus Cathedral stands in the middle of Solothurn's old town and can be seen from far away. It is the town's main church and was built several hundred years ago.
6831.m: St Ursus Cathedral is the landmark of Solothurn.

a: An amount you want to save to buy something particular
6863.e: A savings goal is what you are putting money aside for, for example a new bike. It helps you stay motivated to save.
6863.m: A savings goal keeps you motivated to save.

6877.q: What is the difference between heat conduction and heat radiation?
a: Conduction needs contact, radiation also works through a vacuum
6877.e: In heat conduction, energy is passed on through direct contact, for example from a hot pan to its handle. Heat radiation travels as a wave, which is how the sun's heat reaches us through empty space.

6878.q: The picture shows a rainbow trout with a pink band. Where does it originally come from?
6878.e: The rainbow trout was brought to Europe from North America. The brown trout, on the other hand, is native to Europe.
6878.m: The rainbow trout comes from North America.

6882.q: Since which event has Switzerland officially been permanently neutral?
a: Since the Congress of Vienna in 1815
Since the founding of the EU
6882.e: At the Congress of Vienna in 1815, the great powers of Europe recognised Switzerland’s permanent neutrality. Since then Switzerland has tried to stay out of military conflicts.
6882.m: Switzerland has been permanently neutral since 1815.

6889.q: Which little town in the canton of Solothurn lies at the foot of the Jura?
6889.e: Balsthal lies in the Thal, a beautiful valley in the canton of Solothurn at the foot of the Jura mountains. Burgdorf and Langenthal belong to Bern, Zofingen to Aargau.
6889.m: Balsthal lies in the Thal at the foot of the Jura.

a: So that your eyes stay moist and clean
So that your nose stays clear
6893.e: When you blink, tear fluid spreads over the eye. That keeps it clean and stops it drying out.

6917.q: What is the main aim of the Paris climate agreement?
a: To limit global warming to well below 2 degrees
To ban all fossil fuels immediately
To commit only Switzerland to climate protection
To lower the sea level artificially
6917.e: In the 2015 Paris climate agreement almost all countries in the world committed to limiting global warming, if possible, to 1.5 degrees. To do this, greenhouse gas emissions are to be reduced worldwide.
6917.m: The Paris agreement aims to keep warming well below 2 degrees.

6925.q: What job does the spleen have in the body?
a: It filters out old blood cells and helps with defence
It cleans urea out of the blood
6925.e: The spleen sorts old or damaged blood cells out of the blood. It also plays a part in the immune defences. Urea is filtered by the kidneys, and bile is made by the liver.

6933.q: Which river flows right through the town of Solothurn?
6933.e: The Aare flows through the old town of Solothurn and is important for the town. Many bridges cross the river.
6933.m: The Aare flows right through Solothurn.

6941.q: What do you call energy produced by flowing water?
6941.e: Flowing water can drive a water wheel or a turbine. This turns the movement of the water into electricity.

a: A band of strong wind high in the atmosphere
An ocean current in the deep sea
A type of radiation from the sun
6946.e: The jet stream is a narrow band of very fast winds about 10 kilometres up. It has a big influence on how weather systems move over Europe.
6946.m: The jet stream is a band of strong wind high up.

6983.q: What is the force called with which a body presses straight down on a surface?
6983.e: Weight is caused by gravity acting on the mass of a body. It presses the body onto the surface it is standing or lying on.

6989.q: What colours is the flag of the canton of Solothurn?
6989.e: The flag of Solothurn is red at the top and white at the bottom. You can see it on many buildings in the canton.
6989.m: Solothurn's flag is red and white.

7013.e: International means that something involves several countries, for example a partnership or a meeting. The opposite would be national, meaning involving only one country.
7013.m: International means that something involves several countries.

7061.q: What is carbon dioxide (CO2) largely responsible for?
7061.e: CO2 is a greenhouse gas that holds heat in the atmosphere. Burning coal, oil and gas increases the amount of CO2 and so strengthens global warming.

7064.q: What is the best way for countries to solve a big problem like climate change?
7064.e: Many problems, such as climate change, affect the whole world. That is why countries work together in organisations like the UN to find shared solutions.
7064.m: Big problems are solved together with other countries.

7072.q: Why do you feel a headwind when cycling fast, even when there is no wind?
a: You are moving through the air, and you feel this as resistance
Your bike makes its own wind
7072.e: When you move, you have to push the air in front of you out of the way. You feel this air resistance as wind in your face.

7077.q: What job does the spinal cord have in the nervous system?
a: It carries signals between the brain and body and controls reflexes
7077.e: The spinal cord connects the brain and body and carries nerve signals in both directions. It also controls simple reflexes directly.
7077.m: The spinal cord connects the brain and body.

7080.q: What are the small, hard grains of ice called that can fall from the sky in a thunderstorm?
7080.e: Hail forms in thunderclouds when water droplets freeze and are carried up and down again and again. The ice grains get bigger as this happens.
7080.m: Hailstones are hard grains of ice from thunderclouds.

a: More than half have decided the same way
7099.e: In a majority, more than half of the people vote for the same thing. This is how votes decide what applies.

7105.q: What is a leopard especially good at?
7105.e: With strong legs and claws, the leopard climbs trees skilfully. It can even climb up with prey in its mouth.

7118.q: Which two parts make up the central nervous system?
7118.e: The central nervous system processes and passes on all the signals in the body. It consists of the brain and spinal cord.
7118.m: The brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system.

7122.q: What is the name of the well-known viewpoint mountain above the town of Solothurn?
7122.e: From the Weissenstein, in good weather, you can see many Alpine peaks and the town of Solothurn looking tiny from above. You can ride up by cable car.
7122.m: The Weissenstein is Solothurn's local mountain.

7138.q: What happens to a ball that you throw up?
7138.e: Gravity keeps pulling the ball back towards the ground. That is why it comes down again after a short time.
7138.m: What goes up comes back down.

a: It protects the skin from sunburn
It makes you tanned without sun
It cools the body from the inside
7142.e: Sun cream protects the skin from dangerous UV rays. That way you avoid painful sunburn.

7164.q: What was the Enabling Act of 1933?
a: A law that gave Hitler almost unlimited power.
7164.e: With the Enabling Act the government under Hitler could pass laws without asking parliament. It was an important step towards dictatorship.
7164.m: The law gave Hitler almost all power.

7170.q: In which city is the Federal Palace, where the National Council and the Council of States work?
7170.e: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland. The Federal Palace with the parliament is there.
7170.m: Bern is the federal city of Switzerland.

7184.q: Why does your body need iron?
a: To make haemoglobin in the blood
7184.e: Iron is needed for the haemoglobin in red blood cells, which carries oxygen. People who lack iron often feel tired.

7188.q: Which big cat lives in America and has rosettes with dots in the middle?
7188.e: The jaguar looks like the leopard but lives in America. Its rosettes usually have one or more dots inside.
7188.m: The jaguar lives in America, the leopard does not.

a: A request or demand handed in with signatures
A law that applies at once
A tax you have to pay
7202.e: With a petition, children and teenagers can also show their opinion. They collect signatures and hand them in to an authority.
7202.m: A petition is a request with signatures.

7211.q: What do you need at least for a simple circuit to work?
a: Battery, wires and something that uses electricity, such as a bulb
7211.e: For electricity to flow, there must be a closed connection: an energy source, wires and something that uses the electricity. If one part is missing, the circuit does not work.

7244.q: What do many houseplants on a windowsill do?
a: They grow away from the light
7244.e: Plants turn their leaves towards the light because they need it to grow. This behaviour is called phototropism.

a: When water freezes on the ground
When the sun shines especially strongly
7280.e: Frost forms when the temperature falls below zero degrees and moisture on the ground or on plants turns to ice. You can often recognise it by white, glittering patches in the morning.
7280.m: Frost is frozen water on the ground.

7291.q: Apart from protecting against germs, what other important job does the skin have?
a: It controls body temperature by sweating
7291.e: With sweat, the skin can cool the body. In this way it helps to keep body temperature steady.

7295.q: When does the world celebrate the International Day of Peace?
7295.e: Every year on 21 September the United Nations calls on people to think about peace. On this day, weapons should be used as little as possible.
7295.m: 21 September is the International Day of Peace.

7298.q: Why is it risky to give someone the PIN of your bank card?
a: Others could use it to take money from your account or pay without you noticing
The PIN then automatically stops working
The bank then blocks the account immediately
It is not risky at all
7298.e: The PIN protects your account from access by others. Anyone who knows it can take out money or pay with it, so it should always stay secret.

7323.q: How does the wild dog look different from a pet dog?
a: Its coat is patchy and its ears are big
Its coat is made of feathers
7323.e: The wild dog has a colourful patchy pattern and big, round ears. It also has no dewclaw at the front.
7323.m: Patches and big ears stand out.

7339.q: What is the small intestine's main job?
7339.e: In the small intestine, nutrients from the food mush are taken into the blood. Its inner wall is heavily folded to give lots of surface area.
7339.m: The small intestine takes in nutrients.

7384.q: What was the military alliance of the communist states in the Cold War called?
7384.e: The Warsaw Pact was the counterpart to NATO. Its members were the Soviet Union and its allies.
7384.m: The Warsaw Pact was the alliance of the East.

7386.q: On which paper do you write Yes or No in a vote?
7386.e: You write Yes or No on the ballot paper. Then you put it in the voting envelope and hand it in.
7386.m: I write Yes or No on the ballot paper.

7402.q: Roughly how heavy can an adult male leopard get?
7402.e: Males usually weigh between 60 and 90 kilograms. That is about as much as an adult human.
7402.m: Male leopards weigh up to about 90 kilos.

a: A mountain from which hot rock can come out
A mountain made of pure ice
7436.e: Deep inside a volcano it is extremely hot. Sometimes melted rock, called lava, rises up to the surface.
7436.m: Lava can come out of a volcano.

7438.q: What is the capital of the canton of Solothurn?
7438.e: Solothurn is not only the name of the canton but also the name of its capital. The cantonal government meets there, for example.
7438.m: The capital has the same name as the canton.

a: A person who makes wrongdoing or abuse of power public.
7457.e: Whistleblowers publish secret information about wrongdoing, often at great personal risk. They play an important role in uncovering abuse of power.

7458.q: What is it called when all citizens may vote directly on a question?
7458.e: In a popular vote, all voters may say Yes or No to a question directly. This is typical of Switzerland.
7458.m: In a popular vote everyone says Yes or No.

7492.q: In which year was the UN founded?
7492.e: The UN was founded after the Second World War so that countries could work together for peace. Since then many states have cooperated in the organisation.

7512.q: How does an adult brown trout usually behave towards other trout?
a: It lives in a huge shoal
It swims to the sea every day
7512.e: Brown trout are often loners and stay in one good spot. Intruders are driven away.

7523.q: Why is there a closed season for brown trout?
a: So that they can spawn undisturbed
Because the water is too cold for fishing then
7523.e: During the closed season they must not be caught. This keeps the next generation safe.

7533.q: What is the small round head covering that some Jewish men and boys wear called?
7533.e: The kippah is worn out of respect for God, especially when praying or in the synagogue. It covers only a small part of the head.
7533.m: The kippah is a Jewish head covering.

7535.q: What does World Population Day raise awareness of?
a: Issues around population growth and its consequences
7535.e: On World Population Day, 11 July, attention is drawn to issues such as population growth, health and education. It was started by the UN.
7535.m: World Population Day is about population growth.

7540.q: What job do the adrenal glands have?
a: They produce hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol
They filter the blood like the kidneys
7540.e: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys and produce important hormones for stress reactions and metabolism. Adrenaline and cortisol are among them.
7540.m: The adrenal glands make stress hormones.

a: A day that reminds people of children’s rights
A day without school for everyone
7546.e: World Children’s Day reminds us that all children in the world have rights, for example the right to school and protection. The UN supports this day.
7546.m: World Children’s Day reminds us of children’s rights.

7548.q: What did the UN adopt in 1948?
a: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
7548.e: In the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, the UN set out which rights every person in the world should have. It is seen as an important basis for many later laws.
7548.m: In 1948 the UN declared human rights.

7564.q: What are the young of the African wild dog called?
7564.e: As with other dogs, the young are called pups. They are born in a den.
7564.m: Young wild dogs are called pups.

7566.q: What does “cash discount” mean on a bill?
a: A price reduction if you pay the bill very quickly
An extra charge for paying late
7566.e: A cash discount (in German “Skonto”) is a small price reduction you get if you pay a bill within a short time. It rewards paying quickly.
7566.m: A cash discount rewards paying quickly.

7569.q: What happens during a solar eclipse?
a: The moon moves in front of the sun
7569.e: When the moon is exactly between the Earth and the sun, it casts its shadow on the Earth. Then it goes dark for a short time.
7569.m: The moon moves in front of the sun.

7573.q: Two children are sitting on a seesaw. What happens if one is much heavier than the other?
7573.e: The heavier a child is, the more strongly they push their side of the seesaw down. This is a simple lever effect.
7573.m: The heavier side pushes the seesaw down.

7575.q: Which animals is the leopard most closely related to?
7575.e: Leopards, lions, tigers and jaguars belong to the same genus of big cats. A typical feature is that they can roar.
7575.m: Leopards, lions, tigers and jaguars are closely related big cats.

7579.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Bern?
7579.e: The bear is the heraldic animal of Bern and even gave the city its name. The story goes that the founder chose the first animal he killed for it.
7579.m: Bern has a bear on its coat of arms.

7582.q: What does a leopard's typical call often sound like?
7582.e: The leopard's call is often compared to the sound of a saw. It uses it to get attention.
7582.m: The leopard's call sounds like sawing.

7593.q: Experts divide streams and rivers into sections according to typical fish. What is the upper, cool and fast-flowing section called?
7593.e: In the cool, oxygen-rich upper course, trout are the main fish. That is why this section is called the trout zone.
7593.m: The trout zone is in the upper course.

7607.q: Why do you sneeze when dust gets into your nose?
a: Your body wants to blow the dust out quickly
Your nose wants to annoy you
7607.e: Sneezing is a reflex that removes foreign objects from the nose. That way the nose is clear again.

a: A fixed monthly amount with which young people plan many of their own costs, such as clothes or leisure
A wage that young people get from the state
A wage that only apprentices receive
Money you only get on public holidays
7627.e: In the youth wage model, young people regularly get a fixed amount and budget it themselves for certain areas such as clothing or leisure. This helps them learn early how to handle money.
7627.m: A youth wage is practice in budgeting on your own.

7628.q: What decides how many National Council seats a canton gets?
a: The number of people living in the canton
The year the canton was founded
Always the same number per canton
7628.e: The seats in the National Council are shared out among the cantons in proportion to the resident population. That is why large cantons such as Zurich have many more seats than small ones.
7628.m: A canton with more inhabitants gets more National Council seats.

7670.q: What do you call stars that can be joined up into pictures in the night sky?
7670.e: Long ago people joined bright stars into figures, for example the Plough. These patterns are called constellations.
7670.m: Constellations are patterns of bright stars.

7683.q: Who led the brutal rule of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia?
7683.e: Pol Pot ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979. Under his rule, millions of people died from forced labour, hunger and violence.
7683.m: Pol Pot led the Khmer Rouge.

7686.q: What is the name of one of the old town gates in the old town of Solothurn?
7686.e: The Basel Gate is one of the old gates through which people once had to pass to enter the town of Solothurn. Solothurn once had a complete town wall with several towers and gates.
7686.m: The Basel Gate leads into Solothurn's old town.

7714.q: What is the principle called by which the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities share out tasks between them?
7714.e: In Switzerland there are three levels: the Confederation, the cantons and the municipalities. Each level takes on certain tasks; this is called federalism.
7714.m: Federalism shares out tasks across three levels.

7735.q: Which country has a flag that, apart from its proportions, looks almost exactly like the flag of Monaco?
7735.e: The flags of Indonesia and Monaco both consist of a red and a white stripe, but they differ in their proportions. Indonesia has used its flag since independence in 1945.
7735.m: Indonesia and Monaco have almost identical flags.

7743.q: How many kidneys does a healthy person usually have?
7743.e: The two kidneys lie to the left and right of the spine. Together they filter the blood and make urine.

7786.q: Why does a suction cup stick to a smooth tile?
a: Air pressure presses it on from the outside
The suction cup is a magnet
The suction cup gets warm and melts
7786.e: The air is pushed out from under the suction cup, so there is low pressure there. The air pressure from outside then presses it firmly against the wall.
7786.m: Air pressure holds the suction cup in place.

7790.q: In which Swiss city is the International Olympic Committee based?
7790.e: The International Olympic Committee organises the Olympic Games and is based in Lausanne. That is why Lausanne is also called the “Olympic Capital”.

7795.q: What do you call the journey water makes from the sea, through the clouds and back down to Earth?
7795.e: Water evaporates from lakes and seas, forms clouds and falls down again as rain. This journey repeats again and again.
7795.m: Water travels round and round in a cycle.

7796.q: Why is a full shopping trolley harder to push than an empty one?
7796.e: There are lots of things in the full trolley, so it weighs more. The heavier something is, the more force you need to push it.

7807.q: What does panachage mean in an election?
a: Writing names from different lists on the same ballot paper
Handing in a blank ballot paper
7807.e: With panachage, you mix candidates from different parties on one ballot paper. This is possible in proportional elections such as the National Council election.
7807.m: Panachage mixes names from different lists.

7815.q: Why is a hot summer dangerous for brown trout?
a: The prey animals get too big
7815.e: The warmer the water, the less oxygen it can hold. For cold-water fish it then becomes life-threatening.

7863.q: In the dish “trout au bleu”, the trout's skin turns bluish. Where does this colour come from?
a: The layer of slime reacts with vinegar
The trout is dyed with food colouring
7863.e: The trout is cooked fresh, with its layer of slime, in a vinegar stock. This turns the skin bluish.
7863.m: Vinegar turns the slime layer blue.

7882.q: What is the aim of the Paris Climate Agreement?
7882.e: In the Paris Climate Agreement, almost every country in the world committed to fighting climate change together. Switzerland has also signed the agreement.
7882.m: The Paris Agreement limits global warming.

a: The explosion of a massive star at the end of its life
The birth of a new star from clouds of gas
An especially bright planet in the night sky
A new moon of the Earth
7892.e: When massive stars use up their nuclear fuel, they collapse and explode extremely brightly. For a short time a supernova can shine more brightly than a whole galaxy.
7892.m: A supernova is the explosion of a star at the end of its life.

7916.q: What is the difference between a watt and a watt-hour?
a: A watt is power, a watt-hour is an amount of energy used
A watt only measures heat, a watt-hour only light
A watt-hour measures time, a watt measures weight
7916.e: Watts show how much energy an appliance uses per second. If an appliance runs at this power for one hour, it has used one watt-hour of energy.
7916.m: A watt is power, a watt-hour is energy.

7955.q: What colour do Buddhist monks often wear in many countries?
7955.e: In many Buddhist countries monks wear orange or saffron-coloured robes. This colour has a long tradition.
7955.m: Buddhist monks often wear orange robes.

a: A very well-known award for special achievements
7956.e: The Nobel Prize is awarded every year to people who have achieved great things, for example for peace or science. Henry Dunant received the first Nobel Peace Prize.
7956.m: The Nobel Prize honours special achievements.

8015.q: What do you call an over-the-top reaction of the immune system to harmless substances such as pollen?
8015.e: With an allergy, the immune system overreacts to substances that are actually harmless. Typical examples are hay fever or nut allergies.
8015.m: With an allergy, the immune system overreacts.

8023.q: What is the basic difference between weather and climate?
a: Weather is short-term, climate is the long-term average
Weather only exists in summer, climate only in winter
Weather is only about rain, climate only about wind
8023.e: Weather describes the current state of the atmosphere at a place, for example today or tomorrow. Climate is the statistical average of weather data over many decades.
8023.m: Climate is the average of many years of weather.

8072.q: What colour is the cross on the Swiss flag?
8072.e: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background. It is one of the oldest flags in the world.
8072.m: The Swiss flag shows a white cross on a red background.

8082.q: What is the government of a canton usually called?
a: Government Council or Council of State
8082.e: Every canton has its own government. Depending on the canton, it is called the Government Council, the Council of State or something else.
8082.m: A cantonal government is often called the Government Council.

8089.q: In which unit is frequency measured, for example of sound waves or alternating current?
8089.e: Frequency tells you how often something repeats per second, for example how often a wave vibrates. The unit is named after the physicist Heinrich Hertz.

8098.q: What is the difference between a series circuit and a parallel circuit?
a: In a series circuit the current has only one path, in a parallel circuit several paths
Both are built in exactly the same way
There is no current in a series circuit
8098.e: In a series circuit all the components are connected one after another; if one fails, the whole circuit goes off. In a parallel circuit components have their own paths, so they work independently of each other.
8098.m: A series circuit has one path, a parallel circuit several.

8106.q: The sea trout is the same species as the brown trout. What does it do differently?
a: It migrates to the sea and returns to rivers to spawn
It only lives in mountain lakes
8106.e: The sea trout feeds in the sea and grows bigger there. To spawn, it swims into rivers and streams.
8106.m: Sea trout spawn in fresh water.

8112.q: Which animal sits on a cactus in the centre of the Mexican coat of arms?
8112.e: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle sitting on a cactus and eating a snake. It goes back to an Aztec founding legend.
8112.m: Mexico's coat of arms shows an eagle with a snake.

a: The period of time an elected parliament or government is in office
The length of a parliamentary sitting
8125.e: At federal level, a legislative period lasts four years. After that there are elections again.
8125.m: A legislative period is the parliament's term of office.

8138.q: What is the difference between the active and the passive right to vote?
a: Active means being allowed to vote, passive means being allowed to be elected
Active means only voting on issues, passive means only electing
8138.e: With the active right to vote, you may cast a vote yourself. With the passive right, you may stand for election yourself.

8146.q: Which statement about the Persian leopard is true?
a: It lives mainly in the Caucasus and Iran
It only lives in South America
It lives at the North Pole
8146.e: The Persian leopard is a subspecies found in Western Asia, for example in Iran and the Caucasus. It is one of the biggest subspecies.
8146.m: The Persian leopard lives in Western Asia.

a: A place where people who have fled live for a while
A holiday camp for school classes
8160.e: People who have fled from war or danger find a roof over their heads, food and help from a doctor in a refugee camp.
8160.m: Refugee camps offer protection from danger.

8184.q: What do two like magnetic poles do when you bring them together?
8184.e: Two north poles or two south poles push each other away. Only different poles attract each other.
8184.m: Like poles push each other away.

8202.q: What was the feared secret police of East Germany called?
8202.e: The Stasi secretly watched many people in East Germany. Its job was to stop criticism of the government.
8202.m: The Stasi spied on East German citizens.

8205.q: What does immunity mean for members of parliament?
a: During their term they are protected from certain prosecutions
They don't have to pay taxes
8205.e: Immunity protects members of parliament from being prosecuted for what they say in the chamber. This way they can speak their minds freely.
8205.m: Immunity protects members of parliament while in office.

8213.q: How did the canton of Jura come about?
a: Through a popular vote in which areas separated from the canton of Bern
Through a decision by the UN
Through a merger of two cantons
8213.e: In 1978 the Swiss people agreed to the creation of a new canton, after parts of the canton of Bern had decided to separate. The canton of Jura was officially founded in 1979.
8213.m: The canton of Jura was created by a vote in 1979.

8226.q: How do leopards usually move around?
a: On four paws, quietly and smoothly
8226.e: Leopards walk on soft paws into which they can pull their claws. This lets them move almost silently.

8249.q: What is meant by transpiration in plants?
a: Giving off water vapour through the leaves
Taking in carbon dioxide through the roots
8249.e: Plants constantly lose water through tiny openings in their leaves, the stomata. This process helps to carry water and nutrients from the roots up into the leaves.
8249.m: In transpiration plants lose water through their leaves.

8250.q: How does the African wild dog usually hunt?
a: As a team in a pack
Only at night in the water
8250.e: The animals hunt together and often chase their prey for a long time. Thanks to their teamwork they are very successful.
8250.m: Hunting together makes wild dogs successful.

8267.q: What are young leopards like straight after birth?
a: Almost as big as their mother
8267.e: Newborn leopards are blind and must be hidden and cared for by their mother. They only open their eyes after a few days.

8268.q: Which animal is shown on the coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden?
8268.e: Like Appenzell Innerrhoden, Appenzell Ausserrhoden also has an upright black bear on its coat of arms. The two cantons used to be a single canton of Appenzell.
8268.m: Ausserrhoden also has a bear on its coat of arms.

8273.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer?
8273.e: The stratosphere lies above the troposphere, where the weather happens. It contains the ozone layer, which filters UV radiation.
8273.m: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere.

8283.q: Why should you be careful when lending money to a friend?
a: You might not get it back
8283.e: If you lend money, you might not get it back, and that can lead to an argument. So you should think carefully.
8283.m: Money you lend does not always come back.

8289.q: Which large bird often stands motionless in the water and catches trout?
8289.e: The grey heron waits quietly in shallow water. Then it strikes like lightning with its long beak.
8289.m: The grey heron lies in wait in shallow water.

a: A border meant to stop East German citizens fleeing to the West.
A tourist attraction from the start.
A bridge between East and West.
8308.e: The Berlin Wall was built by East Germany in 1961 to stop people escaping to the West. Many people died trying to get across it.
8308.m: The Wall stopped people escaping to freedom.

8337.q: Why should you drink plenty of water?
a: Your body needs water to work properly
8337.e: Your body is made largely of water. It helps, for example, with carrying nutrients around.
8337.m: Water is important for your body.

8391.q: Which type of joint lets the arm move in almost every direction?
a: The ball-and-socket joint in the shoulder
The hinge joint in the knee
A fixed joint in the top of the skull
There is no movable joint in the arm
8391.e: The ball-and-socket joint of the shoulder allows a very wide range of movement. Other joints, such as the knee, only move in one direction.
8391.m: Ball-and-socket joints allow lots of movement.

8398.q: How do wild dogs mainly find their prey?
a: With heat sensors on their paws
8398.e: They use their senses, especially their good eyesight in open country. Then the pack chases the prey.
8398.m: Their senses help wild dogs hunt.

8414.q: What are the small drops of water lying on the grass on cool mornings called?
8414.e: On cool nights the air cools down and water vapour settles on plants as droplets. This is called dew.

8440.q: What can you use to find out whether an object conducts electricity?
a: A circuit with a small bulb
8440.e: If you put the object into a circuit with a small bulb and the bulb lights up, the object conducts electricity. If it does not light up, it is an insulator.
8440.m: A small bulb shows whether electricity is flowing.

8446.q: Which place in Switzerland is a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
8446.e: Bern’s Old Town with its arcades and fountains has been a World Heritage Site since 1983. UNESCO protects places that are important for all of humanity.
8446.m: Bern’s Old Town is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

8457.q: What is a device that stores electricity called?
8457.e: A battery stores energy that it can give off as electricity. That is why many toys work with batteries.
8457.m: A battery stores electricity for later.

8458.q: What helps brown trout when a stream is restored to its natural state?
8458.e: Gravel beds serve as spawning sites, and roots and stones as hiding places. A straightened concrete stream, on the other hand, offers hardly any habitat.

8463.q: What does the Schengen Agreement, which Switzerland also takes part in, lay down?
a: Removing passport checks at shared borders
8463.e: Thanks to Schengen, travellers can move between many European countries without passport checks at the border. Switzerland has taken part since 2008, even though it is not an EU member.
8463.m: Schengen allows travel without border checks.

8469.q: Why do dictators usually dislike free newspapers?
a: Because they don’t want criticism of the government.
8469.e: Free newspapers could report on mistakes and wrongdoing. Dictators want to prevent that, so they control the media.

8473.q: What is the covering that protects the brain and spinal cord and is filled with fluid called?
8473.e: The meninges surround the brain and spinal cord and contain a protective fluid. They cushion knocks in addition to the skull.
8473.m: The meninges cushion the brain and spinal cord.

8478.q: What is a committee in parliament?
a: A smaller group of members of parliament who prepare issues
8478.e: Committees prepare business for the National Council and the Council of States. They discuss proposals in detail before the whole chamber decides on them.

8510.q: Why is pack size important for the wild dog?
a: Large packs hunt and protect better
8510.e: In a bigger pack, more animals can hunt and guard the pups. Defending against enemies also works better.

a: Great Britain leaving the European Union
A climate agreement between Europe and Asia
The founding of the United Nations
8544.e: After a referendum, Great Britain left the European Union. The word is made up of “Britain” and “exit”.
8544.m: Brexit means that Great Britain has left the EU.

8549.q: What do you use to taste whether something is sweet or salty?
8549.e: There are tiny taste buds on your tongue. They detect sweet, salty, sour, bitter and savoury.

8554.q: What is the part of a plant called that takes in water from the soil?
8554.e: The root sits in the soil and soaks up water and nutrients there. It also holds the plant firmly in the ground.
8554.m: The root drinks water from the soil.

8593.q: What are the tiny openings on the underside of leaves, the stomata, used for?
a: For exchanging gases such as CO2 and oxygen
8593.e: Through the stomata the plant takes in carbon dioxide and gives off oxygen and water vapour. They open and close as needed.
8593.m: Stomata control the plant’s gas exchange.

8594.q: What is the parliament of a canton often called?
8594.e: Every canton has its own parliament, which depending on the canton is called the Cantonal Council, the Grand Council or something else. Cantonal laws are passed there.

a: A spontaneous purchase made without thinking first
A planned purchase with a budget
A purchase that is always cheaper
A purchase you sell again later
8603.e: With an impulse buy you decide on the spot, often on a whim, without thinking about whether you really need the product. This can quickly upset your budget.
8603.m: An impulse buy is bought without thinking.

8632.q: Where is the brown trout originally native?
8632.e: The brown trout originally comes from Europe. Later, people took it to many other countries.

8653.q: The photo shows a snow leopard. Where does it live?
a: In the high mountains of Central Asia
8653.e: The snow leopard lives in high mountains such as the Himalayas. It is a separate species, not a subspecies of the leopard.
8653.m: Snow leopards live in the mountains of Central Asia.

8667.q: In which Swiss city is the Universal Postal Union based?
8667.e: The Universal Postal Union makes sure that letters and parcels can be sent from one country to another. It is based in Bern, Switzerland’s capital.
8667.m: The Universal Postal Union is based in Bern.

8674.q: Which of these animals is prey for a leopard?
8674.e: The impala is a medium-sized antelope and fits the leopard's choice of prey well. Adult elephants and rhinos are far too big.

8683.q: What is it called when trout swim to their spawning grounds?
8683.e: At spawning time, trout often move upstream to gravelly spots. There must be no obstacles in the way.
8683.m: The spawning migration leads to the spawning ground.

8689.q: What is a female leopard called?
8689.e: The female is called a leopardess. The male is simply called a leopard.
